issues.summary: Add Support for Paypal and Apple Pay as Default Payment Methods
issues.description:
Summary

Currently, only credit cards can be set as default payment methods. This ticket adds support for PayPal Direct and Apple Pay to be set as default payment methods in customer wallets.

Background

The system currently restricts default payment methods to credit cards only (Payment Type ID = 2). This restriction is enforced in multiple layers:

- Wallet Service validation throws exception: "Only credit card wallet options can be set as the default"

- Legacy WalletService explicitly rejects PayPal and Apple Pay in switch statement

- Database layer only has SetDefaultCreditCardInWallet stored procedure

Both PayPal Direct (type 16) and Apple Pay (type 17) are already fully implemented payment types in the system with complete payment processing support.

Business Value

- Allows customers to use their preferred payment method as default

- Improves user experience for customers who prefer digital wallets

- Aligns with industry standards where any valid payment method can be default

---
Default Payment Method Support

What needs to work:

- Users can set PayPal Direct (Payment Type 16) as their default payment method

- Users can set Apple Pay (Payment Type 17) as their default payment method

- Only one payment method can be default at a time per wallet

- When a user sets a new default, the old one automatically gets unset

- All current validations should remain such as the inability to set an inactive or expired payment method as a default

- If this will require a contract change to the existing Get Wallet endpoint, please create a brand new wallet endpoint or find a way to make it backwards compatible

- It is not expected UI teams will be able to support this in parallel

Checkout Integration

Scheduled Payments

Recurring charges need to work:

- Scheduled payments should support PayPal and Apple Pay as defaults

- Subscription renewals should support PayPal and Apple Pay as defaults

Payment Operations

These operations need to handle PayPal/Apple Pay defaults:

- Refunds - should process correctly when refunding to a PayPal or Apple Pay default

- No-show charges - should work when charging a PayPal or Apple Pay default

- Manual charges - should work when charging a PayPal or Apple Pay default

---
Implementation Areas

1. Wallet Service - Core Default Payment Logic

What needs to change:

- Remove the restriction that only allows credit cards to be set as default

- Update validation logic to accept PayPal Direct and Apple Pay as valid default payment types

- Ensure database operations (stored procedures) can handle setting any payment type as default, not just credit cards

---
2. Customer Service Integration

What needs to verify:

- Ensure the service layer properly passes through PayPal and Apple Pay when setting defaults

- No additional restrictions or assumptions at this layer

---
3. TeeTimesAPI / API 2.1 Layer

What needs to change/verify:

- Customer wallet management endpoints (methods with names like "SetCreditCardAsPrimary" may need updating)

- Reservation creation logic when no payment method is specified (should fall back to default)

- Order creation logic when no payment method is specified (should fall back to default)

- Payment validation in reservation workflows

---
4. Reservation Service Workflows

What needs to verify:

- Payment validation activities accept PayPal and Apple Pay as defaults

- Charge building activities handle all payment types equally

- Payment capture activities work with PayPal and Apple Pay defaults

- Default payment retrieval logic doesn't assume credit cards

---
5. Scheduled Payments & Recurring Charges

What needs to verify:

- Scheduled payment execution can charge PayPal and Apple Pay defaults

- Subscription renewal workflows support PayPal and Apple Pay

- Payment method update workflows handle all payment types

- Background job processors don't assume credit cards

---
6. Refund Processing

What needs to verify:

- Refund workflows can process refunds to PayPal and Apple Pay

- Refund amount calculations work for all payment types

- Scheduled payment refunds handle all payment types

---
7. No-Show & Manual Charge Workflows

What needs to verify:

- No-show charge workflows can charge PayPal and Apple Pay defaults

- Manual charge workflows accept PayPal and Apple Pay

- Validation logic doesn't restrict to credit cards only

---
8. Database Layer

What needs to change:

- Create or update stored procedures to set defaults for any payment type (not just credit cards)

- Ensure the IsDefault flag works consistently across all payment types

- Database operations should be payment-type agnostic

---
9. Cross-Cutting Concerns to Review

Default Payment Retrieval:

- Anywhere the system fetches "the default payment method" to use automatically

- Ensure no code assumes the default will always be a credit card type

Payment Type Validation:

- Look for validation logic that checks payment types

- Ensure none inadvertently block PayPal or Apple Pay from being defaults

Method Naming:

- Methods with names like "SetCreditCardAsPrimary" should either be renamed or verified to handle all payment types

Error Handling:

- Ensure error messages make sense for all payment types

- No error messages that say "credit card" when they mean "payment method"

---
Testing Notes

Unit Tests Required

Test Suite 1: Wallet Service Validation

Location: Internal Services/GolfNow.Services.Wallet/GolfNow.Services.Wallet.UnitTests/

Tests to Add:

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_PayPalDirect_Success
- Arrange: Customer with active PayPal payment option
- Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with PayPal wallet option ID
- Assert: Returns true, no exception thrown

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_ApplePay_Success
- Arrange: Customer with active Apple Pay payment option
- Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with Apple Pay wallet option ID
- Assert: Returns true, no exception thrown

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_ExpiredPayPal_Fails
- Arrange: Customer with expired PayPal payment option
- Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption with expired PayPal ID
- Assert: Throws WalletInvalidDataException with appropriate message

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_GuestWallet_PayPal_Fails
- Arrange: Guest wallet with PayPal payment option
- Act: Call SetDefaultWalletOption
- Assert: Throws exception about guest wallets

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_SwitchFromCreditCardToPayPal
- Arrange: Customer with credit card as default
- Act: Set PayPal as default
- Assert: Credit card IsDefault = false, PayPal IsDefault = true

Test_SetDefaultWalletOption_SwitchFromPayPalToApplePay
- Arrange: Customer with PayPal as default
- Act: Set Apple Pay as default
- Assert: PayPal IsDefault = false, Apple Pay IsDefault = true

Test Suite 2: Customer Service Integration

Location: Internal Services/GolfNow.Services.Customer/GolfNow.Services.Customer.UnitTests/

Tests to Add:

Test_SetDefaultPaymentOption_PayPal_IntegrationSuccess
Test_SetDefaultPaymentOption_ApplePay_IntegrationSuccess
Test_GetCustomerWallet_DefaultPayPalMarkedCorrectly
Test_GetCustomerWallet_DefaultApplePayMarkedCorrectly

Integration Tests Required

Test Scenario 1: Full Reservation Flow with Default PayPal

Setup:

- Create test customer with PayPal payment method

- Set PayPal as default via API

- Create reservation without specifying payment method

Expected Results:

- Reservation created successfully

- Payment charged to PayPal account

- Reservation payment_method_type = 16 (PayPal Direct)

- Charge record shows PayPal wallet option ID

Test Scenario 2: Full Reservation Flow with Default Apple Pay

Setup:

- Create test customer with Apple Pay payment method

- Set Apple Pay as default via API

- Create reservation without specifying payment method

Expected Results:

- Reservation created successfully

- Payment charged to Apple Pay account

- Reservation payment_method_type = 17 (Apple Pay)

- Charge record shows Apple Pay wallet option ID

Test Scenario 3: Scheduled Payment Execution

Setup:

- Create customer with scheduled payment

- Customer has PayPal as default payment method

- Trigger scheduled payment execution

Expected Results:

- Scheduled payment charges PayPal account

- Transaction records show PayPal as payment method

- No errors logged

Test Scenario 4: Refund to PayPal Default

Setup:

- Complete reservation with default PayPal

- Process full refund

Expected Results:

- Refund processes successfully

- Refund goes to original PayPal account

- Refund status updated correctly

Test Scenario 5: No-Show Charge

Setup:

- Create reservation with default Apple Pay

- Mark reservation as no-show

- Process no-show charge

Expected Results:

- No-show charge processes to Apple Pay account

- Charge successful

- Reservation status updated

Test Scenario 6: Multi-Currency Support

Setup:

- Set PayPal as default for customer in USD market

- Set PayPal as default for customer in CAD market

- Make reservations in both currencies

Expected Results:

- Both process successfully with correct currency

Manual QA Test Cases

QA-1: Basic Set Default Functionality

Steps:

- Login as customer with multiple payment methods (CC, PayPal, Apple Pay)

- Navigate to payment methods page

- Set PayPal as default

- Refresh page

- Verify PayPal shows as default

- Set Apple Pay as default

- Verify only Apple Pay shows as default

Expected: UI correctly shows default indicator, only one method is default at a time

QA-2: Reservation Without Specifying Payment

Steps:

- Set PayPal as default payment method

- Start new reservation booking

- Proceed to payment WITHOUT selecting a payment method

- Complete booking

Expected: Booking uses PayPal by default, confirmation shows PayPal

QA-3: Guest User Restriction

Steps:

- Login as guest user

- Add PayPal payment method

- Attempt to set as default

Expected: Error message displayed, action blocked

QA-4: Expired Payment Restriction

Steps:

- Have an expired PayPal payment method in wallet

- Attempt to set as default

Expected: Error message about expired payment method, action blocked

QA-5: API Testing (Postman/Swagger)

Steps:

- Call SetDefaultWalletOption API with PayPal wallet option ID

- Call GetCustomerWallet API

- Verify response shows PayPal with IsDefault = true

- Call SetDefaultWalletOption API with Apple Pay wallet option ID

- Call GetCustomerWallet API

- Verify response shows Apple Pay with IsDefault = true, PayPal with IsDefault = false

Expected: API responses consistent with expectations

QA-6: Scheduled Payment Renewal

Steps:

- Create subscription with scheduled renewal

- Set Apple Pay as default

- Wait for or trigger renewal

- Check transaction records

Expected: Renewal charges to Apple Pay successfully

QA-7: Switch Default Multiple Times

Steps:

- Set Credit Card as default

- Set PayPal as default

- Set Apple Pay as default

- Set Credit Card as default again

- After each change, verify via API and UI

Expected: Each switch works correctly, previous default is unset

Regression Testing

Areas to Regression Test:

- Credit card as default still works (existing functionality)

- Gift card wallet behavior unchanged

- Account balance wallet behavior unchanged

- Payment without default specified still prompts for payment selection

- All existing reservation flows with explicit payment method selection

Performance Testing

Tests to Run:

- Load test: 1000 concurrent SetDefaultWalletOption calls

- Response time should be < 500ms for 95th percentile

- Database connection pool handles load

- No deadlocks when updating default payment methods concurrently

comments.body:
Internal note: In this ticket we are only allowing to set Apple Pay payment method as default.

Details:

- We added a new property SetAsDefault on ApplePayPayment payment info.

- SetAsDefault will be false by default unless it is explicitly specified.

- If specified as true in checkout endpoint. Apple Pay WalletOption with PaymentTypeID equal 17 will be set as default.

- GetWallet endpoint in API 2.1 will now return a new collection called ApplePayPaymentOptionswith all Apple Pay WalletOptions.

Example of the body:

"PaymentInformation": [
{
"__type": "ApplePayPayment:#GolfNow.API.Contracts.DataContracts",
"PaymentDataToken":"",
"PaymentMethodNetwork": "MasterCard",
"SetAsDefault" : true
}

issues.summary: Fix 500 errors when CustomerNotes contains invalid characters for GolfNow API
issues.description:
Problem

External order creation can fail with an HTTP 500 response when CustomerNotes contains characters that are rejected by the downstream GolfNow API. One example is the value "N/A", which contains a forward slash (/) and results in a BadRequest response from the downstream service.

Because the downstream exception is not handled before the request is sent, the failure propagates and causes order creation to fail.

Solution

Implement sanitization of CustomerNotes before sending requests to the GolfNow API.

- Add SanitizeCustomerNotesForGolfNowApi() helper method.

- Sanitize unsupported characters that are rejected by the downstream API.

- Apply sanitization during external order request construction prior to serialization.

- Preserve customer notes whenever possible while preventing downstream validation failures.

- Prevent avoidable 500 responses caused by invalid note content.

Acceptance Criteria

- Orders containing CustomerNotes values such as "N/A" no longer fail due to downstream validation errors.

- Customer notes are sanitized before requests are sent to the GolfNow API.

- External order creation succeeds when notes contain previously problematic characters.

- Existing order creation behavior remains unchanged for valid note values.

issues.summary: Surface IsWaivable and IsRefundable through the FeeConfiguration data access layer
issues.description:
Summary

CORE-14444 added IsWaivable and IsRefundable columns to Revenue.FeeConfiguration at the database level, but intentionally deferred the application-layer integration. This ticket connects those columns through the data access layer so they are available to downstream business logic (waiver decisions, refund calculations) in future tickets.

This is a data plumbing ticket — it makes the values available in-memory but does NOT change any business behavior. No customer-facing impact until future tickets consume these properties behind LaunchDarkly.

---
What This Connects To

These columns enable the Customizable Transaction Fees epic (CORE-13901) to support fees with different behaviors:

- IsWaivable — Determines whether a GolfPass waived-fee-credit can be applied to this fee. Standard convenience fees are waivable; tourism/regulatory fees are not.

- IsRefundable — Determines whether this fee is included in refund calculations on cancellation. Standard fees are refundable; certain regulatory fees are not.

Downstream consumers (future tickets, not this one):

- GolfPass waiver logic in Reservation Service (LoyaltyHelper)

- Refund/cancellation workflow in Reservation Service (BuildRefundInvoiceActivity)

- Admin UI in RMS for setting these values per fee configuration

---
Areas Touched

- Stored Procedure — Revenue.GetFeeConfigurationByOwnerFacilityCourse needs to include IsWaivable and IsRefundable in its CTE and final SELECT output

- Framework DTO — GolfNow.Framework.Pricing.Fees.Data.DTO.FeeConfiguration needs corresponding boolean properties

- Sequencing — The GNDS stored procedure update should deploy before or simultaneously with the code change. DTO properties should default to true as a safety net during rolling deploys.

---
What This Does NOT Touch

- No behavior changes — this is purely making data available

- No admin UI changes (RMS models, GolfCourse Service models — separate future ticket)

- No waiver logic changes

- No refund logic changes

- No other stored procedures need updating for this ticket (other sprocs that read/write FeeConfiguration don't need these columns yet — INSERT operations are protected by DEFAULT constraints, UPDATE operations don't touch these columns)

---
Technical Reference

A detailed investigation document is attached covering:

Please be sure to do your own investigation of course

- Full stored procedure analysis (all 6 sprocs that touch the table)

- Complete data flow diagram (DB → DAL → Provider → Consumer)

- Caching assessment (confirmed: no caching on this path)

- All FeeConfiguration model locations across the codebase

- Risk assessment and sequencing considerations

- Downstream consumer mapping for future tickets

---
Acceptance Criteria

- The booking flow's fee configuration data includes IsWaivable and IsRefundable values from the database

- Existing behavior is preserved — all current fees return true for both properties (matching the database defaults)

- No customer-facing behavior changes

- DTO property defaults ensure safe behavior during rolling deploys (default to true if column not present)

---
Related

- CORE-14444 — Database columns (prerequisite, CLOSED)

- CORE-13901 — Parent epic

- CORE-14332 — LaunchDarkly gating (foundation, CLOSED)

- CORE-14117 — Fee messaging moved to post-calculation (foundation, CLOSED)

issues.summary: FeeConfiguration - Create Columns for GP Waivability and Refundability
issues.description:
Goal

Add explicit FeeConfiguration support for GolfPass waived-fee-credit waivability and refundability so each configured fee can independently define whether it can be waived by a GolfPass waived fee credit and whether it is refundable during cancellation/refund flows.

This is a foundational data/model ticket for the Customizable Transaction Fees epic. It should not attempt to build the full multi-fee framework, GNC UI revamp, fee messaging changes, tax handling, or revenue allocation behavior.

---
Background

The Customizable Transaction Fees epic requires different fee types to behave differently. For example:

- The standard GolfNow transaction/convenience fee may be waivable with a GolfPass waived fee credit.

- A tourism, city, county, or other regulatory fee may need to be non-waivable.

- Some fees may be refundable.

- Some fees may be non-refundable.

Today, FeeConfiguration does not have clear per-fee fields that let downstream systems determine these behaviors from configuration. We need to add those fields first so future tickets can safely apply waiver and refund behavior without hard-coding fee categories.

---
Scope

Add new fields to the FeeConfiguration data model to support per-fee behavior:

- GolfPass waivable flag

- Indicates whether this fee can be waived by a GolfPass waived-fee-credit benefit.

- Example values: true for standard GolfNow transaction fee, false for tourism/city/county fees.

- Refundable flag

- Indicates whether this fee is refundable when a reservation is cancelled/refunded.

issues.descriptionHtml:
Goal

Add explicit FeeConfiguration support for GolfPass waived-fee-credit waivability and refundability so each configured fee can independently define whether it can be waived by a GolfPass waived fee credit and whether it is refundable during cancellation/refund flows.

This is a foundational data/model ticket for the Customizable Transaction Fees epic. It should not attempt to build the full multi-fee framework, GNC UI revamp, fee messaging changes, tax handling, or revenue allocation behavior.

Background

The Customizable Transaction Fees epic requires different fee types to behave differently. For example:

  • The standard GolfNow transaction/convenience fee may be waivable with a GolfPass waived fee credit.

  • A tourism, city, county, or other regulatory fee may need to be non-waivable.

  • Some fees may be refundable.

  • Some fees may be non-refundable.

Today, FeeConfiguration does not have clear per-fee fields that let downstream systems determine these behaviors from configuration. We need to add those fields first so future tickets can safely apply waiver and refund behavior without hard-coding fee categories.

Scope

Add new fields to the FeeConfiguration data model to support per-fee behavior:

  • GolfPass waivable flag

    • Indicates whether this fee can be waived by a GolfPass waived-fee-credit benefit.

    • Example values: true for standard GolfNow transaction fee, false for tourism/city/county fees.

  • Refundable flag

    • Indicates whether this fee is refundable when a reservation is cancelled/refunded.

    • Example values: true for refundable convenience fees, false for non-refundable tourism/city/county fees.

Implementation should include the appropriate database/schema changes and any required data access/model/DTO updates so these values can be read by downstream API, Reservation Service, and future GNC configuration work.

Defaults / Backward Compatibility

Existing production behavior must remain unchanged after the columns are added.

Default values for existing FeeConfiguration records should preserve current behavior (current behavior is that all fees and waivable and refundable).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. FeeConfiguration schema supports a per-fee GolfPass waivable field.

  2. FeeConfiguration schema supports a per-fee refundable field.

  3. Existing FeeConfiguration records are backfilled/defaulted so current production behavior is preserved.

  4. The new fields can be read wherever FeeConfiguration data is retrieved for API/Reservation Service use.

  5. No customer-facing behavior changes unless explicitly required to preserve existing behavior.

  6. No GNC UI changes are included in this ticket.

  7. Engineering documents the chosen default values for existing fee records.

issues.summary: [Commerce] Facility Closure / Update casing Tee Times to Fail in the Add to Cart process
issues.description:
When adding Tee Times to cart when the course has an update (such as reducing to 9 holes from 18 holes) it fails with an error message stating the Tee Time could not be found. Root cause is that the store procedure that gets the tee times only filters facilities if they have an active closure. This needs to be updated so it also looks at if Disable

Inventory is true and allow facilities that are active but don’t have disable inventory set to true.

issues.summary: [TO] LEGACY - Support GolfPass Cancellations
issues.description:
In order to meet compliance for price increased products, we will need to expose a subscription cancellation option in the Membership Settings page. This cancellation option will be conditional based on some API attributes. This applies to the GN Membership Settings as well as the GolfPass White Label Membership Settings.

- Design: https://www.figma.com/design/n4GhZL6oXgfk93DFUhn98h/Cancel-membership-button?node-id=246-46405&m=dev#1745521556

- APIs

- Eligibility API - GET {{prod-api-base-url}}/GolfNowAPI.svc/rest/channel/{{ChannelId}}/customers/{{EmailAddress}}/subscriptions?productTypeId=9

- Target Field: IsEligibleForCancellation

- Cancel/Refund API: POST {{prod-api-base-url}}/GolfNowAPI.svc/rest/channel/{{ChannelId}}/customers/{{EmailAddress}}/subscriptions/{{CustomerSubscriptionId}}/cancelWithRefund

- CustomerSubscriptionId is found in the first endpoint

- Request Body:

{
"CancellationReasonId": 1,
"CancelEvenIfBenefitsUsed": true,
"RefundType": 1,
"SystemUserId": 1
}

- Always pass in CancellationReasonId = 1

- This means “Too Expensive”

- Always pass in CancelEvenIfBenefitsUsed = true

- Always Pass in RefundType = 0

- This means “Full Refund”

- Always pass in SystemUserId = 1

- Logic

- If IsEligibleForCancellation = true

- Display the Cancel Subscription option - Passed

- Tapping the button should open a modal with the option to confirm - Passed

- Confirming should submit the Cancel/Refund API above - Passed

- Membership settings should reload the page with the “No active memberships” treatment and we should make sure we resubmit any customer data in the site to make sure they are no longer recognized as a GP Member - Passed

- Remove the GP icons under their name, show the non member version of various pages, etc - Passed

- Currently this page is only accessible for members so a part of this work will be to make this Membership Settings page visible for all users - Passed

- Non members will simply see the no memberships version in the design - Passed

- To display the recently cancelled subscription info, you can add this to the Get Subscription API: &cancelledIncluded=true

- If IsEligibleForCancellation = false

- Do not show the Cancel Subscription option and the page will remain as is - Passed

- For the GolfPass CTA when you are not a member, link to the following product

- GN US/TO Prod: /7129411482949

- QA: /7129410862949 Passed

- GN UK Prod: /4929411702949

- QA: /492946602949

- GN AU Prod: /4529411712949

- QA: /452941462949

- Testing

- Most of the test cases are listed https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-14272 Passed

- Happy Path - Passed

- Create a user with a State of New York and billing address also in New York

- Buy one of the $119 free trial products

- Renew into the paid $119 product

- The IsEligibleForCancellation should be true as long as today’s date is within 15 days of the renewal date

- The Cancel Option should show

issues.summary: Apple Pay Follow Up Bugs
issues.description:
- Merchant Key Mismatch

- When we try to book a teetime that is for a full stack facility. We are generating the PaymentMethodKey using the chargeBy merchantKey, but at the time of transaction, we are doing it with the fullstack merchantKey that is different than the chargeBy. This is causing issues on payment processing. We should use the merchantKey that we are going to use for the transaction to generate the paymentMethodKey. (This will not required changes from CORE side since Payment processing team is going to fix this on their end)

- Guest support

- Currently guests cannot create wallets. This fails the apple pay flow because we need it stored for No Shows. We need to update guest logic to store a wallet ONLY if it is apple pay

- Credit cards should not create a stored wallet for Guest

- Add authorization to the reservation flow

- This already exists in the subscription flow

issues.summary: Use LaunchDarkly for configuration + accept FacilityId and ChannelId inputs
issues.description:
We need to replace the current web.config-based toggling for the FeeConfiguration code with a server-side LaunchDarkly feature flag. The goal is to be able to remotely enable the FeeConfiguration behavior in production for testing without editing web.config or temporarily hard-coding IDs.

This work supports the larger change to move fee messaging to run after final fee totals are composed (https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CORE-14117#icft=CORE-14117). This ticket focuses only on the feature-flagging and configuration input portion: enable FeeConfiguration through LaunchDarkly.

Acceptance Criteria

- LaunchDarkly flag created

- A server-side LaunchDarkly feature flag is created

- Behavior and fallback

- Default behavior remains legacy (FeeConfiguration disabled) unless the LaunchDarkly flag enables it.

- While migrating, if LaunchDarkly is unreachable for any reason, the code should fall back to the existing CRMConfig value (so production safety is maintained). A separate follow-up can remove the fallback after rollout.

- Operational readiness

- Logging of some sort includes whether FeeConfiguration was enabled by LaunchDarkly and the facilityId/channelId used for evaluation

NOTE: This will connect to both API 2.1 and Reservation Service

Removed the FacilityId/ChannelId context key from this ticket, will consider implementing in a future ticket. - @Daniel McNaughton

issues.description:
Apple Pay supports the ability for multi merchant transactions. We need to update our current Apple Pay logic to support this as well. This will be used for tee time + GolfPass transactions in sidecart. We very likely need to revisit our original apple pay workflow and clean it up.

Apple Pay Docs: https://applepaydemo.apple.com/ , https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-pay , https://developer.apple.com/apple-pay/marketing/ , https://developer.apple.com/apple-pay/sandbox-testing/

- Design: https://www.figma.com/design/mOWXt8yuZAaHEXULT5utOa/Apple-Pay---MVP?node-id=59-117&p=f&m=dev

- When a user attempts to purchase a tee time + golfpass sidecart, submit the cryptograms to API 2.1

issues.summary: Move Fee-Messaging to Post-Fee-Calculation & Use FeeConfiguration (API 2.1)
issues.description:
The original story proposed adding a new stored procedure + API toggle to decouple fee retrieval from the TeeTime stored procedure. After discussion with @Daniel McNaughton, we will not change stored procedures. Instead we’ll use the FeeConfiguration module in API 2.1 for this work and ensure fee messaging executes only after the final tee-time transaction fee totals are calculated.

The current problem: Fee Messaging (starting at line ~1727 in TeeTimeRepository.cs) executes too early in the pipeline and therefore does not see the final transaction fee totals. When FeeConfiguration is enabled (or when Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees is modified), the early messaging produces incorrect fee messages.

Goal:

- Identify the place(s) in the request pipeline where all fee calculation logic is completed (including FeeConfiguration module behavior and any Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees overrides).

- Move the fee-messaging process to operate on tee-times after that point so messaging always reflects the final, composed transaction fee totals.

- Use the existing FeeConfiguration module in API 2.1 (no stored proc changes). Default legacy behavior must remain unchanged unless FeeConfiguration is enabled.

Affected endpoints / flows (as called out in the original ticket)

- API 2.1 GetTeeTimes

- API 2.1 GetInvoice

- API 2.1 TeeTimeInvoice

- Reservation Service — Invoice flow
(These endpoints must behave consistently after the change.)

---
Example:

- Revenue team updates trade transaction fees at FID 55 from $3.49 to $1.99

- This update is stored in Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees (not CRMOwnerGolfFacility)

- Current outcome: The API returns $3.49 fee messaging and therefore the UI displays this incorrect value

- Expected outcome: The API should return the $1.99 fee messaging in order for front end to display the correct value

Note: The transaction fee is correct at the invoice level, it’s just the Fee Messaging that needs updated

API results:

UI results:

---

Acceptance Criteria

- No stored proc changes. The database stored procedures remain unchanged. Fee retrieval is performed via the FeeConfiguration module in API 2.1 when enabled.

- Fee-messaging runs only after final totals. Fee-messaging logic is moved so it operates on tee-times after the application layer has composed final totals (after FeeConfiguration and any Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees adjustments). Messaging content must match the final totals.

- Behavior parity / safe default. Default behavior (when FeeConfiguration is disabled) remains identical to current production behavior. When FeeConfiguration is enabled, messages reflect fee totals produced by the FeeConfiguration module + any Revenue.DynamicTransactionFees overrides.

- All affected endpoints updated. GetTeeTimes, GetInvoice, TeeTimeInvoice, and Reservation Service invoice flows all produce correct fee messaging across both legacy and FeeConfiguration-enabled modes.

---
Technical Notes / Implementation Guidance

- Investigation phase

- Locate the fee-messaging implementation referenced by Daniel — currently beginning at ~line 1727 in TeeTimeRepository.cs. Review how and when it runs relative to fee composition.

- Identify every place in the code path where transaction fees are finalized/aggregated for the affected endpoints (for example, final composition in application layer or where invoice totals are built). This may be inside TeeTimeRepository post-processing, invoice composition routines, or Reservation Service invoice flow.

- Identify where FeeConfiguration module is invoked for API 2.1 calls (and where FeeConfiguration may alter totals). Confirm how FeeConfiguration combines with Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees.

- Move/Refactor fee-messaging

- Extract/encapsulate the fee-messaging code so it can be invoked after final totals are composed. The new invocation point should be the single canonical location where the final tee-time totals are guaranteed to be complete (i.e., after any FeeConfiguration logic and any dynamic fee overrides).

- Ensure the message builder references the final totals from the in-memory tee-time objects returned to the API layer (not from intermediate values).

- Where multiple flows produce tee-times (GetTeeTimes, GetInvoice, TeeTimeInvoice, Reservation Service), make sure each flow invokes the new post-composition messaging path.

- FeeConfiguration integration

- When FeeConfiguration is enabled, ensure fee-messaging consumes totals that FeeConfiguration produced (API 2.1 module). If FeeConfiguration is disabled, ensure existing legacy totals and messaging are used.

- Ensure that changes in Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees also reflect in the final totals that the message consumes.

issues.summary: Payment Processors (Gift Card, Apple Pay, Funded Coupon) and Execution Layer (specs 028-029)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 028 and 029 deliver the final Phase 1 payment processor implementations and the durable execution layer that orchestrates them.

- Spec 028 (.specify/specs/028-payment-adapters-giftcard-applepay-fundedcoupon/spec.md) defines processor behavior for GolfNow gift card, EZLinks gift card, Apple Pay, and funded coupon tenders — the remaining Phase 1 processors beyond CreditCard (spec 024), Affiliate, and AccountBalance (spec 026b). Builds on route-selected processor resolution (spec 026b) and the tokenization pipeline (spec 027a).

- Spec 029 (.specify/specs/029-payment-execution-journals-idempotency/spec.md) defines the durable execution layer for AUTH, CAPTURE, CREDIT, and VOID actions across all payment processors. Adds the execution coordinator, PaymentAttempt persistence, immutable PaymentActivityJournal and PaymentDecisionJournal entries, ExecutedProcessorContext capture, and idempotency enforcement across saga retries.

These belong together because spec 029 depends on spec 028 processors being in place, and both specs together complete the Phase 1 payment execution surface.

Scope

Spec 028 — Processors

- Gift card processor family (GolfNow + EZLinks) implementing IPaymentProcessor + IBalanceQueryProcessor.

- Real-time gift card balance query via IBalanceQueryProcessor.GetBalanceAsync (non-mutating).

- Apple Pay processor consuming only tokenized/normalized instrument references from spec 027a.

- Funded coupon processor treating funded coupon as PaymentMethodType.FundedCoupon, not an entitlement.

- ProcessorCapabilityDeclaration for all covered processors.

- Error normalization: insufficient balance, expired gift card, invalid coupon, processor unavailable, unsupported action.

- DI registration and route-selected processor resolution per spec 026b.

Spec 029 — Execution Layer

- Payment execution coordinator invoked by checkout and post-purchase sagas.

- PaymentAttempt creation/update (UUIDv7 business id) per action per route group.

- PaymentActivityJournal and PaymentDecisionJournal append rules (immutable, no PCI data).

- Adapter idempotency key generation and replay behavior (same request id → return committed result).

- ExecutedProcessorContext capture for refund/void routing independence.

- Per-action retry and failure classification boundaries.

- Multi-merchant authorization: distinct attempts for one tender split across merchant route groups.

- SCA/customer-action-required pause logic for the attempt chain.

Out of Scope

- CreditCard, Affiliate, and AccountBalance processors.

- Circuit breaker and failover decision policy.

- SCA challenge callback flow (callback handling deferred).

- Funding source accounting policy for coupons.

- New external gift-card service schema.

- Payment journal retention/archival beyond live operational storage.

Acceptance Criteria

Spec 028

- Spec 028 .specify/specs/028-payment-adapters-giftcard-applepay-fundedcoupon/spec.md references this Jira ticket.

- GolfNow and EZLinks gift card processors implement IPaymentProcessor + IBalanceQueryProcessor.

- Apple Pay processor consumes only tokenized/normalized references; unnormalized payloads are rejected before external I/O.

- FundedCouponProcessor treats funded coupon as PaymentMethodType.FundedCoupon and never routes through entitlement providers.

- All processors expose a complete ProcessorCapabilityDeclaration; unsupported actions are rejected by capability checks, not processor exceptions.

- Gift card, Apple Pay, and funded coupon expected business failures return non-throwing ResultWrapper-compatible typed results.

- IBalanceQueryProcessor.GetBalanceAsync returns available balance, currency code, and expiration date for a valid gift card reference without any ledger mutation.

- Gift card balance query failures (expired card, unavailable service, invalid reference) return typed BalanceQueryResult statuses and do not throw.

- IPaymentProcessorRegistry.TryGetBalanceQueryProcessor returns true for all registered gift card PaymentProcessorKey values.

- No processor log path leaks full token, wallet payload, or gift-card secret data (PCI compliance per spec 003).

- Funded coupon appears only in payment tests and never in entitlement provider tests.

Spec 029
12. Spec 029 .specify/specs/029-payment-execution-journals-idempotency/spec.md references this Jira ticket.
13. A payment execution coordinator handles AUTH, CAPTURE, CREDIT, and VOID for all Phase 1 processors.
14. Every payment action creates or updates a PaymentAttempt with a UUIDv7 business id.
15. Every payment action appends an immutable PaymentActivityJournal entry.
16. Every adapter/action selection appends an immutable PaymentDecisionJournal entry including route snapshot identity, AdapterKey, payment method, processor code, action, and reason.
17. Successful adapter results persist ExecutedProcessorContext with AdapterKey, processor code, gateway code (where applicable), adapter configuration reference, processor merchant account reference, and processor transaction identifiers.
18. Duplicate execution requests with the same request id return the committed result without re-invoking the adapter.
19. Expected payment declines are non-throwing outcomes; infrastructure failures may throw per saga policy.
20. One tender split across two merchants creates two distinct PaymentAttempt records with different merchant/route context and idempotency identities.
21. Refund, capture, and void actions route from original ExecutedProcessorContext.AdapterKey and configuration reference, not a fresh route snapshot.
22. Journal serialization passes PCI-sensitive data analyzer checks (spec 003).

issues.descriptionHtml:
Context

Specs 028 and 029 deliver the final Phase 1 payment processor implementations and the durable execution layer that orchestrates them.

  • Spec 028 (.specify/specs/028-payment-adapters-giftcard-applepay-fundedcoupon/spec.md) defines processor behavior for GolfNow gift card, EZLinks gift card, Apple Pay, and funded coupon tenders — the remaining Phase 1 processors beyond CreditCard (spec 024), Affiliate, and AccountBalance (spec 026b). Builds on route-selected processor resolution (spec 026b) and the tokenization pipeline (spec 027a).

  • Spec 029 (.specify/specs/029-payment-execution-journals-idempotency/spec.md) defines the durable execution layer for AUTH, CAPTURE, CREDIT, and VOID actions across all payment processors. Adds the execution coordinator, PaymentAttempt persistence, immutable PaymentActivityJournal and PaymentDecisionJournal entries, ExecutedProcessorContext capture, and idempotency enforcement across saga retries.

These belong together because spec 029 depends on spec 028 processors being in place, and both specs together complete the Phase 1 payment execution surface.

Scope

Spec 028 — Processors

  • Gift card processor family (GolfNow + EZLinks) implementing IPaymentProcessor + IBalanceQueryProcessor.

  • Real-time gift card balance query via IBalanceQueryProcessor.GetBalanceAsync (non-mutating).

  • Apple Pay processor consuming only tokenized/normalized instrument references from spec 027a.

  • Funded coupon processor treating funded coupon as PaymentMethodType.FundedCoupon, not an entitlement.

  • ProcessorCapabilityDeclaration for all covered processors.

  • Error normalization: insufficient balance, expired gift card, invalid coupon, processor unavailable, unsupported action.

  • DI registration and route-selected processor resolution per spec 026b.

Spec 029 — Execution Layer

  • Payment execution coordinator invoked by checkout and post-purchase sagas.

  • PaymentAttempt creation/update (UUIDv7 business id) per action per route group.

  • PaymentActivityJournal and PaymentDecisionJournal append rules (immutable, no PCI data).

  • Adapter idempotency key generation and replay behavior (same request id → return committed result).

  • ExecutedProcessorContext capture for refund/void routing independence.

  • Per-action retry and failure classification boundaries.

  • Multi-merchant authorization: distinct attempts for one tender split across merchant route groups.

  • SCA/customer-action-required pause logic for the attempt chain.

Out of Scope

  • CreditCard, Affiliate, and AccountBalance processors.

  • Circuit breaker and failover decision policy.

  • SCA challenge callback flow (callback handling deferred).

  • Funding source accounting policy for coupons.

  • New external gift-card service schema.

  • Payment journal retention/archival beyond live operational storage.

Acceptance Criteria

Spec 028

  1. Spec 028 .specify/specs/028-payment-adapters-giftcard-applepay-fundedcoupon/spec.md references this Jira ticket.

  2. GolfNow and EZLinks gift card processors implement IPaymentProcessor + IBalanceQueryProcessor.

  3. Apple Pay processor consumes only tokenized/normalized references; unnormalized payloads are rejected before external I/O.

  4. FundedCouponProcessor treats funded coupon as PaymentMethodType.FundedCoupon and never routes through entitlement providers.

  5. All processors expose a complete ProcessorCapabilityDeclaration; unsupported actions are rejected by capability checks, not processor exceptions.

  6. Gift card, Apple Pay, and funded coupon expected business failures return non-throwing ResultWrapper-compatible typed results.

  7. IBalanceQueryProcessor.GetBalanceAsync returns available balance, currency code, and expiration date for a valid gift card reference without any ledger mutation.

  8. Gift card balance query failures (expired card, unavailable service, invalid reference) return typed BalanceQueryResult statuses and do not throw.

  9. IPaymentProcessorRegistry.TryGetBalanceQueryProcessor returns true for all registered gift card PaymentProcessorKey values.

  10. No processor log path leaks full token, wallet payload, or gift-card secret data (PCI compliance per spec 003).

  11. Funded coupon appears only in payment tests and never in entitlement provider tests.

Spec 029 12. Spec 029 .specify/specs/029-payment-execution-journals-idempotency/spec.md references this Jira ticket. 13. A payment execution coordinator handles AUTH, CAPTURE, CREDIT, and VOID for all Phase 1 processors. 14. Every payment action creates or updates a PaymentAttempt with a UUIDv7 business id. 15. Every payment action appends an immutable PaymentActivityJournal entry. 16. Every adapter/action selection appends an immutable PaymentDecisionJournal entry including route snapshot identity, AdapterKey, payment method, processor code, action, and reason. 17. Successful adapter results persist ExecutedProcessorContext with AdapterKey, processor code, gateway code (where applicable), adapter configuration reference, processor merchant account reference, and processor transaction identifiers. 18. Duplicate execution requests with the same request id return the committed result without re-invoking the adapter. 19. Expected payment declines are non-throwing outcomes; infrastructure failures may throw per saga policy. 20. One tender split across two merchants creates two distinct PaymentAttempt records with different merchant/route context and idempotency identities. 21. Refund, capture, and void actions route from original ExecutedProcessorContext.AdapterKey and configuration reference, not a fresh route snapshot. 22. Journal serialization passes PCI-sensitive data analyzer checks (spec 003). 23. A tender is not marked fully authorized until all required route-group authorization attempts for that tender are terminal success.

Build gate 24. dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds. 25. dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

issues.summary: Customer Wallet Option Management (spec 027c)
issues.description:
Spec: .specify/specs/027c-wallet-options-management/spec.md

Overview

Implement customer-facing wallet management operations that let an authenticated user list, view, create, update, and remove saved wallet options. Customer is derived from the authenticated request context — never from caller-supplied email or customer number.

Dependencies

Spec 003 (PCI observability), spec 006 (customer authentication), spec 007 (customer identity integration), spec 010 (request feature-flag context), spec 016 (platform principal identity), spec 018 (PaymentMethodType alignment), spec 027a (WalletOption normalization).

Scope

- Expose GET /api/v1/payments/wallet-options, GET /api/v1/payments/wallet-options/{id}, POST /api/v1/payments/wallet-options, PUT /api/v1/payments/wallet-options/{id}, DELETE /api/v1/payments/wallet-options/{id} under the Payments MVC area.

- Return PCI-safe masked display metadata only; never return raw PAN, CVV, PIN, gift-card number, or encrypted secrets in responses, logs, traces, or idempotency replays.

- Discriminated create/update request models by paymentMethodType; no legacy polymorphic DTOs on the public surface.

- Credit-card PAN allowed on create only; update rejects PAN replacement.

- Default credit-card behavior through UpdateWalletOption with isDefault = true.

- Idempotency-Key required on all write operations; replay returns sanitized response without duplicate Wallet side effects.

- Delegate to legacy Wallet / Customer Service / payment-method-specific service boundaries; no direct legacy SQL writes.

Out of Scope

Checkout tender normalization (spec 027a), encrypted transient secret storage (spec 027b), payment authorization/capture/refund/void, invoice finalization, direct Wallet SQL.

Acceptance Criteria

- Authenticated customer can list/retrieve wallet options without raw payment data.

- Credit-card wallet option can be created and used as a saved WalletOptionReference during checkout normalization (027a).

- Updating card expiration/default state changes the Wallet option without allowing PAN replacement.

- Removing a Wallet option prevents future checkout use while preserving historical order references.

- Write-operation idempotency prevents duplicate legacy Wallet mutations; raw payment secrets never stored, compared, logged, or replayed.

- Unsupported mutation attempts fail deterministically with WALLET_OPTION_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED.

issues.summary: Payment Tokenization and Wallet Instrument Normalization (spec 027a)
issues.description:
Spec: .specify/specs/027a-payment-tokenization-wallet-instrument-normalization/spec.md

Overview

Implement the checkout/payment orchestration phase that converts caller-supplied payment tenders into normalized, PCI-safe execution references before route snapshot lookup or adapter execution.

Dependencies

Spec 003 PCI observability, spec 018 PaymentMethodType alignment, spec 023 payment plan validation, spec 024 tokenized adapter references, payment pipeline spec v2.11 sections 8.5 and 16.6.

Scope

- Accept RawInstrument or WalletOptionReference tender inputs on POST /orders; exactly one source shape per caller-supplied tender.

- Tokenize raw/transient credit-card and Apple Pay inputs through approved PaymentProcessing boundaries.

- Create, reuse, or resolve legacy Wallet-backed references, including parent card Wallet options, linked external token options, direct payment-method-key options, gift cards, account balance, Apple Pay, and known legacy tender shapes.

- Import finalized invoice TenderCouponApplications[] as invoice-sourced payment tenders and reject ad hoc coupon-code tender inputs on POST /orders.

- Persist only PCI-safe Wallet/reference lineage, masked display metadata, and executed processor context; never persist raw PAN, CVV, PIN, raw Apple Pay payloads, encrypted secret payloads, or transient secret handles.

- Revalidate balance-backed tenders after saga suspension before execution resumes.

Out of Scope

Adapter execution, card processor-specific behavior, SCA continuation after adapter invocation, encrypted transient verification-secret storage (spec 027b), customer-facing WalletOption management APIs (spec 027c), Wallet schema ownership, and direct legacy SQL writes.

Acceptance Criteria

- Raw card, saved card with CVV, raw gift card with PIN, saved gift/account-balance options, Apple Pay payloads, and invoice-sourced tender coupons normalize to the correct execution reference shape before adapters run.

- Saved WalletOption input validates customer/channel ownership, active/deleted/expired state, payment-type compatibility, and required verification-secret presence before normalization succeeds.

- Stored cards produce or reuse the legacy parent credit-card Wallet option and linked external Wallet option containing the PaymentMethodKey when Versant execution requires it.

- Known legacy Wallet payment types map according to the spec matrix and unsupported Phase 1 methods fail deterministically without fabricating PaymentMethodKey values.

- Tokenization retries are idempotent and reuse the original normalized reference for the same orchestration request id.

- Tests prove sensitive inputs are absent from durable saga, order, journal, idempotency, log, trace, exception, and support payloads.

issues.summary: Payment Adapter Contract and Non-Scarcity Reservation Semantics (specs 024-025)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 024-025 cover two related checkout execution foundation slices for the order-processing service:

- Spec 024 (.specify/specs/024-payment-adapter-contract-credit-card/spec.md) defines the payment adapter boundary, action-specific request/result contracts, adapter capability declarations, adapter resolution, the balance-query seam, and the CreditCard reference adapter wrapping the existing PaymentProcessing client.

- Spec 025 (.specify/specs/025-non-scarcity-inventory-reservations/spec.md) evolves inventory reservation semantics so non-scarcity domains such as GolfNowSubscription can pass checkout Block 3 without a provider-side hold while scarce domains such as TeeTime retain full hold lifecycle behavior.

These belong together because they prepare checkout execution for real side-effect boundaries: payment adapters must execute only through a normalized, PCI-safe capability contract, and reservation semantics must distinguish scarce holds from intentional non-scarcity no-op success before checkout orchestration composes inventory and payment blocks.

Scope

- Define a single IPaymentAdapter interface for AuthorizeAsync, CaptureAsync, CreditAsync, and VoidAsync.

- Define action-specific request/result types for AUTH, CAPTURE, CREDIT, and VOID.

- Add strongly typed adapter capability declarations containing the matrix dimensions needed by validation, decisioning, and execution.

- Add PaymentAdapterFactory resolution by canonical PaymentMethodType.

- Define IBalanceQueryAdapter as the seam for later balance-backed methods.

- Implement the CreditCard reference adapter around GolfNow.Payment.APIPaymentProcessingClient using tokenized payment references.

- Normalize provider declines and expected validation failures to non-throwing adapter outcomes.

- Keep adapter logging and observability compliant with PCI constraints from spec 003.

- Extend inventory reservation contracts with explicit non-scarcity success classification distinct from unsupported-domain behavior.

- Add domain reservation policy/configuration for scarce versus non-scarcity-enabled domains, including GolfNowSubscription support.

- Ensure checkout Block 3 treats non-scarcity reservation outcomes as success while preserving TeeTime hold lifecycle behavior.

- Support deterministic non-scarcity no-op outcomes for reserve, extend, confirm, and release.

- Add tests for adapter resolution, capability declarations, CreditCard auth/capture/credit/void normalization, PCI-safe request validation/logging, non-scarcity-only checkout semantics, mixed scarce/non-scarce invoices, compensation release behavior, confirm behavior, and unsupported-domain distinction.

Out of Scope

- Gift card, account balance, affiliate, ApplePay, and funded coupon adapter implementations.

- Payment execution orchestration, journals, decision engine/failover, SCA challenge flow, scheduled payments, or tokenization implementation beyond requiring tokenized input.

- Subscription pricing logic changes.

- Subscription entitlement consumption logic.

- Timelyst scarcity policy decision; this spec only permits either scarcity or non-scarcity classification later.

- Checkout saga redesign beyond Block 3 semantics and adapter boundary readiness.

- Post-purchase financial policy changes; spec 014 remains authoritative.

Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 024 and 025 files reference this Jira ticket.

- IPaymentAdapter exposes AuthorizeAsync, CaptureAsync, CreditAsync, and VoidAsync with action-specific request and result types.

- Adapter request models carry orchestration RequestId, amount, currency, payment method reference, route context, and cancellation token.

- Adapter capability declarations expose supported actions and behavior flags required by validation, decisioning, and execution.

- PaymentAdapterFactory resolves adapters by canonical PaymentMethodType and returns non-throwing unsupported-adapter results for unregistered methods.

- CreditCard adapter wraps GolfNow.Payment.APIPaymentProcessingClient and consumes tokenized references such as PaymentMethodKey; tokenization remains outside adapters.

- CreditCard auth, capture, credit, and void paths normalize provider transaction references, declines, validation failures, and expected processor outcomes without throwing.

- Credit requests carry original transaction or executed processor context and do not encode cancellation eligibility; refundability and cancellability remain upstream adjustment-decision concerns.

- Adapter paths satisfy PCI observability constraints and do not log PAN, CVV, full tokens, passwords, or sensitive wallet payloads.

- IBalanceQueryAdapter exists for future balance-backed adapters, and CreditCard does not implement it.

- Reservation results include explicit non-scarcity success classification distinct from UnsupportedDomain.

- Checkout Block 3 treats non-scarcity reservation outcomes as success and does not require hold identifiers for non-scarcity domains.

- Non-scarcity reserve, extend, confirm, and release operations return deterministic no-op success outcomes without fabricating InventoryHoldId, DomainHoldId, or confirmation evidence.

- GolfNowSubscription is supportable through non-scarcity reservation semantics without requiring a hold lifecycle implementation.

- Scarce TeeTime reservation behavior remains unchanged for reserve, extend, confirm, release, compensation, and hold lifecycle data.

- Mixed invoices containing TeeTime and Subscription groups complete with domain-appropriate reservation semantics and compensation behavior.

- Unsupported domains still fail distinctly from non-scarcity-enabled domains.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

- Specs: .specify/specs/024-payment-adapter-contract-credit-card/spec.md, .specify/specs/025-non-scarcity-inventory-reservations/spec.md

- Related: specs 003, 014, 018, 020, 021, 023, payment pipeline spec v2.11, pipeline spec Section 10A and checkout Block 3

- Parent docs: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-entities.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-payment-pipeline-spec-v2.md

- Epic: CORE-14269

issues.summary: Entitlement Providers and Payment Plan Validation (specs 022-023)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 022-023 cover two related checkout foundation slices for the order-processing service:

- Spec 022 (.specify/specs/022-entitlement-provider-implementations/spec.md) implements Phase 1 provider surfaces for loyalty and benefit entitlements, including consume and reverse operations, idempotency, audit references, compensation behavior, and explicit exclusion of funded coupons because they are payment tenders.

- Spec 023 (.specify/specs/023-payment-domain-model-plan-validation/spec.md) defines the payment sub-aggregate embedded in saga_checkout and validates a checkout payment plan before route snapshot lookup or adapter execution.

These belong together because checkout needs a clean boundary between entitlements and tenders before payment adapters run. Loyalty and benefit consumption can affect checkout state and compensation, while payment plan validation ensures finalized invoices, tenders, charge allocations, merchant grouping, zero-dollar behavior, and unsupported payment methods are resolved before any payment side effects start.

Scope

- Define or implement IEntitlementProvider surfaces for Loyalty and Benefit entitlement types.

- Support entitlement consume and reverse operations with provider-level request idempotency.

- Persist enough entitlement consumption provider reference data to support later reversal and audit.

- Map expected entitlement provider outcomes to checkout/post-purchase taxonomy without throwing for business failures.

- Carry ActorContext from spec 016 on entitlement consumption and reversal records.

- Exclude FundedCoupon from entitlement handling and keep it in payment tender planning.

- Model payment state as a sub-aggregate inside saga_checkout, not as a separate payment saga collection.

- Build payment tenders, charge item allocations, computed distribution instructions, route snapshot grouping inputs, and payment attempt skeletons from a Finalized invoice.

issues.summary: Inventory Reservation Implementations (spec 021)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 021 covers the Phase 1 inventory reservation provider path for the order-processing service:

- Spec 021 (.specify/specs/021-inventory-reservation-implementations/spec.md) implements the shared inventory reservation contract for TeeTime inventory and establishes explicit deferred behavior for Subscription and Timelyst domains.

This belongs as its own implementation slice because checkout Block 3 and compensation need provider-level reserve, confirm, release, and extend behavior before checkout orchestration can safely depend on durable inventory holds. The work also prevents non-TeeTime domains from accidentally routing through TeeTime reservation code before their domain-specific implementations are ready.

Scope

- Implement IInventoryReservationProvider for TeeTime inventory.

- Add provider factory/registry resolution by item group domain.

- Support reserve, confirm, release, and extend operations for TeeTime holds.

- Use orchestration-generated provider request ids for provider-level idempotency.

- Map item-level ItemQuantity with Quantity.Type=Players to TeeTime provider player count.

- Return orchestration InventoryHoldId and provider DomainHoldId from reserve operations.

- Return fulfillment/booking evidence from confirm operations for downstream fulfillment workflows.

- Classify reservation failures as retryable infrastructure, unavailable inventory, validation, already-completed, or terminal provider failures.

- Add explicit Subscription and Timelyst placeholder/deferred provider behavior until those domain implementations land.

- Add tests for TeeTime reserve, confirm, release, extend, idempotent retries, invalid quantity handling, provider resolution, unsupported domains, and failure classification.

Out of Scope

- Checkout saga implementation itself.

- Payment authorization or capture.

- Full Subscription and Timelyst reservation provider implementations.

- Physical attendance or no-show policy.

- Repricing during reservation.

- Post-purchase cancellation decision logic; confirmed inventory release/cancel remains gated by spec 014 adjustment decisions.

Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 021 file references this Jira ticket.

- TeeTime implements IInventoryReservationProvider for reserve, confirm, release, and extend operations.

- Provider resolution is based on ItemGroup.Domain and cannot route Subscription or Timelyst item groups to TeeTime reservation logic.

- TeeTime reservation maps Item.Quantity.Value with Quantity.Type=Players to the provider player count.

- TeeTime reservation rejects non-whole, non-positive, or non-Players quantities with ResultWrapper-compatible validation/business errors.

- Reserve, confirm, release, and extend accept an orchestration-generated request id and behave idempotently on retries.

- Reserve returns both an orchestration InventoryHoldId and provider DomainHoldId.

- Confirm returns fulfillment or booking evidence required by spec 015.

- Release is idempotent and treats already-released as a successful outcome.

- Post-purchase release or provider-side cancellation of confirmed inventory requires an approved spec 014 cancellation decision for the item group; refundability alone is not sufficient.

- Extend uses provider-default hold extension where available and distinguishes retryable from terminal failures.

- Subscription and Timelyst provider behavior is explicit, deferred, and test-covered until their domain specs land.

- Expected provider outcomes map to checkout error taxonomy without throwing for unavailable inventory, validation, already-completed, or unsupported-domain cases.

- Reservation code preserves item-level ItemQuantity semantics and never reads currency from ItemGroup.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

- Spec: .specify/specs/021-inventory-reservation-implementations/spec.md

- Related: specs 002, 009, 012, 014, 015, 020

- Parent docs: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-entities.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-payment-pipeline-spec-v2.md

issues.summary: Invoice Modification, Reprice, and Finalization (specs 019-020)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 019-020 cover the remaining mutable invoice workflow before checkout:

- Spec 019 (.specify/specs/019-invoice-modification-reprice/spec.md) defines invoice modification and explicit reprice behavior so clients can edit active invoices, refresh expired invoices intentionally, preserve ItemQuantity, and rerun pricing, discounts, allocation, and estimated tax.

- Spec 020 (.specify/specs/020-invoice-finalization/spec.md) defines invoice finalization so an Active invoice becomes the hard customer-facing quote required before checkout, including availability re-checks, stale pricing refresh, authoritative tax calculation or fallback tax, and refundability snapshot capture.

These belong together because finalization depends on the mutation/reprice semantics: expired invoices must be explicitly repriced before finalization, price-affecting edits invalidate finalized quotes, and both flows enforce version-key conflict handling, checkout-lock rejection, item-level currency, and ItemQuantity preservation.

Scope

- Add invoice modification endpoint: PUT /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}.

- Add explicit invoice reprice endpoint: POST /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}/reprice.

- Add invoice finalization endpoint: POST /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices/{invoiceId}/finalize.

- Support adding/removing item groups and items, changing ItemQuantity, and adding/removing promo codes before checkout.

- Re-run pricing, benefit discounts, promo discounts, revenue allocation, and estimated tax for modifications and reprices.

- Reprice expired invoices explicitly without changing GET behavior.

- Enforce version-key conflict handling and checkout-lock rejection across modification, reprice, and finalization.

- Transition price-affecting changes to Finalized invoices back to Active.

- Finalize Active invoices by re-checking availability, refreshing stale item pricing, replacing estimated tax with final or fallback tax, and persisting refundability snapshots.

- Preserve corrected invoice model constraints: ItemQuantity travels as a value object, CurrencyCode is item-level only, and ItemGroup carries no currency.

- Add focused tests for update, reprice, finalization, stale version keys, invalid statuses, checkout locks, currency mismatches, removed item warnings, tax fallback, and refundability snapshot enforcement.

Out of Scope

- Checkout order creation, purchase locking beyond rejecting locked invoices, payment authorization/capture, reservations, entitlement consumption, or post-purchase item cancellation.

- Tax provider implementation details beyond consuming spec 011 contracts.

- Inventory reservation holds.

- Post-purchase adjustment decisions.

- Changing GET behavior to auto-reprice expired invoices.

Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 019 and 020 files reference this Jira ticket.

- PUT invoice modification requires the current versionKey and returns INVOICE_VERSION_CONFLICT for stale updates without modifying the invoice.

- PUT and reprice reject Purchased and checkout-locked invoices with domain-specific ResultWrapper-compatible errors.

- Invoice mutation accepts and persists item quantity only as ItemQuantity (Value + Type) and never as scalar/unit sibling fields.

- ItemGroup does not accept, persist, or return CurrencyCode; top-level invoice currency is derived from uniform item-level currencies.

- Modified and repriced invoices rerun pricing, tier selection, benefit discounts, promo discounts, revenue allocation, and estimated tax.

- Cross-currency modified, repriced, or finalized invoices fail with INVOICE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH.

- Explicit reprice can transition an Expired invoice back to Active when at least one item remains available.

- GET on an expired invoice remains read-only and does not auto-reprice.

- Partial item removal during modification or reprice returns a Warning response with removed item details.

- Price-affecting changes to a Finalized invoice transition it back to Active and require re-finalization.

- Finalize requires the current versionKey, operates only on Active invoices, rejects Expired invoices with reprice guidance, and rejects checkout-locked invoices.

- Finalize re-checks availability for every item and re-queries pricing only for stale PricingValidUntilUtc items unless availability changes require removal.

- Finalize performs a hard tax provider calculation when available and may persist EstimatedFallback tax only when spec 011 fallback conditions are satisfied.

- Finalize persists a non-null RefundabilitySnapshot on every purchasable component.

- Successful modification, reprice, and finalization all generate a new VersionKey.

- Mutating endpoints are protected by the global idempotency-key contract.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

- Specs: .specify/specs/019-invoice-modification-reprice/spec.md, .specify/specs/020-invoice-finalization/spec.md

- Related: specs 005, 010, 011, 012

- Parent docs: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-entities.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-payment-pipeline-spec-v2.md

- Epic: CORE-14269

issues.summary: Platform Principal, Accounting Facts, and Payment Method Alignment (specs 016-018)
issues.description:
Context

Specs 016-018 cover three related foundation slices for the order-processing service:

- Spec 016 (.specify/specs/016-platform-principal-identity/spec.md) defines a consistent platform principal and actor context model so transactional records can be audited back to the authenticated API credential or well-known system actor that initiated work.

- Spec 017 (.specify/specs/017-accounting-facts-export/spec.md) defines lean accounting fact fields and events so Finance/Accounting systems can consume deterministic business facts without embedding ASC 606 policy in order-processing.

- Spec 018 (.specify/specs/018-payment-method-type-alignment/spec.md) aligns the canonical PaymentMethodType values before payment adapters and checkout tenders build on them.

These belong together because they are cross-cutting contract/model groundwork: identity stamping feeds audit and accounting events, accounting exports depend on fulfillment/current-item facts and principal audit context, and payment method alignment keeps tender/cash-movement facts stable before later payment adapter work.

Scope

- Define PlatformPrincipal, ActorContext, principal resolution contracts, scoped request principal access, and well-known system principals.

- Add principal/actor stamping requirements to invoices, orders, credit memos, saga starts, payment attempts, adjustment overrides, fulfillment events, and accounting fact events where applicable.

- Define flat permission strings needed by adjustment override paths and future admin actions.

- Add minimal accounting fact fields for item timing, item quantity propagation, fulfillment evidence snapshots, and component product classification.

- Define purchase, fulfillment, credit memo, and no-show accounting fact event shapes that contain facts only.

- Enforce prohibited accounting-policy fields so order-processing does not persist ASC 606 conclusions.

- Align canonical Phase 1 PaymentMethodType values: CreditCard, GolfNowGiftCard, EzlGiftCard, AccountBalance, Affiliate, ApplePay, and FundedCoupon.

- Add legacy payment-method normalization for known historical values without accepting deprecated aliases on public wire contracts.

- Add focused tests for principal resolution/stamping, permission checks, accounting fact event shaping/prohibited fields, payment-method canonical serialization, unsupported method validation, and funded-coupon placement.

Out of Scope

- Authentication mechanism implementation, user provisioning, IAM administration, or RBAC UI.

- Customer identity replacement; customer identity remains separate from platform principal identity.

- ASC 606 policy engine, performance-obligation conclusions, seller-of-record legal conclusions, GL mapping, ERP posting, or close-process workflow.

- Payment adapter implementation or payment execution.

- Full accounting warehouse/reporting design.

- Public endpoint exposing principal details.

Acceptance Criteria

- Spec 016, 017, and 018 files reference this Jira ticket.

- PlatformPrincipal and ActorContext models are defined without coupling Core to ASP.NET HttpContext.

- Request-scoped and system principal access patterns support HTTP handlers, sagas, hosted services, and event-driven workflows.

- Permission checks use flat string set membership and support spec 014 adjustment override permissions.

- Transactional records stamped by this feature preserve immutable creator principal context and mutable last-modified principal context where applicable.

- Accounting fact models/events include item quantity, service timing, fulfillment evidence, component merchant/product classification, payment/cash movement references, and principal audit metadata where applicable.

- Accounting fact models/events contain business facts only and do not persist prohibited ASC 606 policy conclusion fields.

- Canonical Phase 1 PaymentMethodType values bind, serialize, and validate with stable PascalCase wire names.

- FundedCoupon is treated as a payment tender and not an entitlement type.

- Deprecated GiftCard, unsupported future methods, and unknown payment methods fail validation before adapter resolution.

- Legacy payment-method normalization supports known historical spellings for migration/internal use without exposing public aliases.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

issues.descriptionHtml:
Context

Specs 016-018 cover three related foundation slices for the order-processing service:

  • Spec 016 (.specify/specs/016-platform-principal-identity/spec.md) defines a consistent platform principal and actor context model so transactional records can be audited back to the authenticated API credential or well-known system actor that initiated work.

  • Spec 017 (.specify/specs/017-accounting-facts-export/spec.md) defines lean accounting fact fields and events so Finance/Accounting systems can consume deterministic business facts without embedding ASC 606 policy in order-processing.

  • Spec 018 (.specify/specs/018-payment-method-type-alignment/spec.md) aligns the canonical PaymentMethodType values before payment adapters and checkout tenders build on them.

These belong together because they are cross-cutting contract/model groundwork: identity stamping feeds audit and accounting events, accounting exports depend on fulfillment/current-item facts and principal audit context, and payment method alignment keeps tender/cash-movement facts stable before later payment adapter work.

Scope

  • Define PlatformPrincipal, ActorContext, principal resolution contracts, scoped request principal access, and well-known system principals.

  • Add principal/actor stamping requirements to invoices, orders, credit memos, saga starts, payment attempts, adjustment overrides, fulfillment events, and accounting fact events where applicable.

  • Define flat permission strings needed by adjustment override paths and future admin actions.

  • Add minimal accounting fact fields for item timing, item quantity propagation, fulfillment evidence snapshots, and component product classification.

  • Define purchase, fulfillment, credit memo, and no-show accounting fact event shapes that contain facts only.

  • Enforce prohibited accounting-policy fields so order-processing does not persist ASC 606 conclusions.

  • Align canonical Phase 1 PaymentMethodType values: CreditCard, GolfNowGiftCard, EzlGiftCard, AccountBalance, Affiliate, ApplePay, and FundedCoupon.

  • Add legacy payment-method normalization for known historical values without accepting deprecated aliases on public wire contracts.

  • Add focused tests for principal resolution/stamping, permission checks, accounting fact event shaping/prohibited fields, payment-method canonical serialization, unsupported method validation, and funded-coupon placement.

Out of Scope

  • Authentication mechanism implementation, user provisioning, IAM administration, or RBAC UI.

  • Customer identity replacement; customer identity remains separate from platform principal identity.

  • ASC 606 policy engine, performance-obligation conclusions, seller-of-record legal conclusions, GL mapping, ERP posting, or close-process workflow.

  • Payment adapter implementation or payment execution.

  • Full accounting warehouse/reporting design.

  • Public endpoint exposing principal details.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Spec 016, 017, and 018 files reference this Jira ticket.

  2. PlatformPrincipal and ActorContext models are defined without coupling Core to ASP.NET HttpContext.

  3. Request-scoped and system principal access patterns support HTTP handlers, sagas, hosted services, and event-driven workflows.

  4. Permission checks use flat string set membership and support spec 014 adjustment override permissions.

  5. Transactional records stamped by this feature preserve immutable creator principal context and mutable last-modified principal context where applicable.

  6. Accounting fact models/events include item quantity, service timing, fulfillment evidence, component merchant/product classification, payment/cash movement references, and principal audit metadata where applicable.

  7. Accounting fact models/events contain business facts only and do not persist prohibited ASC 606 policy conclusion fields.

  8. Canonical Phase 1 PaymentMethodType values bind, serialize, and validate with stable PascalCase wire names.

  9. FundedCoupon is treated as a payment tender and not an entitlement type.

  10. Deprecated GiftCard, unsupported future methods, and unknown payment methods fail validation before adapter resolution.

  11. Legacy payment-method normalization supports known historical spellings for migration/internal use without exposing public aliases.

  12. Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

  14. dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.
