issues.summary: Fulfillment Model (spec 015)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 015 (.specify/specs/015-fulfillment-model/spec.md) introduces durable item-level fulfillment tracking for the order read model. The goal is to make current item state explicit for post-purchase adjustment decisions, no-show decisions, support workflows, accounting evidence, and downstream consumers.

For Phase 1, fulfillment is a purchase/entitlement concept, not physical attendance. A tee time is fulfilled when the booking is confirmed on the third-party tee sheet and confirmation is received. Physical golfer attendance remains separate and is handled by no-show workflows.

Scope

- Add fulfillment event modeling to the order document.

- Add current item-group fulfillment state projection on the order read model.

- Preserve ItemQuantity semantics for fulfilled, pending, cancelled, and unfulfilled quantities.

- Track fulfillment source, external reference, occurrence time, recording time, and compact fulfillment evidence.

- Support Pending, Fulfilled, PartiallyFulfilled, Unfulfilled, and Cancelled item-level fulfillment states.

- Maintain top-level order fulfillment status derived from item-group state.

- Add Phase 1 immediate-capture behavior and future-compatible capture-strategy fields without enabling deferred capture.

- Feed fulfillment state into spec 014 post-purchase adjustment provider context.

- Ensure fulfilled items can be non-cancellable while still potentially refundable depending on provider policy.

- Add focused unit coverage for fulfillment event application, quantity validation, current-state projection, idempotency, and post-purchase context integration.

Out of Scope

- Domain-specific fulfillment trigger implementation for TeeTime, Subscription, Timelyst, or add-on providers.

- Deferred capture / delayed payment execution, fulfillment-triggered partial capture, authorization-window extension, and accounts-receivable recovery.

- Physical delivery or shipping tracking.

- Revenue recognition accounting rules.

- Facility-side fulfillment system integration beyond contracts/events needed by this service.

- Public fulfillment administration UI.

Acceptance Criteria

- Order model supports fulfillmentEvents[] with stable event identity, event type, item-group references, ItemQuantity fulfilled amounts, source metadata, external reference, occurrence time, recorded time, and Phase 1 capture fields.

- Order model supports current item-group fulfillment state projection with purchased, fulfilled, pending, cancelled, and unfulfilled quantities.

- Order top-level fulfillment status derives from all item-group fulfillment states.

- Fulfillment events are idempotent by stable eventId and/or domain externalReference where available.

- Event application preserves ItemQuantity.Type and rejects unit conversion/mismatched quantity types.

- Phase 1 defaults every item to immediate capture and fulfillment events do not trigger payment actions.

- Deferred capture values are treated as future-state only and cannot bypass checkout Block 5 capture.

- Unfulfilled events feed post-purchase adjustment evaluation rather than directly issuing refunds or voids in Phase 1.

- Spec 014 adjustment policy context receives per-item fulfillment state including status, fulfilled quantity, pending quantity, and relevant fulfillment timestamps/evidence.

- No-show logic can distinguish tee-time booking fulfillment from physical attendance/no-show outcomes.

- Credit memo and adjustment execution remain responsible for financial refund state; fulfillment events update operational/current purchase state only.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw for expected validation failures.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

issues.summary: Post-Purchase Adjustment Decision Engine (spec 014)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 014 (.specify/specs/014-refund-decision-engine/spec.md) introduces a centralized post-purchase adjustment decision engine. The engine consults domain-specific policy providers and produces per-item-group cancellation/refundability decisions plus a complete net-effect manifest / credit memo blueprint when financial movement is available.

This broadens the original refund-only framing: cancellation ability and refundability are separate decisions. For example, a completed tee time may no longer be operationally cancellable, but it may still be refundable through weather, goodwill, support, or other policy paths.

Scope

- Define IPostPurchaseAdjustmentDecisionEngine and the core orchestration flow.

- Define IAdjustmentPolicyProvider and provider factory contracts for per-domain policy evaluation.

- Define adjustment request, line-item adjustment, cancellation decision, refundability decision, override, policy response, net-position, tender allocation, support-action, and decision-result models.

- Load order, purchase invoice, checkout payment state, and prior credit memos before evaluation.

- Compute net refundable position from applied credit memos and purchase-time refundability snapshots.

- Validate requested quantity type, remaining refundable amount, cancellation ability, refundability, and override permissions.

- Merge provider decisions into per-item-group adjustment decisions and a credit memo blueprint including fees, warnings, overrides, tender allocation, support/manual actions, and orderRefundVersionAtCreation.

- Add focused unit coverage for cancellation/refundability separation, engine orchestration, rejection paths, fees, tender caps, fallback handling, override audit behavior, and idempotency.

Out of Scope

- Credit memo persistence and lifecycle implementation itself (spec 013).

- Fulfillment model implementation (spec 015), beyond accepting nullable fulfillment state as input to policy providers.

- Payment CREDIT execution, tax adjustment execution, inventory release execution, and operational cancellation execution.

- Customer-facing refund/cancellation request API endpoint design.

- Admin override UI.

- Concrete TeeTime, Subscription, or Timelyst policy rules beyond interface contracts and test doubles/stubs needed by this feature.

Acceptance Criteria

- IPostPurchaseAdjustmentDecisionEngine.EvaluateAsync accepts a PostPurchaseAdjustmentRequest and returns a PostPurchaseAdjustmentDecisionResult.

- IAdjustmentPolicyProvider interface is defined; IAdjustmentPolicyProviderFactory resolves by domain.

- Engine loads order, purchase invoice, checkout saga/payment state, and prior credit memos before evaluating.

- Engine calls the correct domain provider for each affected item group.

- For every affected item group, the result includes an explicit cancellation decision and refundability decision.

- Cancellation request types reject or route manual resolution when any requested item group is not automatically cancellable, without suppressing available refundability details.

- Refund-only request types may approve financial refunds for item groups that are not operationally cancellable.

- Request quantities validate ItemQuantity.Type against the purchased item, and provider contexts/credit memo blueprints preserve ItemQuantity.

- Provider responses are correctly merged into the adjustment decision and net-effect manifest.

- netRefundAmount equals gross refund credits minus total fees.

- Tender resolution distributes the net refund across tenders respecting per-tender caps and provider preferences.

- Admin overrides are permission-gated, applied, and audited.

- Original-tender-unavailable scenarios resolve through channel fallback policy or reject with REFUND_NO_VALID_TENDER when no fallback exists.

- Engine is idempotent for identical requests using the same request id on output.

- Business-rule rejection paths return ResultWrapper-compatible errors and do not throw.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

- Parent docs: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-payment-pipeline-spec-v2.md, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-entities.md

issues.summary: Credit Memo Entity (spec 013)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 013 (.specify/specs/013-credit-memo-entity/spec.md) introduces a first-class CreditMemo entity for post-purchase adjustments (refunds, fees, discretionary credits) as a typed sibling to Purchase invoices.

This fills the structural gap for item-level refund auditability and gives refund orchestration a durable financial-adjustment document.

Scope

- Add InvoiceType discriminator support (Purchase, CreditMemo) in the invoices collection model.

- Define and persist the CreditMemo shape (status lifecycle, reason metadata, signed line items, totals, allocation resolution, side-effect state).

- Add order-level refund tracking state (creditMemoIds, totalRefunded, refundableRemaining, orderRefundVersion, itemPurchaseState).

- Add stale-credit-memo concurrency protection using orderRefundVersionAtCreation and execution-time version checks.

- Define Abstractions wire contracts/enums for CreditMemoResponse and related types.

- Preserve existing required order indexes per entities spec.

- Add/adjust tests for model, mapping, totals, lifecycle transitions, and stale-state handling.

Out of Scope

- Refund decisioning policy logic itself (spec 014).

- Fulfillment model implementation (spec 015).

- Customer-facing rendering/PDF/email of credit memos.

- Non-essential accounting integration workflows beyond credit memo persistence/shape.

Acceptance Criteria

- InvoiceType supports Purchase and CreditMemo with backward-compatible handling for legacy purchase rows.

- Credit memo document shape and status lifecycle are implemented and validated.

- Credit memo signed totals and netRefundAmount are computed per spec.

- Order-level refund tracking fields are maintained correctly.

- Stale credit memo detection rejects execution when order refund version has advanced.

- Abstractions wire contract for CreditMemoResponse and supporting enums/types is in place.

- Existing required order indexes are preserved.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

issues.summary: Invoice Property Relocation (spec 012)
issues.description:
Context

Spec 012 (.specify/specs/012-invoice-property-relocation/spec.md) realigns the Order Processing invoice model after requirements review found several properties on the wrong entity level.

The implementation starts from branch docs/invoice_enhancements and should follow the existing Spec-Kit workflow before code changes.

Scope

- Move PricingTier and PricingTierSavings from item components up to invoice items.

- Move MerchantId from invoice items down to item components.

- Replace loose item quantity fields with a required ItemQuantity value object (Value + QuantityType).

- Introduce PaymentLocationAmount for DueOnline and DueAtFacility at component, item, and invoice totals levels.

- Add purchase-time RefundabilitySnapshot metadata on item components and expose the customer-facing refundability projection.

- Update domain models, wire contracts, converters, pricing provider contracts/stubs, invoice builder merchant derivation, totals calculation, and tests.

Out of Scope

- Retrofitting spec 005; spec 012 owns this post-F3 alignment.

- Payment pipeline implementation beyond wire/spec alignment.

- Saga implementation for checkout.

- DueOnlineLater or additional payment-location categories.

- MongoDB migration unless persisted pre-GA invoices exist in the target environment.

Acceptance Criteria

- Item has item-level PricingTier, PricingTierSavings, and required ItemQuantity; it no longer has item-level MerchantId.

- ItemComponent has component-level MerchantId, PaymentLocationAmount-typed DueOnline/DueAtFacility, and RefundabilitySnapshot.

- InvoiceResponse exposes the corrected item/component placement, PaymentLocationAmountResponse, refundability response, and invoice Totals.

- InvoiceBuilder.DeriveMerchantIds() derives the top-level merchant list from all item components with case-insensitive de-duplication.

- Pricing provider contracts and the in-memory pricing provider return item-level tier/quantity values and component-level merchant/refundability values.

- Totals follow spec 012: TotalDue = DueOnline.Amount + DueOnline.SalesTax; TotalTax = DueOnline.SalesTax + DueAtFacility.SalesTax.

- Unit/integration tests are updated for the new shape and all existing tests pass.

- dotnet build GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release succeeds.

- dotnet test GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx --configuration Release passes.

References

- Example ticket shape: CORE-14439

- Spec: .specify/specs/012-invoice-property-relocation/spec.md

- Parent docs branch: docs/invoice_enhancements

issues.summary: Tax control plane on gn-svc-platform — TaxProvider + TaxProviderProfile (spec authoring)
issues.description:
Context

CORE-14443 introduces a production ITaxProvider abstraction in gn-api-orderprocessing (Vertex Phase 1, Avalara + SensibleWeather to follow). Every provider call needs a stored configuration — endpoint, credentials, currencies, remit responsibility — and that configuration must live on gn-svc-platform, paralleling the existing payment-processor control plane.

This ticket covers the platform-side work: new TaxProvider and TaxProviderProfile entities with full CRUD + CSFLE-encrypted credentials + admin HTTP surface + seed task. Without this landed, CORE-14443 has nowhere to load Vertex credentials from at call time, so this ticket is a hard upstream of CORE-14443's Phase 1.

Scope reduction — seed task removed

Commit 64b144d on feature/CORE-14445-0.

issues.description:
Context

Replaces the current StubEstimatingTaxProvider with a production-shaped tax abstraction. Unblocks F5 (Invoice Finalization), F9–F10 (Checkout Block 6 CommitTax), and F18–F20 (post-purchase tax adjustments). See plan at ~/.claude/plans/what-s-next-to-work-reactive-panda.md.

Scope — F6 Tax Provider Abstraction

- Substrate-neutral ITaxProvider covering the four tax phases from pipeline §9: estimate, finalize, commit, reversal (void / credit).

- Tax rate store with soft-TTL read semantics; Mongo-backed Phase 1 behind a substrate-neutral abstraction (DynamoDB swap deferred).

- Vertex Phase-1 adapter as the only concrete provider.

- EstimatedFallback behaviour on provider outage when rate store has a (stale) entry. Cold-store + unreachable = hard failure.

Scope — F7 Tax Provider Response Archival

- Per-operation archival of raw provider request/response pairs to durable object storage, out-of-band from the hot path.

- Retention + lifecycle aligned with 7y business retention.

- PCI/PII redaction before archival.

- F9–F10 Checkout saga Block 6.

- F18/F19/F20 post-purchase sagas.

- F26 Saga Execution Safety (pairs with first real saga, not tax).

- DynamoDB adapter for ITaxRateStore.

- Avalara + SensibleWeather adapters.

- gn-svc-platform changes.

- Admin manual tax seed endpoint.

- Tax error-code domain — 40K cross-cutting per pipeline §14.2, or carve a new 60K tax domain?

- S3 bucket + IAM provisioning ownership — gn-iac, Aspire resource, or service-startup bootstrapper?

issues.summary: Add Rate Set Fee Support to New Transaction Fee Retrieval Stored Procedure
issues.description:
As part of the Customizable Transaction Fees initiative, the first ticket introduced a parallel transaction fee retrieval path by creating a new stored procedure that retrieves fees outside of the Tee Time Search stored procedure.

The current implementation supports retrieving transaction fees by:

- FacilityID

- OwnerID (existing behavior)

However, the roadmap requires rate set–level fee overrides, which are currently impossible with the legacy stored procedure.

This ticket introduces the ability for the new transaction fee stored procedure to retrieve fees by GolfCourseID, enabling the first step toward full fee customization.

The legacy stored procedure remains unchanged.

---
Goal

Extend the new transaction fee stored procedure to support retrieving fees by GolfCourseID, allowing the system to apply the proper fee hierarchy:

- Rate Set level (highest priority)

- Facility level

- Owner level (default baseline)

The API will continue using the toggle introduced in Ticket #1.

---
Scope

Enhance the new transaction fee stored procedure so that it can:

- Accept GolfCourseID as an optional parameter

issues.summary: LaunchDarkly Request Context Builder (spec 010)
issues.description:
Context

Every LaunchDarkly flag evaluation in gn-api-orderprocessing today goes through a single static context — Context.New("service:order-processing") hardcoded in LaunchDarklyInvoiceTtlResolver. No channel targeting, no customer targeting, no regional targeting. A "5% rollout" against that one service key is all-or-nothing in practice.

CORE-14438 (in-flight) introduces ILaunchDarklyContextFactory with a single-kind service context that adds a region custom attribute. Spec 010 extends that factory — it does not replace it — by adding a request-scoped multi-context with three kinds (channel, customer, service) so flag rules can target (channel, customer, region, saga-role) tuples.

Three context kinds

- channel — key = channelId from the route (32-bit signed integer, base-10 string-encoded). Attributes extensible; none required initially.

- customer — key = customerId (UUIDv7, canonical lowercase string). Attributes: country, isGuest, authenticationMethod. Omitted when ICustomerIdentityAccessor.Current == null.

- service — key = service:order-processing (preserves CORE-14438 compatibility). Attributes: region (from CORE-14438) + new isSagaActiveRegion derived from the lease store.

Locked design decisions

- Saga-region source — consume ILeadershipLeaseStore + RegionalSagaOptions.CurrentRegion directly from CORE-14438. Blocked by CORE-14438 merging to develop.

- ChannelId source — route only. Migrate InvoicesController endpoints from /api/v1/invoicing/invoices to /api/v1/invoicing/channels/{channelId:int}/invoices. Remove ChannelId from CreateInvoiceRequest wire body; re-attach as typed int on CreateInvoiceCommand.

- ChannelId type correction — the canonical ChannelId in GolfNow's domain is a 32-bit integer. CreateInvoiceRequest.ChannelId and InvoiceResponse.ChannelId on develop are currently typed Guid; spec 010 corrects both to int.

- Country seam — extend CORE-14421's CustomerIdentity record with string Country = "US". HttpContextCustomerIdentityAccessor hardcodes US until Profile Service emits a country claim. No separate resolver abstraction.

- Anonymous behavior — omit the customer kind from the multi-context when ICustomerIdentityAccessor.Current == null. Channel + service always present.

Scope

In scope:

- Extend ILaunchDarklyContextFactory with CreateRequestContext() returning a multi-context.

- New IRequestLdContextScope (scoped) caching the built Context per request.

- Three per-kind builders (ChannelContextKindBuilder, CustomerContextKindBuilder, ServiceContextKindBuilder).

- isSagaActiveRegion attribute on the service kind, derived from CurrentRegion == LeadershipLease.HolderRegion with fail-closed semantics on lease-read failure.

- Migration of LaunchDarklyInvoiceTtlResolver to consume IRequestLdContextScope (proof the seam works end-to-end).

- Route refactor for InvoicesController (POST + GET) — /channels/{channelId:int}/... prefix. [FromRoute] int channelId on both actions.

- Retype CreateInvoiceRequest.ChannelId (removed from wire body) and InvoiceResponse.ChannelId (stays on response body) from Guid to int.

- CustomerIdentity record extension with string Country = "US" + WebApi accessor hardcode.

- Unit + integration test coverage (Integration trait for end-to-end route + captured-context assertions).

Out of scope:

- Profile Service integration for real customer country (seam present, follow-up ticket).

- Channel attributes beyond channelId.

- New feature flags (infrastructure only; existing flags adopt the context automatically).

- Mediator pipeline-level ambient-context injection.

- Saga-originated flag evaluation (no HttpContext; handled by future alternate scope).

Dependencies

- Blocked by CORE-14438 (spec 008 regional saga control plane). ILaunchDarklyContextFactory, RegionalSagaOptions, and ILeadershipLeaseStore must exist on develop before implementation starts. This ticket currently delivers groundwork only — spec.md + this ticket + worktree; no code changes until the block clears.

- Speckit flow (/speckit skill) will generate plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, quickstart.md, contracts/*, and tasks.md in a follow-up pass.

Constitution alignment

- Principle VIII — ILeadershipLeaseStore and LD abstractions stay in Core; driver code stays in Repository.Mongo.

- Principle IX — lease-read failure logs a Warning and returns isSagaActiveRegion = false (fail closed); does not throw.

- Principle XII — wire contract isolation: ChannelId removed from CreateInvoiceRequest wire body; moves to a typed int ChannelId parameter on CreateInvoiceCommand.

Spec location

.specify/specs/010-launchdarkly-request-context-builder/spec.md on branch features/CORE-14439-01 (branched from develop, committed at 61de486, pushed to origin). Worktree: ~/source/worktrees/gn-api-orderprocessing/features-CORE-14439-01. See the spec file for the full Data Types dictionary (ChannelId, CustomerId, InvoiceId, VersionKey, Country, AwsRegion, IsSagaActiveRegion, and all LD kind keys + attributes).

Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — Authenticated request with channelId (integer) on the route produces a multi-context containing all three kinds with expected attrs.

- AC2 — Anonymous request with channelId on the route produces a multi-context with channel + service only (customer omitted).

- AC3 — isSagaActiveRegion flips based on RegionalSagaOptions.CurrentRegion == LeadershipLease.HolderRegion.

- AC4 — A lease-read failure returns isSagaActiveRegion = false, logs a Warning, and the request still completes.

- AC5 — LaunchDarklyInvoiceTtlResolver evaluates invoice-ttl and invoice-pricing-ttl against the new multi-context with existing fallback behavior preserved.

- AC6 — Kiota-generated OrderProcessingApiClient reflects the new /channels/{channelId:int}/invoices route shape on build; the regenerated ChannelId on both CreateInvoiceRequest (removed) and InvoiceResponse (int) builds green for consumers.

issues.summary: Regional Saga Control Plane — spec 008 readiness review + impl
issues.description:
Scope

Pre-implementation readiness review of Speckit feature 008 (Regional Saga Control Plane), plus the implementation PRs that follow once the review clears. Phase 0 in this ticket is read-only against docs/* — harmonization gaps get classified and filed, not fixed in this PR.

Phase 0 deliverables (this PR)

#

Work

Deliverable

1

Relocate untracked files onto ticket branch

.specify/specs/008-regional-saga-control-plane/, .specify/specs/009-saga-execution-safety/, docs/gn-api-orderprocessing_regional-saga-spec.md

2

Mechanical heading renumber inside 008 package

# 003 — → # 008 — in spec.md, plan.md, research.md, tasks.md

3

Spec-package integrity audit

No placeholders; 7 ACs trace to tasks; phases 1a–1e fully covered; constitution refs live

4

Cross-spec consistency check

F1/F2 dependencies landed; F#### internal refs reconciled against folder numbers; duplicate 006- prefix logged

5

Harmonization memo vs docs/*

Per-doc section citing regional content, flagging conflicts/gaps, classifying MUST/SHOULD/NICE

Background

Spec 008 delivers the multi-region coordination machinery for leader-scoped saga execution (MongoDB-backed global leadership lease, regional monitor, SNS→SQS router, endpoint lifecycle, LaunchDarkly override, observability) plus single-region mode used by dev/stg. It is independently shippable — no concrete saga is required. Spec 009 (saga-execution-safety) picks up the per-saga execution lease, step deadlines, watchdog, and recovery — explicitly deferred by 008.

The spec package already contains spec.md, plan.md, research.md, and tasks.md — it is past planning and sitting at the gate between planning and implementation. Phase 0 verifies the package is coherent and the parent docs in docs/* don't silently contradict the regional model before 3–4 engineer-weeks commit to building it.

Implementation phases (follow-up PRs under this Story)

Per .specify/specs/008-regional-saga-control-plane/plan.md:

- Phase 1a — Leadership lease substrate (ILeadershipLeaseStore, LeadershipLeaseRepository, leadership_lease collection, TTL index).

- Phase 1b — Regional monitor + eligibility resolution (topology subscription, debounce, preference-list fallback).

- Phase 1c — Message router + SNS/SQS topology (ingress SNS, per-region SQS + DLQ, router hosted service, single-region pass-through).

- Phase 1d — Endpoint lifecycle + LaunchDarkly override (start/stop bound to lease, region pin, dead-man timeout).

- Phase 1e — Observability + rollout (OTel metrics/traces, Datadog dashboard + alerts, single-region in dev/stg, prod multi-region deactivation-default).

Expected effort: 3–4 engineer-weeks after Phase 0 closes clean.

Branch + worktree

- Cut from: develop HEAD.

- Worktree: $WORKTREE_BASE/gn-api-orderprocessing/features-CORE-XXXXX-01 (this ticket's key substituted).

- Work folder: $JIRA_DOCS/CORE-XXXXX/.

Acceptance

- Phase 0 memo at $JIRA_DOCS/CORE-XXXXX/readiness-review.md covers all four sections (package integrity, cross-spec consistency, per-doc harmonization, disposition).

- Every harmonization finding is classified MUST / SHOULD / NICE with a recommended action and a follow-up ticket candidate.

- Heading renumber committed: grep -n "^# 003" .specify/specs/008-*/*.md returns zero matches; grep -n "^# 008" returns four.

- No modifications to the existing five docs/*.md files — only the new gn-api-orderprocessing_regional-saga-spec.md is added.

- Implementation decision recorded: either "ready to proceed — opening sub-tasks for phases 1a–1e" or "gated on follow-up tickets X/Y/Z".

Dependencies

- Depends on: F1 / CORE-14041 (Order Processing API Setup — persistence foundations), F2 / CORE-14406 (MassTransit Infrastructure & Saga Persistence). Both in Development; spec 008 treats them as landed.

- Related: spec 009 (saga-execution-safety) — paired with the first concrete saga, separate ticket.

- Unblocks: any future leader-scoped saga (checkout, cancellation, refund, no-show) once 008 + 009 are both in place.

Out of scope

- Spec 009 (saga-execution-safety) — separate ticket.

- Any concrete saga implementation.

- Inbound webhook routing (separate spec).

- Edits to existing docs/*.md — the harmonization memo recommends fixes, parallel tickets implement them.

References

- Authoritative parent doc: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing_regional-saga-spec.md

- Speckit package: .specify/specs/008-regional-saga-control-plane/

- Plan file (local): ~/.claude/plans/i-want-to-create-recursive-hejlsberg.md

- Sibling tickets under same epic: CORE-14406 (F2), CORE-14411 (F23), CORE-14418 (F3), CORE-14419/-14421 (customer auth).

- Constitution principles cited by spec 008: IV, VIII, IX, XI, XII.

issues.summary: Add a Member Pricing identifier in GNC Reservation Details
issues.description:
We would like to add a Member Pricing identifier to Reservation Details so there is a clear reason why the booking was charged less than the associated hot deal and also improve support.

Logic:

- Display two new boxes:

- Is Member Pricing?

- True/False

- True = ReservationMetadataTypeId 75 = Member

- False = ID 75 is not Member or does not exist

issues.summary: Migrate idempotency + customer-auth caches from Redis to Valkey
issues.description:
Context

gn-api-orderprocessing currently uses AWS ElastiCache for Redis 7.x as the substrate for two concerns:

- Idempotency response cache (FR-016 / entities spec §14) — landed under CORE-14041 (F1).

- Customer-auth token validation cache (CORE-14419) — landed this sprint in GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Authentication.Customer/Caching/RedisCustomerTokenCache.cs.

After Redis Inc. relicensed under SSPL/RSAL in March 2024, AWS launched ElastiCache for Valkey (the Linux-Foundation OSS fork) in October 2024. Valkey is wire-compatible with Redis (RESP protocol preserved), so StackExchange.Redis continues to work unchanged — but the platform, naming, and configuration references across our code and docs need to be migrated so we're operating on the OSS track going forward.

This story is the application-side switch. The infrastructure provisioning (ElastiCache Valkey cluster) is tracked in CORE-14405 (rescoped from Redis → Valkey).

Scope

In-scope

- Client wiring & configuration

- src/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Repository.Redis/ — rename project to Repository.Valkey (folder, .csproj, namespaces, DI extension methods AddOrderProcessingRedis* → AddOrderProcessingValkey*).

- RedisConnectionFactory, RedisKeyBuilder, RedisCustomerTokenCache (CORE-14419) → rename to Valkey* equivalents; keep StackExchange.Redis as the client library (still the AWS-recommended Valkey client).

- Config key rename: ConnectionStrings:Redis → ConnectionStrings:Valkey; RedisOptions → ValkeyOptions.

- appsettings*.json / Octopus variable placeholders: #{Redis.ConnectionString} → #{Valkey.ConnectionString}.

- Documentation

- CLAUDE.md project section — replace Redis references (Persistence Conventions, Dependencies, ElastiCache sidebar).

- docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md + docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-entities.md §14 — rewrite the Redis chapter to Valkey.

- .specify/memory/constitution.md Principle VIII and related sections.

- Auto-memory entries (feedback_idempotency_is_redis.md, repository-split entry) refreshed after ticket lands.

- Tests

- tests/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Repository.Redis.Tests/ → rename + update.

- Testcontainers-managed integration tests: swap the redis:7 image for valkey/valkey:8 (or equivalent AWS-aligned tag).

- CI / deploy

- Octopus variable set rename; no new environment provisioning (that's CORE-14405).

Out-of-scope

- Provisioning the Valkey cluster itself — CORE-14405.

- Changing the cache semantics (TTL, key pattern, fail-closed behavior, SET NX EX atomic first-write) — only the engine identity changes.

- Replacing StackExchange.Redis with a different client library — remains the canonical choice for Valkey per AWS guidance.

Acceptance criteria

- All production .cs, .csproj, .slnx, .json, and .yml files reference Valkey, not Redis, for the idempotency + customer-auth caches.

- Repository.Redis project renamed to Repository.Valkey with folders, namespaces, and DI registrations updated.

- CLAUDE.md, docs/*.md, .specify/memory/constitution.md updated; no stale Redis references outside historical commit messages and archived speckit documents.

- Existing idempotency + customer-auth integration tests pass against a Valkey container image.

- Connection-string config key renamed end-to-end (appsettings, Octopus, Secrets Manager references).

- All PR checks green; LogTemplateAllowlistTests unaffected (no new log template tokens introduced).

Dependencies

- Blocked by: CORE-14405 (ElastiCache Valkey provisioning — rescoped from Redis).

- Related: CORE-14041 (F1 persistence foundations), CORE-14419 (customer-auth cache introduced the second Redis touchpoint).

Notes

- StackExchange.Redis ≥ 2.8.x is the AWS-documented client for ElastiCache for Valkey — no library swap required.

- Valkey preserves the RESP2/RESP3 protocol, SET NX EX, EXPIRE, and AUTH semantics we rely on, so no behavioral changes are expected.

- Naming rename is load-bearing for future reviewers: "Repository.Redis" holding a Valkey client would be a trap.

issues.summary: Customer-auth integration wave: F3 endpoint wiring + speckit backfill + mediator identity context
issues.description:
Scope

Consolidation wave following CORE-14419 (customer-auth infrastructure). Four deliverables under one branch, stacked sequentially. No new user-facing feature.

Four-step plan

#

Work

Deliverable

1

Backfill speckit spec for CORE-14419 as-shipped

.specify/specs/006-customer-authentication/ (spec, plan, tasks, research, quickstart, contracts/)

2

Harden customer-auth Redis cache with Polly resilience (circuit breaker + tight timeout)

RedisCustomerTokenCache wrapped in named ResiliencePipeline; new contracts/redis-resilience.md; 5 new configurable options

3

Design + ship standard mechanism for customer-identity propagation into mediator commands/queries

.specify/specs/007-customer-identity-integration/ + Core abstraction seam + Core pipeline behavior + WebApi adapter

4

Decorate F3 invoice endpoints with [CustomerAuthentication(Required)] + ownership check on GET

InvoicesController changes + handler refactor to consume identity context

Background

CORE-14419 shipped dual-auth infrastructure (X-GolfId-Token / X-Customer-Token validator, handler, middlewares, Redis cache, DI wiring) in 5 commits on features/CORE-14419-01. The ticket description punted two follow-ups: "Rolling out the attribute to existing controllers — follow-up tickets after infrastructure merges."

Four gaps remain to close before F4 Invoice Modification:

- Documentation. CORE-14419 bypassed the speckit workflow — no 006-* folder exists. The as-shipped contract (dual-header mutual exclusion, Profile Service validator shape, cache TTL semantics, claim types, error codes) lives only in code + tests.

- Cache resilience. RedisCustomerTokenCache calls IConnectionMultiplexer directly with the 5s multiplexer default timeout and no circuit breaker. Auth path is latency-sensitive; a hung Redis hammers every customer-scoped request. Fail-open handling exists but isn't fail-fast.

- Integration. The [CustomerAuthentication] attribute is NOT decorating any endpoint. InvoicesController carries only [Authorize] (PlatformPrincipal).

- Identity propagation. CreateInvoiceCommand reads customerId from the request body — anyone can claim any identity. No ICurrentCustomer / ICustomerIdentityAccessor exists anywhere in Core. IdempotencyMiddleware reads the claim directly off HttpContext.User, which is too coupled to the web layer for handlers to reuse.

Design — Redis cache resilience (Step 2)

Polly v8 ResiliencePipeline named "CustomerAuth.Cache" wraps every RedisCustomerTokenCache operation.

- Timeout strategy — per-call budget, default 150ms (configurable via Auth:CustomerAuthentication:CacheOperationTimeoutMs).

- Circuit breaker strategy — default 20% failure ratio over a 30s rolling window, min 10 calls, 10s break duration, 1 probe in half-open. All configurable: CacheBreakerFailureRatio, CacheBreakerSamplingWindowSeconds, CacheBreakerMinimumThroughput, CacheBreakerBreakDurationSeconds.

- No retry — cache is an optimization; a failed cache read falls straight through to the validator (which has its own retry policy via AddStandardResilienceHandler). Retries here would extend latency with no correctness benefit.

- Fail-open preserved — pipeline exceptions (TimeoutRejectedException, BrokenCircuitException) surface to the existing catch-all in TryGetAsync/SetAsync, which treats them as cache miss. No call-site changes elsewhere.

- Observability — new counters customer_auth.cache.timeouts and customer_auth.cache.breaker_state{state=open|half-open|closed} on CustomerAuthDiagnostics.

Design — Mediator customer-identity propagation (Step 3)

Explicit over ambient. Follows GNC's LoginCommand(LoginRequest, string IpAddress) pattern — additional request-context metadata is a command constructor parameter, not hidden scope state. Testability wins over implicit ambient access.

- New CustomerIdentity record (Core): (Guid CustomerId, string? CustomerNumber, string? Email, bool IsGuest, CustomerTokenType Source).

- New ICustomerIdentityAccessor (Core) with Current (nullable) and GetRequired() (throws — contract violation per Principle IX when authz should have blocked).

- HttpContextCustomerIdentityAccessor (WebApi) reads CustomerClaimTypes.CustomerId/… from HttpContext.User; derives Source from the authenticationMethod claim.

- ICustomerScopedRequest marker interface on commands/queries that require customer context.

- CustomerIdentityBehavior<TRequest,TResponse> pipeline behavior (after ValidationBehavior, before LoggingBehavior) returns ResultWrapper.Forbidden with messageType=CUSTOMER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED for scoped requests with no identity — belt-and-suspenders against future non-HTTP dispatchers.

- Commands gain CustomerIdentity Customer as an explicit ctor param; controller populates from the accessor before mediator.Send(...).

Design — F3 endpoint wiring (Step 4)

- POST /api/v1/invoicing/invoices → [CustomerAuthentication(Mode = Required)]. Authenticated claim overrides any customerId in the wire DTO (which is removed from CreateInvoiceRequest entirely).

- GET /api/v1/invoicing/invoices/{id} → [CustomerAuthentication(Mode = Required)] with ownership check. Handler compares stored invoice.customerId == claim.CustomerId; mismatch → 403 with new INVOICE_ACCESS_DENIED = 10403 error code.

- CreateInvoiceRequest.CustomerId removed (breaking change to Kiota client — safe because no consumer callers exist yet).

Branch + worktree

- Cut from: features/CORE-14419-01 HEAD (bf834b5), not develop.

- Worktree: $WORKTREE_BASE/gn-api-orderprocessing/features-CORE-14421-01.

- Rebase onto develop after CORE-14419 PR merges.

- Work folder: $JIRA_DOCS/CORE-14421/.

Sequence

One PR with four stacked commits:

- docs(speckit): backfill 006-customer-authentication spec for CORE-14419 (CORE-14421)

- feat(security): Polly circuit breaker + tight timeout on customer-auth Redis cache (CORE-14421)

- feat(security): ICustomerIdentityAccessor + CustomerIdentityBehavior for mediator customer-scoped handlers (CORE-14421)

- feat(invoicing): [CustomerAuthentication(Required)] on F3 endpoints + ownership check on GET (CORE-14421)

Acceptance

- Step 1: .specify/specs/006-customer-authentication/ exists with spec.md, plan.md, research.md, tasks.md, quickstart.md, and contracts/ (dual-header-mutual-exclusion, profile-service-validator, customer-claim-types, redis-cache-key-format, error-codes-customer-auth).

- Step 2: RedisCustomerTokenCache wraps Redis calls in the named CustomerAuth.Cache pipeline; timeout fires at 150ms; circuit breaker trips after 20% failures over 30s; customer_auth.cache.timeouts counter increments under a slow Redis; fail-open passthrough still returns null from TryGetAsync (validator still called). New contracts/redis-resilience.md documents the contract.

- Step 3: ICustomerIdentityAccessor + HttpContextCustomerIdentityAccessor + ICustomerScopedRequest + CustomerIdentityBehavior landed; unit tests cover missing-identity (Forbidden) and spoofed-identity (body-trumped-by-claim) paths; behavior-registration-order test asserts CustomerIdentityBehavior runs after ValidationBehavior, before LoggingBehavior.

- Step 4: POST /api/v1/invoicing/invoices without a customer token → 401 CUSTOMER_TOKEN_REQUIRED. GET /api/v1/invoicing/invoices/{id} with a mismatched customer claim → 403 INVOICE_ACCESS_DENIED. CreateInvoiceCommand no longer reads customerId from request body — authoritative value comes from the claim. IdempotencyMiddleware continues to scope keys per customer (no regression).

- Kiota regenerates with CreateInvoiceRequest no longer carrying CustomerId.

- Full-settings test profile passes (Testcontainers Mongo + Redis + Authentication.Customer integration scenarios).

Dependencies

- Depends on: CORE-14419 (infrastructure — branch-stacked; rebases onto develop after CORE-14419 merges).

- Related: CORE-14418 (F3 endpoints being decorated), CORE-14411 (F23 PCI observability — log property allowlist may need CustomerIdentity-derived fields).

- Unblocks: F4 Invoice Modification (PUT/reprice) — identity propagation must be idiomatic before that ships.

Out of scope

- Rolling the attribute onto non-invoice endpoints (none yet warrant it).

- Publishing Authentication.Customer as a NuGet package (separate ticket).

- F4 Invoice Modification.

- Replacing the PlatformPrincipal scheme.

- Extending the resilience pattern to the idempotency Redis cache — separate concern, separate ticket.

Open questions (resolve during implementation)

- ChannelId — body field or header? CORE-14419 doesn't define a channel claim. Default: keep on body with allowlist validation; revisit if F4/F5 review disagrees.

- CustomerIdentityBehavior.Forbidden — 401 or 403? Default 403 (request reached the handler, something claimed auth); revisit if real flows show 401 is warranted.

References

- Plan file (local): ~/.claude/plans/using-this-worktree-as-peaceful-peach.md

- Predecessor tickets under same epic: CORE-14418 (F3), CORE-14419 (customer-auth infrastructure).

- Constitution: Principle IX (Exceptions for Exceptional Only), Principle XI (In-Process CQRS Dispatch via Source-Generated Mediator), Principle XII (Wire Contract Isolation).

- CLAUDE.md: GNC LoginCommand(LoginRequest, string IpAddress) pattern precedent.

Step 5 added — missing customer email is a failure case

Mid-wave scope addition (spec review of 006 surfaced the gap). Commit e5cca18.

Contract change: Profile Service returning a valid token but a customer record with null/empty/whitespace email now fails authentication with 401 CUSTOMER_DATA_INCOMPLETE (new error code 40439) instead of silently omitting the email claim as CORE-14419 originally shipped.

- CustomerAuthenticationFailureReason.CustomerDataIncomplete = 5

- CustomerTokenValidationOutcome.CustomerDataIncomplete = 3

issues.summary: Customer Authentication — Dual-Auth Handler for gn-api-orderprocessing
issues.description:
Customer Authentication — Dual-Auth Handler for gn-api-orderprocessing

Context

gn-api-orderprocessing currently authenticates callers with PlatformPrincipal (service-to-service). For customer-scoped endpoints, we also need to authenticate the end-user's customer token. The request must present both: a valid PlatformPrincipal and a valid customer token — in either X-GolfId-Token or X-Customer-Token (but never both).

The existing CustomerTokenAuthenticationHandler / RequiresCustomerTokenAttribute in WebApi/Authentication/ are placeholders that don't validate anything. A primitive implementation exists in gn-lib-core (Golf.Authentication.AspNetCore/Customer/CustomerAuthenticationHandler.cs) but it lacks mutual-exclusion at the request level, dual-auth composition, attribute-based opt-in, and caching. The authoritative token-validation logic lives in golfnow-internal-authentication-client (GolfNow.Auth.Client.CustomerAuthenticationClient), which calls Profile Service at GET /api/authentication?token={t}&tokenType={1|2} (1 = legacy CustomerToken, 2 = GolfIdToken).

We want a proper replacement for the placeholder, built as its own project inside the gn-api-orderprocessing solution so it can be extracted to a shared library later.

Setup

- Create new worktree forked off features-CORE-14418-01:

cd ~/source/repos/GolfNowEng/gn-api-orderprocessing
git worktree add ~/source/worktrees/gn-api-orderprocessing/feature-<THIS-TICKET>-01 -b feature/<THIS-TICKET>-01 features/CORE-14418-01

- Work folder at ~/OneDrive - VERSANT/Working Folder/_docs/jira/<THIS-TICKET>/.

New project

src/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Authentication.Customer/ — added to GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx.

Dependencies only (extractability — no refs to Core or WebApi):

- Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication

- Microsoft.Extensions.Http + Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience (Polly)

- Microsoft.Extensions.Options, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions, Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Abstractions

- StackExchange.Redis (consumed via injected IConnectionMultiplexer, not self-initialized)

- System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource (for OTel ActivitySource / Meter)

Central Package Management — add entries in Directory.Packages.props; project file uses <PackageReference Include="..." /> with no version.

Public surface

GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Authentication.Customer/
├─ CustomerAuthenticationAttribute.cs       // [CustomerAuthentication(Required|Optional, Cache=Disabled|Enabled)]
├─ CustomerAuthenticationMode.cs            // Required, Optional
├─ CustomerAuthenticationCache.cs           // Disabled, Enabled
├─ CustomerAuthenticationOptions.cs         // Profile Service URL, default TTLs, header names, scheme name
├─ CustomerClaimTypes.cs                    // public const strings: CustomerId, CustomerNumber, Email, IsGuest, PrincipalType, AuthenticationMethod, AuthenticationToken
├─ CustomerAuthenticationDefaults.cs        // Scheme name = "CustomerToken", header constants
├─ DependencyInjection/
│   └─ CustomerAuthenticationServiceCollectionExtensions.cs
│       // AddCustomerAuthentication(IConfiguration section) — wires handler, validator, cache, authz requirement
├─ Ttl/
│   ├─ ICustomerAuthTtlProvider.cs          // GetSuccessTtl(), GetFailureTtl() — LD-compatible seam
│   └─ OptionsCustomerAuthTtlProvider.cs    // default impl reads IOptionsMonitor<CustomerAuthenticationOptions>
├─ Validation/
│   ├─ ICustomerTokenValidator.cs
│   ├─ CustomerTokenValidationResult.cs     // Outcome (Success|InvalidToken|ServiceError), Customer data, failure reason
│   ├─ CustomerTokenType.cs                 // GolfIdToken = 2, CustomerToken = 1
│   └─ ProfileServiceCustomerTokenValidator.cs  // uses IHttpClientFactory + Polly
├─ Caching/
│   ├─ ICustomerTokenCache.cs
│   ├─ RedisCustomerTokenCache.cs           // IConnectionMultiplexer, SHA256 token hash
│   └─ NullCustomerTokenCache.cs
├─ Handler/
│   ├─ CustomerAuthenticationHandler.cs     // AuthenticationHandler<CustomerAuthenticationOptions>
│   └─ BothHeadersRejectionMiddleware.cs    // 400 with envelope when both X-GolfId-Token and X-Customer-Token are present
├─ Authorization/
│   ├─ CustomerAuthenticationRequirement.cs
│   └─ CustomerAuthenticationAuthorizationHandler.cs
├─ Response/
│   └─ ICustomerAuthenticationResponseWriter.cs  // host writes envelope; default = problem+json
└─ Observability/
└─ CustomerAuthDiagnostics.cs           // ActivitySource + Meter (counters for success/failure/cache-hit/cache-miss)

Runtime flow

- Middleware — BothHeadersRejectionMiddleware runs before UseAuthentication. If both headers are present on the request, short-circuit with 400 via ICustomerAuthenticationResponseWriter.

- Authentication pipeline — PlatformPrincipal stays the default scheme and runs as-is via AuthenticationMiddleware. "CustomerToken" is registered as an additional scheme but is not default; it's only invoked on demand.

- Endpoint authorization — Endpoints marked [Authorize] continue to require PlatformPrincipal. Endpoints additionally marked [CustomerAuthentication] trigger CustomerAuthenticationRequirement.

- Authz handler —

- Look up [CustomerAuthentication] on httpContext.GetEndpoint()?.Metadata. None → context.Succeed(requirement) and return.

- Call await httpContext.AuthenticateAsync("CustomerToken").

- The CustomerAuthenticationHandler does the work: reads whichever of the two headers is present, checks cache (if attribute's Cache == Enabled), calls validator on miss, caches result, returns AuthenticateResult.Success(...) or Fail(...).

- Compose on the auth result:

- Succeeded → merge the customer ClaimsIdentity into httpContext.User via AddIdentity, call context.Succeed(requirement).

- Failed → always context.Fail() (even in Optional mode — invalid token is explicit).

- None (no headers) → Optional ⇒ Succeed, Required ⇒ Fail.

- Failure response — Fail() propagates up; HandleChallengeAsync writes the GN response envelope via ICustomerAuthenticationResponseWriter with codes like CUSTOMER_TOKEN_REQUIRED / CUSTOMER_TOKEN_INVALID.

- Idempotency — Introduce a lightweight CustomerIdentityInjectionMiddleware between UseAuthentication and UseIdempotency that runs the CustomerToken scheme when the endpoint has [CustomerAuthentication], merges the identity into HttpContext.User, and caches the AuthenticateResult in HttpContext.Features so the authz handler doesn't revalidate. Keeps idempotency keys customer-scoped.

Modern patterns

- IHttpClientFactory — ProfileServiceCustomerTokenValidator receives its HttpClient from a typed client: services.AddHttpClient<ICustomerTokenValidator, ProfileServiceCustomerTokenValidator>().AddStandardResilienceHandler() (Polly via Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience).

- ILogger<T> — every component. Validator logs Debug for success, Warning for invalid tokens, Error for Profile Service failures (correlation id, not raw token).

- OpenTelemetry — CustomerAuthDiagnostics exposes:

- ActivitySource("GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Authentication.Customer") with spans around validator HTTP calls and cache lookups

- Meter counters: customer_auth.attempts (tags: result, token_type, cache), customer_auth.cache_hits, customer_auth.cache_misses, customer_auth.validation_duration

- No hard dep on OTel packages — just System.Diagnostics primitives; host registers them with its existing OTel pipeline.

Configurable TTLs (LaunchDarkly seam, no hard LD dep)

CustomerAuthenticationOptions section in appsettings.json under Auth:CustomerAuthentication:

{
"ProfileServiceBaseUrl": "https://...",
"HttpClientTimeoutSeconds": 5,
"SuccessCacheTtlSeconds": 300,
"FailureCacheTtlSeconds": 15,
"CacheKeyPrefix": "custauth:v1"
}

Bound via services.Configure<CustomerAuthenticationOptions>(section). IOptionsMonitor<CustomerAuthenticationOptions> is used everywhere so reloads take effect without restart.

For LD-driven TTLs, consumer registers their own ICustomerAuthTtlProvider:

public interface ICustomerAuthTtlProvider
{
TimeSpan GetSuccessTtl();
TimeSpan GetFailureTtl();
}

Default OptionsCustomerAuthTtlProvider reads from IOptionsMonitor. Host wires LD-backed impl: services.AddSingleton<ICustomerAuthTtlProvider, LaunchDarklyCustomerAuthTtlProvider>(). The new project has zero LD knowledge.

Handler specifics

- HandleAuthenticateAsync:

- Read both headers. If neither → AuthenticateResult.NoResult().

- Both → defensive Fail (middleware catches upstream).

- Determine CustomerTokenType, extract token value.

- Read [CustomerAuthentication] from endpoint metadata for cache eligibility.

- If cache enabled → await _cache.TryGetAsync(tokenType, token). On hit return cached result.

- On miss → await _validator.ValidateAsync(tokenType, token, ct).

- Success → build ClaimsIdentity, cache with success TTL, return Success.

- InvalidToken → cache with failure TTL, return Fail.

- ServiceError → do not cache, return Fail (explicit).

- Cache key: {prefix}:{tokenType}:{base64url(sha256(token))}; value = serialized CustomerTokenValidationResult.

- Claims produced (public CustomerClaimTypes constants): CustomerId, CustomerNumber, Email, IsGuest, PrincipalType = "Person", AuthenticationMethod = GolfNow:GolfId or GolfNow:CustomerToken, AuthenticationToken = raw header value.

WebApi wiring changes

Startup.cs

- ConfigureServices: services.AddCustomerAuthentication(Configuration.GetSection("Auth:CustomerAuthentication"))

- Let [CustomerAuthentication] attribute drive authorization per-endpoint via the registered requirement.

- Replace OpenAPI security mapping: remove AddSecurityMapping<RequiresCustomerTokenAttribute>, add AddSecurityMapping<CustomerAuthenticationAttribute> with X-GolfId-Token and X-Customer-Token schemes.

- Configure pipeline order:

- UseMiddleware<BothHeadersRejectionMiddleware>()

- UseAuthentication() (PlatformPrincipal)

- UseMiddleware<CustomerIdentityInjectionMiddleware>()

- UseIdempotency()

- UseAuthorization()

appsettings.json — add Auth:CustomerAuthentication section; keep Auth:PlatformPrincipal untouched.

Retire (after callers migrate):

- WebApi/Authentication/CustomerTokenAuthenticationHandler.cs (placeholder)

- WebApi/Authentication/RequiresCustomerTokenAttribute.cs (placeholder)

Critical files to modify

- src/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.WebApi/Startup.cs (auth registration around lines 259-326, middleware pipeline)

- src/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.WebApi/Middleware/IdempotencyMiddleware.cs (update ResolveCustomerId to read CustomerClaimTypes.CustomerId)

- src/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.WebApi/appsettings.json (new config section)

- GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.slnx (add new project)

- Directory.Packages.props (new package versions)

Reuse from existing code

- Validator HTTP call shape — mirror GolfNow.Auth.Client.Customer.CustomerAuthenticationClient.

- Claim structure — mirror gn-lib-core's Golf.Authentication.AspNetCore/Customer/CustomerAuthenticationHandler claim set.

- Redis access — inject existing IConnectionMultiplexer singleton; don't register a second one.

- Response envelope — host-side ICustomerAuthenticationResponseWriter implementation uses repo's ResponseBuilder / ErrorCodes from Golf.Abstractions.

Acceptance Criteria

Unit tests (new tests/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Authentication.Customer.Tests/):

- CustomerAuthenticationHandler: headers absent → NoResult; GolfId valid → Success with correct claims; CustomerToken valid → Success; invalid → Fail; cache-enabled → validator not called on hit; cache-disabled → validator always called; service error → Fail and no cache write.

- CustomerAuthenticationAuthorizationHandler: Required + NoResult → fail; Required + Failed → fail; Required + Success → succeed; Optional + NoResult → succeed; Optional + Failed → fail; Optional + Success → succeed.

- BothHeadersRejectionMiddleware → 400 with envelope.

- RedisCustomerTokenCache → hash determinism, separate TTLs, serialization round-trip.

- OptionsCustomerAuthTtlProvider → reload picks up IOptionsMonitor.OnChange.

Integration tests (WebApplicationFactory, stub ICustomerTokenValidator, Redis via Testcontainers):

- [CustomerAuthentication(Required)] + valid X-GolfId-Token → 200, customer claims on HttpContext.User.

- Same with X-Customer-Token → 200.

- Both headers → 400.

- Neither header + Required → 401.

- Neither header + Optional → 200, no customer claims.

- Invalid token (Required or Optional) → 401.

- Cache-enabled endpoint: second request hits cache.

- IdempotencyMiddleware sees CustomerClaimTypes.CustomerId.

Manual smoke — run service locally, curl flagged endpoint with each header, both, and neither. Inspect OTel traces and metrics counters.

OpenAPI — Swagger UI advertises the two new header schemes for customer-auth endpoints.

Out of scope

- DeviceAttestationAuthenticationHandler — leave placeholder as-is; separate ticket.

- Rolling out the attribute to existing controllers — follow-up tickets after infrastructure merges.

- Publishing as a NuGet package — later ticket once a second API wants to consume it.

issues.summary: F23: PCI Data Handling & Observability
issues.description:
Scope

Establish the cross-cutting PCI data-handling and observability contract for Order Processing: logging sanitization rules, SensitiveDataClass enforcement, structured-log allowlist, correlation-ID propagation, and OpenTelemetry metrics/spans/logs for payment outcomes, 3DS, failover, and circuit-breaker events. F23 is constitutional — its rules apply to every subsequent feature (F3–F21) rather than to a single deliverable surface.

In addition, F23 absorbs two deferred tests from F2 — SagaSpanHierarchyTests (F2 T035) and SagaStructuredLogsTests (F2 T037) — and lands the saga observability emission code they depend on (review memo §4 F2 TODO, line 140).

Dependencies

- Blocked by: CORE-14406 (F2 — MassTransit Infrastructure & Saga Persistence) — infrastructure scaffolding for SagaDiagnostics.ActivitySource + Meter is already wired by F2; F23 adds the emission layer on top.

- Related: CORE-14041 (F1 — Persistence Foundations) for the ResultWrapper<T> error-detail shape + idempotency response-cache hygiene; CORE-14405 (ElastiCache provisioning) for TLS/AUTH telemetry expectations.

- Unblocks: every downstream feature that emits saga/payment telemetry — F9, F10, F11, F12, F13, F14, F15, F16, F17, F18, F19, F20.

Deliverables

- PCI logging policy — the SensitiveDataClass taxonomy (PCI Category A/B/C, PII, payment-method identifiers, tokens, tender strings), serialization destructuring rules, and a build-time analyzer or unit-test guardrail that fails CI if a banned property name leaks into a structured-log template or response payload.

- Structured-logging allowlist — the finite set of properties permitted in log events emitted from sagas, adapters, and middleware. Everything outside the allowlist is either dropped or hashed; the allowlist is codified as an ILogEventEnricher (Serilog) + MEL LogFilterOptions pair.

- Correlation-ID propagation — W3C traceparent honored end-to-end: HTTP ingress → saga → outgoing PaymentProcessingClient / Wallet.Client / tax providers. ICorrelationIdAccessor populated from Activity.Current.TraceId; no service-generated log IDs (constitution Principle IX alignment).

- Saga observability emission (completes F2 T035 + T037): MassTransit IConsumeObserver + ISagaStateMachineObserver<TSaga> pair in Repository.Mongo.Sagas, registered from OrderProcessingSagaServiceCollectionExtensions.ApplySagaBusRegistration. - Payment-specific observability — OTel metrics + spans for: authorize/capture/credit/void outcomes (bucketed by adapter + processor); 3DS/SCA challenge outcomes; processor failover transitions; circuit-breaker open/half-open/closed transitions. Metric names + cardinality caps defined per contract (reuse F2's cardinality guardrail pattern).

- Deferred F2 tests — land SagaSpanHierarchyTests and SagaStructuredLogsTests (assertion scaffolds already documented in F2's quickstart.md Scenarios 12 + 14).

- Constitution amendment — promote PCI/observability rules to a numbered principle (provisional: Principle X "PCI Data Handling & Observability Contract"). Future feature plans must cite it in their Sync Impact.

h3. F23 implementation complete — PR opened

PR: [#6|https://github.com/GolfNowEng/gn-api-orderprocessing/pull/6] (draft, base {{develop}})

Scope landed (94-task Speckit plan across 10 phases):

- Build-time defense: {{GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Analyzers}} project + GNPCI0001/0002/0003 rules + JSON allowlists ({{banned-properties.json}}, {{log-properties.json}}) with schemas and CODEOWNERS gates.

- Runtime defense: {{ActivityEnrichmentProcessor}} (OTel), {{BannedPropertyDestructuringPolicy}} (Serilog), {{LogPropertyAllowlistLoggerProvider}} (MEL), {{PciResponseScrubMiddleware}} (opt-in via {{[ScrubsResponseBody]}} attribute), {{LegacyCorrelationIdMiddleware}} + outbound HTTP handler + MassTransit send filter, saga observer pair in {{Repository.Mongo.Sagas.Observability}}, {{PaymentTelemetry}} static surface + {{MetricCardinalityGuard}}.

- Composition: {{PciObservabilityExtensions.AddPciObservability}}; {{PaymentTelemetryBootstrap}} hosted service registered at index 0.

- Performance gate (SC-008, p95 < 1 ms/span + observer overhead ≤ 15%): {{SensitiveDataEnricherBenchmarks}} + {{SagaObserverBenchmarks}} + {{.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml}}.

- Constitution: v1.7.2 → v1.8.0 amendment adding Principle X (PCI Data Handling & Observability Contract). Bundled in-PR per EM approval.

- F2 deferrals closed: CORE-14406 T035 (span hierarchy) + T037 (structured-log templates) now land via the observer pair; F2 docs swept to cite Principle X.

- Review feedback applied: 26 of 27 findings addressed; 1 false alarm, 1 declined with rationale.

Test status:

- 294/294 Unit tests pass locally post-rebase (15 Client + 83 WebApi + 166 Core + 30 Analyzers).

- Integration suite gated on {{integration-tests.yml}} (Docker-backed).

- Benchmark suite gated on {{benchmarks.yml}} (workflow_dispatch + weekly schedule).

- Coverage (Unit-only): Core.Observability 89.0%, WebApi.Observability 75.4%, Repository.Mongo.Sagas.Observability measured under Integration.

Follow-ups to complete before wave close:

- Wire {{BannedPropertyDestructuringPolicy}} into Serilog via a non-DI resolution path (current DI resolution deadlocks NSwag's {{aspnetcore2openapi}} host probe).

- Refresh SC-008 baselines by running {{benchmarks.yml}} to replace seeded values with real BDN measurements.

- Rework {{SagaObserverBenchmarks}} measurement shape — {{harness.Consumed.Any}} is a fold-left collector that scales linearly with BDN iteration count.

Declined review findings (documented in PR body):

- #14 "make {{ISagaStateTracker}} public": kept internal; {{InternalsVisibleTo}} is compile-time test-visibility outside Principle VIII's runtime-adapter-coupling scope.

- #4 "benchmarks.yml action versions": false alarm — {{actions/*@v6}} do exist.

Blockers for prod: none from this PR. Security-team signoff on the initial {{banned-properties.json}} allowlist is a review item but does not block merge.

issues.summary: F2: MassTransit Infrastructure & Saga Persistence
issues.description:
Scope

Wire MassTransit 8.* as the saga orchestration substrate for Order Processing, with MongoDB-backed persistence that honors F1's ObjectId-always _id invariant. Unblocks F9 (Checkout Saga Validate/Authorize), F11 (Payment Domain Model), and downstream post-purchase features (F18-F20).

Dependencies

- Blocked by: CORE-14041 (F1 — Persistence Foundations) — merged on features/CORE-14041-01, pending PR to main

- Related: CORE-14405 (ElastiCache provisioning — required for F1 idempotency and useful for F2's downstream circuit-breaker state)

Deliverables

- MassTransit bus registration in Repository.Mongo / WebApi DI composition

- BsonClassMap<TSaga> overrides registered in Repository.Mongo BEFORE MassTransit.MongoDbIntegration's default class maps (constitution §1.7.1 TODO #1). Maps ISaga.CorrelationId → named element (orderId / sagaId) and adds a separate ObjectId-valued Id → _id

- Saga repository registration for the four primary saga collections (checkout_sagas, cancellation_sagas, refund_sagas, noshow_charge_sagas) per entities §2

- Retry / timeout / redelivery policies per saga type

- OpenTelemetry span hierarchy for saga transitions, message publish/consume, retry attempts

- Unique indexes on correlation-ID fields via IndexBootstrapper

- MassTransit v8.* version pin enforced (constitution §1.7.1 TODO #2) — CI check or test that fails on v9+

Open design decisions (resolved during /speckit specify and /speckit plan)

- P0 gap 2.1 (review memo §2.1): one saga collection (checkout_sagas with inline payment sub-aggregate) vs two (checkout_sagas + payment_sagas). Decision pins downstream F9/F11 architecture.

- Transport choice: RabbitMQ vs SQS. Flagged as pending in review memo §4 F2.

References

- Review memo docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-spec-review-memo.md §4 F2, §2.1

- Constitution §1.7.1 TODO #1 (BsonClassMap ordering), TODO #2 (MassTransit v8 licensing / EOL 2026-12-31)

- Pipeline spec §11.3 (Saga orchestration), §10.3 (Compensation)

- Payment spec §26 (Saga model)

- Entities §2 (saga document schemas)

Acceptance

Refined via /speckit specify + /speckit plan. High-level:

- Four saga collections persist correctly with the required class-map overrides

- BsonClassMap<TSaga> registration happens before MassTransit defaults (asserted by integration test)

- Unique indexes exist on correlation elements

- Retry / timeout policies documented and enforced

- OTel spans observable for a simple saga round-trip

issues.summary: Post-CORE-14411 wave: doc alignment, F23 cleanup, CQRS ADR, F3 Invoice Create & Read
issues.description:
Scope

The next wave of work for gn-api-orderprocessing after CORE-14411 (F23 PCI Data Handling & Observability). This ticket covers the prep work and the first business-capability feature of the service — four sequential steps landing on branches stacked under this one ticket.

Four-step plan

#

Work

Scope

Deliverable

0

Documentation alignment (per-Item granularity)

Parent spec, CLAUDE.md, spec-review-memo. Moves MerchantId, CurrencyCode, and PricingValidUntilUtc from per-ItemComponent (current wrong wording) to per-Item (correct, per EM decision).

Single doc PR, no code

1

F23 cleanup sweep

Backfill missing unit tests for PaymentTelemetry, MetricCardinalityGuard, LuhnPanValidator (all PCI-critical or concurrency-sensitive, shipped without tests in F23). Apply review findings #3 (volatile fields), #4 (cardinality-guard log snapshot race), #5 (stackalloc oversizing). Memory entry project_f23_open_review_findings.md is the source.

Code PR, new tests +25–40

2

CQRS / Mediator architectural decision

Record DO-NOT-ADOPT decision for martinothamar/Mediator as an ADR. Establishes .specify/adr/ as the canonical ADR location. Five-point rationale: MassTransit already owns dispatch; cross-cutting concerns already placed; weak fit across the backlog; Principle VIII friction; no GolfNow precedent.

.specify/adr/001-no-in-process-mediator.md

3

F3 — Invoice Create & Read

First user-facing endpoint of the new service: POST /api/v1/invoices (Active creation, pricing + benefits + promos + estimated tax stub) and GET /api/v1/invoices/{invoiceId} (Expired returned as-is, no auto-reprice). Depends only on F1 (done). Adds MerchantId, CurrencyCode, PricingValidUntilUtc fields to Item.cs (currently absent).

New speckit feature at .specify/specs/004-invoice-create-read/ + code PR

Dependencies

- Related: CORE-14411 (F23 PR #6 — not yet merged to develop; this wave branches from F23's current tip at commit 8d40f60 and rebases onto develop after F23 merges).

- Related: CORE-14041 (F1 Persistence Foundations) for ResponseWrapper<T> envelope, VersionKey, UuidV7, idempotency middleware, Kiota typed-client pipeline.

- Related: CORE-14406 (F2 MassTransit Infrastructure) for saga substrate (no direct saga work in this wave, but observability contract applies).

- Unblocks (follow-on wave): F4 (Invoice Modification + Reprice), F5 (Invoice Finalization, requires F6), F6 (Tax Provider + Rate Store — swaps F3's stub), F11 (Payment Domain Model — can start in parallel with F4/F6).

Out of scope — deferred explicitly

- Invoice PUT + POST /reprice (F4), POST /finalize (F5), hard-tax commit (F5/F6).

- Vertex ITaxProvider implementation + MongoDB rate store + S3 archival (F6/F7).

- Real IPricingProvider implementations per inventory domain (F3 ships stubs; real providers follow).

- Invoice purchase lock (LockedByOrderId + TTL) — acquired in F9 Block 1.

- Constitution amendment for MerchantId — not needed; constitution only references MerchantId as a structured log property and makes no granularity claim.

Branch + worktree

Single parent branch: features/CORE-XXXXX-01 (this ticket). All four step-PRs stack under it.

- Cut from: features/CORE-14411-01 HEAD (8d40f60)

- Worktree path: $WORKTREE_BASE/gn-api-orderprocessing/features-CORE-XXXXX-01

- Work docs: $JIRA_DOCS/CORE-XXXXX/

- Rebase onto develop once CORE-14411 PR #6 merges.

Acceptance

- Step 0: grep -rn "per.component.*\(MerchantId\|CurrencyCode\|PricingValidUntilUtc\)\|ItemComponent.*\(MerchantId\|CurrencyCode\|PricingValidUntilUtc\)" docs/ CLAUDE.md returns zero matches.

- Step 1: dotnet test green with +25–40 new tests in tests/GolfNow.Api.OrderProcessing.Core.Tests/Observability/; no deadlocks under parallel stress.

- Step 2: ADR file exists under .specify/adr/ with Context / Decision / Consequences / When-to-reconsider sections.

- Step 3: POST /api/v1/invoices creates Active invoice with idempotency replay; GET /api/v1/invoices/{id} returns current state or Expired; Kiota client regenerates; full-settings test profile passes (Testcontainers Mongo + Redis); OTLP sink shows allowlisted-only properties.

References

- Plan file (local to EM's machine): ~/.claude/plans/now-that-we-are-typed-sun.md

- Parent spec: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-pipeline-spec.md §6 (invoice lifecycle)

- Payment spec: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-payment-pipeline-spec-v2.md (relevant for F3 observability contract only)

- Review memo: docs/gn-api-orderprocessing-spec-review-memo.md §4 F3 (scope) + Gap 2.3 (MerchantId — resolved in Step 0 of this wave)

- Memory: project_f23_open_review_findings.md (Step 1 source)

- Constitution: Principle IV (persistence), Principle VIII (adapter isolation), Principle IX (exceptions), Principle X (PCI observability)

issues.summary: Provision ElastiCache Valkey for Order Processing API idempotency cache
issues.description:
The Order Processing API (spec 001 / CORE-14041) requires an AWS ElastiCache for Valkey cluster for its idempotency response cache and customer-auth token cache. The service is wired and fails closed gracefully if the cache is unreachable, but needs a real Valkey instance to honor FR-016 "no side effect re-execution" on retries.

Engine note (2026-04-29): This ticket was rescoped from ElastiCache Redis 7.x to ElastiCache Valkey following the decision to migrate off Redis Inc.'s SSPL/RSAL licensing and onto the Linux-Foundation Valkey fork. Valkey is RESP-wire-compatible with Redis — StackExchange.Redis remains the client — so the application-side changes are naming + config only, tracked in CORE-14424.

Required configuration

- Engine: Valkey — latest GA (Valkey 8.x; AWS ElastiCache for Valkey went GA Oct 2024, tracks upstream 7.2 and 8.x)

- Deployment: Non-clustered replication group — 1 primary + ≥1 replica in a different AZ, automatic failover enabled

- Multi-AZ: enabled

- Encryption in transit: Required (PCI). ElastiCache TLS; connection strings must specify ssl=true

- Encryption at rest: AWS KMS service-owned CMK

- Auth: Valkey AUTH (RESP AUTH command, same wire behavior as Redis AUTH) enabled; auth token rotated via AWS Secrets Manager (service reads via existing GolfNow.Tools.ConfigurationSecrets path)

- Subnet group: private subnets within service VPC; no public endpoint

- Security group: inbound 6379 (or custom TLS port) only from the service's EC2 runner SG

- Parameter group (custom, copy from the Valkey-family default — e.g., default.valkey8 — not the Redis default):

- maxmemory-policy = volatile-ttl

- timeout = 300, tcp-keepalive = 300

- appendonly = no

- notify-keyspace-events = ""

- Backups: disabled or 1-day retention (ephemeral data)

- Logging: slow log + engine log → CloudWatch; slow-log threshold 10 ms

- Node type: non-prod cache.t4g.small; prod cache.m7g.large (steady-state ≈210 MB, ≤1000 writes/sec). Valkey on Graviton offers ~20% price/performance advantage vs Redis on equivalent instances per AWS announcement — carry forward as provisioning cost-savings rationale if asked.

- Scaling: vertical first; cluster-mode shards reserved for 10x expected volume

Connection string

Injected via #{Valkey.ConnectionString} placeholder in appsettings.json and resolved by GolfNow.Tools.ConfigurationSecrets. Wire format is unchanged from the Redis equivalent — host, port, ssl, password — since RESP is preserved.

Acceptance criteria

- Three environments (dev, stg, prd) provisioned on ElastiCache Valkey

- Connection strings published to AWS Secrets Manager under the Valkey-namespaced key

- Health-check probe from the service reports Healthy / Degraded correctly per environment

- Valkey engine version and parameter-group choice recorded in infra repo or runbook

Related

- Blocks: CORE-14041 (Order Processing Persistence Foundations)

- Blocks: CORE-14424 (application-side Redis → Valkey migration)

- Constitution §1.7.0 Sync Impact TODO #3

- Spec 001 entities §14.7 (to be refreshed under CORE-14424 from "Redis 7.x" → "Valkey")

- AWS announcement: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey GA (Oct 2024)

comments.body:
2026-04-29 — Rescoped from Redis to Valkey.

Original scope was ElastiCache Redis 7.x. After the decision to migrate off Redis Inc.'s SSPL/RSAL-licensed engine, this ticket now provisions AWS ElastiCache for Valkey (Linux-Foundation OSS fork, GA on AWS Oct 2024). Valkey preserves the RESP wire protocol, so StackExchange.Redis stays as the client library and the configuration shape (host, port, TLS, AUTH token, volatile-ttl maxmemory policy) is unchanged — only the engine identity + parameter-group family (default.valkey8 vs default.redis7) differ.

Application-side renames and documentation updates are tracked separately in CORE-14424 ("Migrate idempotency + customer-auth caches from Redis to Valkey"), which is now blocked by this ticket.

issues.summary: Provision AWS SQS + SNS for Order Processing API saga orchestration (CORE-14406)
issues.description:
The Order Processing API (spec 002 / CORE-14406) uses MassTransit 8 with the AmazonSQS transport as its saga orchestration substrate. The service is wired end-to-end in-repo and passes integration tests against a LocalStack SQS+SNS, but prod deployment needs real SQS queues, SNS topics, and IAM policies provisioned in AWS.

Required AWS resources

SQS queues — one per saga endpoint

Phase 1 sagas (shipping with F9+ / F11 / F18 / F19 / F20 as they land):

- op-checkout-saga

- op-cancellation-saga

- op-refund-saga

- op-noshow-charge-saga

Per-queue config (entities spec §2 / research §Decision 1):

- Visibility timeout: 30 s (tracks StepTimeoutBudget default)

- Message retention: 4 days

- Receive wait time: 20 s (long polling — reduces idle cost)

- Encryption at rest: AWS KMS service-owned CMK

- Redrive policy: maxReceiveCount = 5 → dead-letter queue <queue-name>-dlq (matches DeadLetterRedriveThreshold in OrderProcessingSagaPolicy.Default)

- Dead-letter queue: one per live queue, same encryption, 14-day retention

SNS topics — one per published message type

MassTransit creates one topic per message contract. Early footprint (grows as sagas register):

- op-checkout-start-command

- op-checkout-state-event

- (expands per-saga as F9–F20 land)

Topic config:

- Encryption at rest: AWS KMS service-owned CMK

- Delivery policy: default retry, exponential backoff

- Topic → queue subscription: raw message delivery enabled

IAM policy — EC2 runner role

Grant the existing Order Processing API runner role:

- sqs:SendMessage, sqs:ReceiveMessage, sqs:DeleteMessage, sqs:GetQueueAttributes, sqs:GetQueueUrl, sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility, sqs:PurgeQueue on arn:aws:sqs:<region>:<acct>:op-*

- sqs:CreateQueue, sqs:SetQueueAttributes, sqs:TagQueue if MT's auto-create path remains enabled (default in dev/stg)

- sns:Publish, sns:CreateTopic, sns:Subscribe, sns:GetTopicAttributes, sns:ListSubscriptionsByTopic on arn:aws:sns:<region>:<acct>:op-*

- kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt on the CMK ARN

Observability — CloudWatch + DataDog

CloudWatch (AWS-native):

- Log group per queue (redrive events)

- Standard queue metrics exported (ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible, ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage, NumberOfMessagesSent, NumberOfMessagesReceived, NumberOfMessagesDeleted)

DataDog (primary operator dashboard + paging):

- AWS SQS integration enabled on the service's AWS account — forwards every queue's CloudWatch metrics into DataDog under aws.sqs.*

- AWS SNS integration enabled — forwards topic metrics under aws.sns.*

- Custom DataDog dashboard Order Processing — Saga Transport with per-queue panels: message age, queue depth, send/receive rate, DLQ depth, approximate age of oldest DLQ message

- DataDog monitors (paging tier — PagerDuty integration on trigger):

- DLQ non-empty: aws.sqs.approximate_number_of_messages_visible{queuename:op-*-dlq} > 0 for 5 m — any DLQ message pages on-call

- Queue backlog: aws.sqs.approximate_age_of_oldest_message{queuename:op-*-saga} > 120 s for 10 m — saga processing is falling behind

- Publish failure rate: aws.sns.number_of_notifications_failed{topicname:op-*} > 0 — transport publish is failing

- DataDog monitors (warning tier — Slack #core-alerts):

- Queue depth elevated: aws.sqs.approximate_number_of_messages_visible{queuename:op-*-saga} > 100 for 15 m — indicates throughput lag worth investigating

- Age of oldest near budget: aws.sqs.approximate_age_of_oldest_message > 60 s for 10 m — early warning before the paging threshold

- DataDog tags applied on every monitor / dashboard panel: service:order-processing, component:saga-transport, env:<dev|stg|prd> — matches existing GolfNow service tagging so drill-downs from the service health dashboard work

- Runbook link attached to each paging monitor (template: https://confluence.golfnow.com/pages/runbook-op-saga-transport — page to be authored as part of this ticket)

Terraform module

- Module op-saga-queues in the existing infra repo

- Inputs: environment (dev/stg/prd), saga list, KMS key ARN, runner role ARN

- Outputs: queue ARNs, topic ARNs, DLQ ARNs (consumed by app config)

- DataDog monitors provisioned via the existing DataDog Terraform provider in the same module (or a sibling op-saga-transport-monitors module) — monitors are infra-as-code, not clicked in via the UI

Connection config

Service reads OrderProcessing:Saga:AmazonSQS:Region from appsettings.json; the AWS SDK resolves credentials from the EC2 instance profile. No access/secret keys in app config. Region placeholder substituted by GolfNow.Tools.ConfigurationSecrets at deploy time.

Acceptance criteria

- Three environments (dev, stg, prd) provisioned with the resource set above

- Terraform module authored, reviewed, and applied in all three

- IAM policies attached to the EC2 runner role

- A smoke-publish from the dev environment lands on the expected queue and drains via the saga consumer

- DataDog dashboard Order Processing — Saga Transport is live in all three environments and shows per-queue telemetry

- Every DataDog monitor listed above is deployed and shown green in steady state

- DLQ alarm tested in dev: force-inject a failing message, verify the DLQ monitor pages PagerDuty (or equivalent routing)

- Runbook page authored and linked from every paging monitor

Related

- Blocks: CORE-14406 (MassTransit Infrastructure & Saga Persistence)

- Constitution §1.7.1 (saga transport selection)

- Spec 002 research.md §Decision 1 (transport selection)

- Pattern reference: CORE-14405 (ElastiCache Redis provisioning for idempotency cache)
