comments.author: Daniel McNaughton
comments.bodyHtml:
Terraform module sketch

Starting point for the op-saga-queues module. Treat this as the shape, not the final code — ops should pick it up, fold in the DataDog provider config, and wire it into the existing account/env layer.

variables.tf

variable "env" {
  description = "Deployment environment (dev/stg/prd)"
  type        = string
}

variable "runner_role_arn" {
  description = "EC2 instance role ARN for the Order Processing API runner"
  type        = string
}

variable "kms_key_arn" {
  description = "KMS CMK ARN for at-rest encryption on every queue and topic"
  type        = string
}

variable "sagas" {
  description = "Per-saga endpoint definition — one entry per MT saga registration"
  type = map(object({
    # Commands that MT will create SNS topics for and subscribe to the saga queue
    commands = list(string)
    # Events the saga publishes — SNS topics only, no saga subscription
    events   = list(string)
  }))

  # F9/F11 populate their own entries here as those features land.
  default = {
    "checkout" = {
      commands = [
        "start-checkout-command",
        "finalize-invoice-command",
        "authorize-payment-command",
        "capture-payment-command",
        "allocate-revenue-command",
        "complete-checkout-command",
      ]
      events = [
        "invoice-finalized-event",
        "payment-authorized-event",
        "payment-captured-event",
        "checkout-completed-event",
        "checkout-failed-event",
      ]
    }
    "cancellation" = {
      commands = [
        "initiate-cancellation-command",
        "refund-payment-command",
        "release-inventory-command",
        "complete-cancellation-command",
      ]
      events = [
        "cancellation-initiated-event",
        "payment-refunded-event",
        "inventory-released-event",
        "cancellation-completed-event",
      ]
    }
    # refund + noshow-charge follow the same shape; F18/F19/F20 append here.
  }
}

locals {
  prefix = "op"
  # flatten the saga → command matrix into a single list for for_each'ing subscriptions
  subscriptions = flatten([
    for saga_name, saga in var.sagas : [
      for cmd in saga.commands : {
        saga    = saga_name
        command = cmd
        key     = "${saga_name}:${cmd}"
      }
    ]
  ])
}

sqs.tf

# Dead-letter queue (14-day retention) — one per saga
resource "aws_sqs_queue" "saga_dlq" {
  for_each = var.sagas

  name                      = "${local.prefix}-${each.key}-saga-dlq"
  message_retention_seconds = 1209600   # 14 days
  kms_master_key_id         = var.kms_key_arn
  sqs_managed_sse_enabled   = false

  tags = {
    service   = "order-processing"
    component = "saga-transport"
    env       = var.env
    saga      = each.key
    role      = "dlq"
  }
}

# Live saga queue — 4-day retention, 30 s visibility, redrive to DLQ
resource "aws_sqs_queue" "saga" {
  for_each = var.sagas

  name                       = "${local.prefix}-${each.key}-saga"
  visibility_timeout_seconds = 30
  message_retention_seconds  = 345600  # 4 days
  receive_wait_time_seconds  = 20      # long polling
  kms_master_key_id          = var.kms_key_arn
  sqs_managed_sse_enabled    = false

  redrive_policy = jsonencode({
    deadLetterTargetArn = aws_sqs_queue.saga_dlq[each.key].arn
    maxReceiveCount     = 5   # matches OrderProcessingSagaPolicy.Default.DeadLetterRedriveThreshold
  })

  tags = {
    service   = "order-processing"
    component = "saga-transport"
    env       = var.env
    saga      = each.key
    role      = "live"
  }
}

sns.tf

# One topic per message contract — commands AND events get topics.
# Commands get subscribed to the saga queue (below); events are fan-out (consumers subscribe their own).
resource "aws_sns_topic" "message" {
  for_each = merge([
    for saga_name, saga in var.sagas : merge(
      { for cmd in saga.commands : "${saga_name}:${cmd}" => { type = "command", name = cmd } },
      { for evt in saga.events   : "${saga_name}:${evt}" => { type = "event",   name = evt } },
    )
  ]...)

  name              = "${local.prefix}-${each.value.name}"
  kms_master_key_id = var.kms_key_arn

  tags = {
    service      = "order-processing"
    component    = "saga-transport"
    env          = var.env
    message_type = each.value.type
  }
}

# SNS → SQS subscriptions: every command lands on the owning saga's queue.
resource "aws_sns_topic_subscription" "command_to_saga" {
  for_each = { for s in local.subscriptions : s.key => s }

  topic_arn            = aws_sns_topic.message["${each.value.saga}:${each.value.command}"].arn
  protocol             = "sqs"
  endpoint             = aws_sqs_queue.saga[each.value.saga].arn
  raw_message_delivery = true
}

# SQS policy allowing SNS to deliver messages into each saga queue.
# Required because the queue is KMS-encrypted and the SNS service principal needs explicit grant.
resource "aws_sqs_queue_policy" "saga_allow_sns" {
  for_each  = var.sagas
  queue_url = aws_sqs_queue.saga[each.key].id

  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect    = "Allow"
      Principal = { Service = "sns.amazonaws.com" }
      Action    = "sqs:SendMessage"
      Resource  = aws_sqs_queue.saga[each.key].arn
      Condition = {
        ArnLike = {
          "aws:SourceArn" = "arn:aws:sns:*:*:${local.prefix}-*"
        }
      }
    }]
  })
}

iam.tf

# Inline policy on the service's existing EC2 runner role — scoped to op-* resources only.
data "aws_iam_policy_document" "runner_saga" {
  statement {
    sid = "SqsReceiveAndSend"
    actions = [
      "sqs:SendMessage",
      "sqs:ReceiveMessage",
      "sqs:DeleteMessage",
      "sqs:GetQueueAttributes",
      "sqs:GetQueueUrl",
      "sqs:ChangeMessageVisibility",
      "sqs:PurgeQueue",
    ]
    resources = ["arn:aws:sqs:*:*:${local.prefix}-*"]
  }

  statement {
    sid = "SnsPublishAndSubscribe"
    actions = [
      "sns:Publish",
      "sns:Subscribe",
      "sns:GetTopicAttributes",
      "sns:ListSubscriptionsByTopic",
    ]
    resources = ["arn:aws:sns:*:*:${local.prefix}-*"]
  }

  statement {
    sid       = "KmsForEncryptedQueues"
    actions   = ["kms:GenerateDataKey", "kms:Decrypt"]
    resources = [var.kms_key_arn]
  }

  # sqs:CreateQueue + sns:CreateTopic only in dev/stg where MT's auto-create is on.
  # Prod locks these down — queues/topics must pre-exist in Terraform state.
  dynamic "statement" {
    for_each = var.env == "prd" ? [] : [1]
    content {
      sid = "AutoCreateInLowerEnvs"
      actions = [
        "sqs:CreateQueue", "sqs:SetQueueAttributes", "sqs:TagQueue",
        "sns:CreateTopic", "sns:TagResource",
      ]
      resources = ["*"]
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "runner_saga" {
  name   = "op-saga-transport"
  role   = var.runner_role_arn
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.runner_saga.json
}

datadog.tf (provisioned in the same module or a sibling)

# DLQ non-empty — paging tier
resource "datadog_monitor" "dlq_non_empty" {
  for_each = var.sagas

  name    = "[${var.env}] op-saga ${each.key} DLQ non-empty"
  type    = "metric alert"
  message = <<-MSG
    The ${each.key} saga DLQ has messages — a saga step has failed past its redrive budget.
    Runbook: https://confluence.golfnow.com/pages/runbook-op-saga-transport
    @pagerduty-core-oncall
  MSG

  query = "avg(last_5m):avg:aws.sqs.approximate_number_of_messages_visible{queuename:${aws_sqs_queue.saga_dlq[each.key].name}} > 0"

  monitor_thresholds { critical = 0 }

  tags = ["service:order-processing", "component:saga-transport", "env:${var.env}", "saga:${each.key}"]
}

# Queue backlog age — paging tier
resource "datadog_monitor" "queue_backlog" {
  for_each = var.sagas

  name    = "[${var.env}] op-saga ${each.key} queue backlog"
  type    = "metric alert"
  message = <<-MSG
    The ${each.key} saga queue has messages older than 120 s for 10 min — processing is falling behind.
    Runbook: https://confluence.golfnow.com/pages/runbook-op-saga-transport
    @pagerduty-core-oncall
  MSG

  query = "avg(last_10m):avg:aws.sqs.approximate_age_of_oldest_message{queuename:${aws_sqs_queue.saga[each.key].name}} > 120"

  monitor_thresholds { critical = 120 }

  tags = ["service:order-processing", "component:saga-transport", "env:${var.env}", "saga:${each.key}"]
}

# Queue depth elevated — warning tier (Slack #core-alerts)
resource "datadog_monitor" "queue_depth" {
  for_each = var.sagas

  name    = "[${var.env}] op-saga ${each.key} queue depth elevated"
  type    = "metric alert"
  message = <<-MSG
    The ${each.key} saga queue has > 100 visible messages for 15 min — investigate throughput.
    @slack-core-alerts
  MSG

  query = "avg(last_15m):avg:aws.sqs.approximate_number_of_messages_visible{queuename:${aws_sqs_queue.saga[each.key].name}} > 100"

  monitor_thresholds {
    warning  = 50
    critical = 100
  }

  tags = ["service:order-processing", "component:saga-transport", "env:${var.env}", "saga:${each.key}"]
}

# Publish failure rate — paging tier (detects SNS delivery failures)
resource "datadog_monitor" "publish_failures" {
  name    = "[${var.env}] op-saga SNS publish failures"
  type    = "metric alert"
  message = <<-MSG
    One or more op-* SNS topics are failing to deliver — bus transport is degraded.
    Runbook: https://confluence.golfnow.com/pages/runbook-op-saga-transport
    @pagerduty-core-oncall
  MSG

  # topic_name tag on aws.sns.* scopes to all op-* topics via wildcard
  query = "sum(last_5m):sum:aws.sns.number_of_notifications_failed{topicname:${local.prefix}-*} > 0"

  monitor_thresholds { critical = 0 }

  tags = ["service:order-processing", "component:saga-transport", "env:${var.env}"]
}

outputs.tf

output "saga_queue_arns" {
  value = { for k, q in aws_sqs_queue.saga : k => q.arn }
}

output "saga_dlq_arns" {
  value = { for k, q in aws_sqs_queue.saga_dlq : k => q.arn }
}

output "topic_arns" {
  value = { for k, t in aws_sns_topic.message : k => t.arn }
}

main.tf (env caller)

module "op_saga_queues" {
  source = "../../modules/op-saga-queues"

  env             = "prd"
  runner_role_arn = data.aws_iam_role.op_api_runner.arn
  kms_key_arn     = aws_kms_key.op_saga.arn
  # sagas = { ... }   # override defaults if needed per env
}

Notes for ops

  • for_each over var.sagas means adding a new saga later (F18 refund, F19 no-show) is a one-line variable update — no new resource blocks.

  • Commands and events are both SNS topics, but only commands get subscribed to the saga queue. Events are fan-out; downstream consumers (notifications, analytics) subscribe their own queues to the topics they care about.

  • MT's mt.AutoDeploy should be set to false in prod so the bus fails loudly if a queue is missing from Terraform state, instead of silently auto-creating a permissionless queue that then fails at delivery. The IAM policy above locks down sqs:CreateQueue / sns:CreateTopic in prd to enforce this.

  • Refund / no-show sagas are omitted from the default variable value — add them when F18 / F19 / F20 register their state machines. Queue naming stays consistent (op-refund-saga, op-noshow-charge-saga).

issues.summary: Configure MongoDB Atlas cross-region replica set (us-east-2 primary / us-east-1 backup) for Order Processing API failover
issues.description:
The Order Processing API (spec 001 / CORE-14041 + spec 002 / CORE-14406) persists saga state and operational collections to MongoDB. Spec 002 FR-025 requires the underlying Atlas cluster to support active/passive cross-region failover (primary us-east-2, standby us-east-1) so in-flight sagas survive a region-wide primary outage without data loss. This ticket provisions the Atlas configuration.

Quorum constraint — why 3 nodes in 2 regions isn't enough

MongoDB elects a new primary only when a strict majority of voting members is reachable. Any 3-node replica set split across only 2 regions (2+1 or 1+2) is asymmetric: one region's failure leaves a minority that cannot self-elect. The outcome is an unrecoverable read-only state until manual reconfig removes the dead members. For automatic bidirectional failover, the replica set MUST span at least 3 failure domains (regions).

Every topology below satisfies that constraint.

Prod topology — 5 nodes across 3 regions (2+2+1)

Region

Voting data-bearing nodes

Priority

Role

us-east-2

2 (different AZs)

7, 6

Primary under normal ops

us-east-1

2 (different AZs)

5, 4

Warm secondary; becomes primary if us-east-2 fails

us-west-2

1 (smallest electable tier)

1

Tiebreaker — no app traffic, no analytics workloads

- Voting quorum = 3 of 5. Any single region can fail without losing quorum. Any single AZ within either active region can fail without impact.

- Electable members: all 5 (so any region can hold primary after failover)

- Cluster tier: baseline M30 on the four us-east-* nodes, M10 on the us-west-2 tiebreaker; revisit under production load

- Do not use arbiters. Atlas deprecates them for multi-region because they can leave you without enough data-bearing majority-write members on a partial failure. Every voting member here is a full data-bearing node.

Stg topology — 3 nodes across 3 regions (1+1+1)

Region

Voting data-bearing nodes

Priority

Role

us-east-2

1

7

Primary under normal ops

us-east-1

1

5

Secondary; becomes primary if us-east-2 fails

us-west-2

1

1

Tiebreaker

- Voting quorum = 2 of 3. Bidirectional automatic failover works the same as prod.

- Cluster tier: M10 on all three nodes — same tier across regions keeps the topology simple and keeps the DR drill representative.

- Topology parity with prod is the point. The consensus / election code paths are identical between 1+1+1 and 2+2+1; only AZ-failure tolerance differs. Stg exercises the same failover flow prod will.

- A 2+1 topology across only 2 regions was considered and rejected — same node cost as 1+1+1 but with asymmetric failover (one region's failure leaves stg read-only). No upside.

Dev topology — 3 nodes single-region (3+0)

Region

Voting data-bearing nodes

Role

us-east-2

3 (different AZs)

Standard single-region replica set

- Cluster tier: M10 × 3

- No cross-region failover — dev is individual-developer work and feature-branch experimentation. Cross-region behavior is validated in stg's integration tests and the quarterly DR drill; reproducing it in dev isn't worth the data-transfer cost.

- Developers who need to reproduce a failover bug locally can spin up a scratch Atlas cluster with the stg topology, or run a local multi-container replica-set for the specific bug.

Failover behavior (all environments with multi-region topology)

- Automatic failover enabled — no manual intervention

- Target election time within Atlas's documented RTO (~10 s election + DNS TTL)

- Write concern: default majority; application tolerates transient primary-election window (already true for any MongoDB driver client, called out in FR-025)

- Read preference: primaryPreferred (saga reads want the latest write; fall back to secondary only when primary is unreachable)

Connection

- SRV endpoint (mongodb+srv://) — Atlas manages primary resolution transparently, application doesn't hard-code region-specific hostnames

- Connection string injected via #{MongoDb.ConnectionString} placeholder in appsettings.json and resolved by GolfNow.Tools.ConfigurationSecrets

- Atlas rotates this if the cluster topology changes; secret-manager entry MUST be the Atlas SRV URI, not a hard-coded replica-set member list

Security

- VPC peering between the Atlas project's VPCs and the service's EC2 VPCs in us-east-2, us-east-1, AND us-west-2 (prod + stg; dev only needs us-east-2)

- Private endpoint (Atlas PrivateLink) preferred over internet-facing endpoints

- TLS in transit: required

- Encryption at rest: Atlas-managed + BYO key via AWS KMS

- Database user: one service account for Order Processing with readWrite on the service's database only

- IP access list: locked to the service's VPC CIDRs in every region the cluster spans

Backups & disaster recovery

- Atlas Continuous Backups enabled (point-in-time restore)

- Backup retention: 7 days minimum

- Quarterly DR drill — run in stg, not prod. Force a primary stepdown of the us-east-2 primary via the Atlas API, verify the service reconnects to the new primary (expected: us-east-1 secondary promoted within ~30 s) and continues serving reads/writes. Repeat with us-east-1 as the failing region to confirm bidirectional recovery.

Observability

DataDog

- Atlas integration enabled — forwards cluster metrics under mongodb.atlas.* / mongodb.*

- Custom DataDog dashboard Order Processing — MongoDB with:

- Primary member + region (changes on failover)

- Replication lag per secondary (us-east-2-secondary, us-east-1, us-west-2)

- Oplog window duration (warn if the lag approaches the window)

- Connection pool saturation

- Saga-collection operation counts + latency (tagged by collection: saga_checkout, saga_cancellation, etc.)

- DataDog monitors (paging tier):

- Replica set unhealthy: Atlas health check degraded for > 2 m — pages on-call

- Replication lag on us-east-1 secondary: mongodb.replset.lag_us_east_1 > 60 s for 5 m — DR posture degraded; failover to us-east-1 would lose recent writes

- Oplog window shrinking: mongodb.oplog.hours_available < 12 h — replication can't catch up; secondary is at risk of resync

- DataDog monitors (warning tier — Slack #core-alerts):

- Primary election occurred: annotation event when mongodb.replset.primary changes — not a page, just a visible marker on dashboards

- Replication lag on us-west-2 tiebreaker: mongodb.replset.lag_us_west_2 > 120 s for 10 m — tiebreaker lag is lower-stakes (it's a voting member, not a failover target), but sustained lag could affect election behavior

- Connection pool elevated: > 70% pool utilization for 10 m

- DataDog tags applied: service:order-processing, component:mongodb, env:<dev|stg|prd>

- Runbook link attached to each paging monitor (https://confluence.golfnow.com/pages/runbook-op-mongodb — to be authored)

Atlas-native

- Atlas Alerts: primary election, replication lag > 60 s, backup job failure — forwarded to the same PagerDuty routing as DataDog monitors

Terraform module

- Module op-mongo-atlas in the existing infra repo using the official mongodb/mongodbatlas provider

- Inputs: environment (dev/stg/prd), service VPC IDs (one per region the environment spans), KMS key ARN for BYOK encryption, topology selection (single-region for dev, 1+1+1 for stg, 2+2+1 for prd)

- Outputs: SRV connection string (pushed to AWS Secrets Manager), Atlas project ID, cluster name

- Includes: project, cluster, database user, network-access-list entries, PrivateLink endpoint per region, DataDog integration

Acceptance criteria

- Three environments provisioned per the topology tables above — dev (3+0 single-region M10), stg (1+1+1 three-region M10), prd (2+2+1 three-region M30/M10)

- Terraform module authored, reviewed, and applied in all three

- Atlas PrivateLink endpoints reachable from the service's EC2 instances in every region the cluster spans

- A smoke query from the dev environment hits the primary and completes successfully

- DR drill executed in stg: (a) force us-east-2 primary stepdown via the Atlas API, verify the service reconnects to the new primary in us-east-1 within ~30 s without a deploy and continues serving reads/writes; (b) force us-east-1 primary stepdown (now that it's primary), verify recovery back to us-east-2. Repeat cadence: quarterly.

- DataDog dashboard Order Processing — MongoDB live in all three environments

- Every DataDog monitor listed above is deployed and green in steady state (prd + stg)

- Runbook page authored and linked from every paging monitor

Related

- Blocks: CORE-14406 (MassTransit Infrastructure & Saga Persistence)

- Relates to: CORE-14041 (Order Processing Persistence Foundations) — CORE-14041's Mongo usage inherits this Atlas topology

- Spec 002 FR-025 (regional failover data-layer support)

- Pattern reference: CORE-14405 (ElastiCache Redis provisioning), CORE-14407 (SQS + SNS provisioning)

Summary

This issue involves researching the Claude Code tooling suite. The focus is on checking documentation, practicing, and creating custom tools to improve usual tasks.

Context

The research aims to enhance understanding and usage of the Claude Code tooling suite. This suite includes slash commands, skills, MCP servers, hooks, agents, and more.

Acceptance criteria

- Review and analyze the documentation for Claude Code tooling.

- Practice using the tools provided in the suite.

- Develop custom tools that improve efficiency in regular tasks.

Other information

issues.summary: Support ChatGPT Deeplinking and Reservation Metadata
issues.description:
Links from our ChatGPT app will contain a UTM param and we need to make sure we store that locally so we can attribute purchases.

-  utm_source=chatgptapp will be appended to all links so page views can be tracked with analytics and we can create a cookie

- Make sure this is not stripped for the app deeplinks

- Store this in the device for 24 hours

- If a reservation is made with that stored value

- Submit ReservationMetadata at time of purchase for any purchase within 24 hours: Key 86, Value: 1

- FYI Key 86 = IsChatGPTReservation

issues.summary: Accept and Apply Salesforce-Provided OwnerIDs for PNAS Enablement
issues.description:
Summary

The original ticket scopes GNC Manage Websites updates based on OwnerIDs derived from the GolfFacilityID mapping. However, Salesforce will explicitly pass the specific OwnerID(s) they want enabled for Pay Now and Save — the endpoint must accept and apply these directly.

Background

The original ticket assumes Owner IDs are resolved internally from the GolfFacilityID (PlayFacilityID). In practice, Salesforce will always pass one or more explicit OwnerID values in the payload to designate which owners should have PNAS enabled. This is a required addition to the inbound payload contract.

Examples of OwnerIDs Salesforce may pass:

- 331

- 7886

- Multiple IDs (array/list)

What's Missing

The inbound Salesforce payload (as scoped in CORE-14186) does not currently include OwnerID(s) as a field. The endpoint must be updated to:

- Accept one or more OwnerID values from the Salesforce payload

- Apply GNC Manage Websites changes (Gotta Play Enabled, Intervals Per Hour) scoped to only the OwnerID(s) provided — not all owners resolved from the facility mapping

Payload Addition Required

Add to the Salesforce Apex payload fields:

- OwnerIDs (array of integers) — one or more Owner IDs for which PNAS should be enabled/disabled

Acceptance Criteria

- The endpoint accepts an OwnerIDs field (array) in the inbound Salesforce payload.

- GNC Manage Websites updates (Gotta Play Enabled, Intervals Per Hour) are applied only to the OwnerID(s) explicitly passed by Salesforce.

- If OwnerIDs is missing or empty, the endpoint returns a validation error (required field).

- Idempotent behavior is maintained — repeated calls with the same OwnerIDs do not cause duplication or inconsistent state.

- OwnerID(s) are included in audit/logging output alongside the resolved facility.

Related

- Parent ticket: CORE-14186

issues.summary: Adding ability to define "seconds" to Autoload
issues.description:
NOTE: This is also happening at TSP facilities (non-AL) according to EZL TTP meeting from 10/23

NOTE: Reported to be an issue also with TSP. Get with Sykes to get examples of this causing issues

---
EZLinks use seconds on their tee times.

Autoload doesn’t support seconds.  In the case where EZL have a 10:00:30 AM and AL is loading a 10:00 AM

This time is not bookable and will received EZL24 error during the TeeTimeValidate steps.

Research into the following:

What changes are needed in order to support seconds for Autoload?

- Any UI changes?

- What application will needs to be updated?

- Are there any database changes?

- Will our inventory sync processes continue to function properly?

- …etc

Engineer Notes:

- NBCU.Golf.RMS.WebApp\Views\Inventory\AutoLoadTeeTimesGrid.cshtml is using .ShortTimeString() where it is removing seconds.

- Seconds should be defaults to 00.

- Make sure timepicker does not remove seconds.

- Check related javascripts, validators, where it might also be removing seconds from the time.

QA Notes

- Regression test booking flow + cache manager for tee-times loaded with seconds to confirm we don’t break prod with this.

issues.summary: Loyalty - Points Not Subtracting for Cancelled Reservations
issues.description:
Golfers booking a TT online, receive GP Points but the cancellation via IVR or Website does not subtract the points earned for this reservation.

This issue is related to a previous ticket - TTSUPPORT-7119: GolfPass Rewards Points not being subtracted after cancelling Planning

Example:
bsteiner23@gmail.com
This account is placing approx. 10 Reservations a day and cancelling while within the courses policy.
The below Canceled Reservations have all retained the points earned upon booking:
418274535- Canceled the same day, 13 hours after booking (256 pts)
418380252- Canceled the same day, 9 hours after booking (251 pts)
418351863- Canceled the same day, 9 hours after booking (241 pts)

Replication:

- Reservation placed by non-GP member, using a credit card as the method of payment.

- Points are placed on the ‘Pending’ list, set to apply to the account on the day of the TT

- TT is canceled before cancellation policy. This can be done via IVR or Website.

- Points remain to be applied after TT date has occurred.

issues.summary: Monthly Promo Codes Not Reinstated After Cancelling Reservation
issues.description:
The $10 monthly promo code is not being reinstated after customers cancel their reservation made with the code (all within the acceptable cancellation window).

Steps to recreate:

- Make reservation using $10 monthly promo code

- Cancel reservation

- Go to GNC and see the promo code is still in ‘claimed’ status

- Also try to reuse promo code to confirm this isn’t just a UI issue

Expected vs actual result:

- Expected: Users who cancel the reservation within the acceptable cancellation window should see the code become reinstated and available for use on another tee time

- Actual: Code remains in ‘claimed’ status and cannot be applied to another tee time

issues.summary: Add Club Fitting Location Id to GNC Facility Settings
issues.description:
We need to add a new field (input value) to GNC’s Facility Settings page called ‘Club Fitting Location Id’. This will allow the business to manually update the location id  themselves without having to wait on us to write a script to insert the data. This should UPSERT to CRMGolfFacilitySettings like the following:

INSERT INTO CRMGolfFacilitySettings
(
[GolfFacilityID],
[Key],
[Value],
[CreateDateTime],
[UpdateDateTime],
[ChangedBy]
)
VALUES
(
20052,
'ClubChampionStoreName',
'Lafayette',
GETUTCDATE(),
NULL,
13590
),

- If the facility status = Master, hide the Club Fitting field on the UI

- If you delete from GNC, it should delete from the database

- Change the field name in DB to ClubFittingLocationId and update associated procs (API 2.1 uses this field currently). Only change DB column name, not API property to avoid breaking UI.

issues.summary: Geosearch2.0 : remove Ids specific filter from search index
issues.descriptionHtml:
currently the code hardcoded the datasource filter like so, in the search aggregation

{
    case "CRM": filterArray.Add(new BsonDocument() { { "exists", new BsonDocument() { { "path", "Ids.CRMId" } } } } ); break;
    case "CourseInfo": filterArray.Add(new BsonDocument() { { "exists", new BsonDocument() { { "path", "Ids.CourseInfoId" } } } }); break;
    case "Fandango": filterArray.Add(new BsonDocument() { { "exists", new BsonDocument() { { "path", "Ids.FandangoTheaterId" } } } }); break;
    default: break;
}

however, to make more generic and not branch specific, we need to remove the Ids specific definition from the search index and use DataOrigin field instead. And we will respect the role level configuration to filter by the role’s DataOrigin. For example : if role’s DataOrigin specify “CRM”, we would filter by if DataOrigin contain “CRM” value.

issues.summary: Research and fix SQL Prompt issue in SSMS 22.4.1
issues.description:
Summary

There is an issue with SQL Prompt in SSMS 22.4.1. This problem arose after upgrading to the latest version.

Context

The issue occurred following an upgrade to SSMS version 22.4.1.

Error activating IHttpClientFactory
No matching bindings are available, and the type is not self-bindable.
Activation path:
7) Injection of dependency IHttpClientFactory into parameter httpClientFactory of constructor of type QtpApiFetcher
6) Injection of dependency IQtpApiFetcher into parameter qtpApiFetcher of constructor of type IndexAnalyzer
5) Injection of dependency IIndexAnalyzer into parameter indexAnalyzer of constructor of type IndexAnalysisResultViewModelFactory
4) Injection of dependency IIndexAnalysisResultViewModelFactory into parameter indexAnalysisResultViewModelFactory of constructor of type QtpIndexesController
3) Injection of dependency IQtpIndexesController into parameter qtpIndexesController of constructor of type IndexAnalysisCommandController
2) Injection of dependency IIndexAnalysisCommandController into parameter indexAnalysisCommandController of constructor of type ShowIndexAnalysisAiCommand
1) Request for ShowIndexAnalysisAiCommand

Suggestions:
1) Ensure that you have defined a binding for IHttpClientFactory.
2) If the binding was defined in a module, ensure that the module has been loaded into the kernel.
3) Ensure you have not accidentally created more than one kernel.
4) If you are using constructor arguments, ensure that the parameter name matches the constructors parameter name.
5) If you are using automatic module loading, ensure the search path and filters are correct.

Acceptance criteria

- Research the SQL Prompt issue.

- Implement a fix for the identified problem.

Solution

Redgate released a new version where the issue was fixed. [https://productsupport.red-gate.com/hc/en-us/community/posts/34727409486493-SQL-Prompt-not-working-on-newest-SSMS-22-4-1-version]
After installed the new version released, SSMS v22.4.1 worked successfully.

issues.summary: Offering Type Mapping
issues.description:
Our production integration partners will use various different names for their Service categories and we will need a way to map those to standardized Service Categories on our platform.

Examples from Club Champion:

- Full Bag

- Full Bag (No Putter)

- Driver

- Iron

- Wedge

- Putter

On our system, we should have platform standard categories so we can make standardized API filters that do not require unique naming conventions. Please use the exact spelling provided below as this will likely be exposed to the UI and would like it to match.

Go Live Service Categories:

- Full bag fitting

- Driver fitting

- Iron fitting

- Wedge fitting

- Putter fitting

Requirements:

- Create standardized service categories

- These should be mapped by ID and not Name just in case the names change in the future

- Create a mapping table where we can map an integrators service names to our standardized names

- Example: We would map ClubChampion’s Full Bag to Full bag fitting

- Example: We would map GOLFTEC’s full_bag_fitting to Full bag fitting

- So when the Inventory API calls to get locations that contain a service for ServiceCategory=Full bag fitting, it would return both Club Champion and GOLFTEC’s locations that contain their version of full bag fittings

- Same for the time slots at an individual location, filtering for ServiceCategory=Full bag fitting should account for any category mapped to Full bag fitting

- We need the ability to add new standard service categories with a database update

- Example: if we wanted to start exposing Hybrid fittings, we could add a new category and start mapping new integrators to it

issues.summary: Timelyst - Replicate Cache Manager behavior
issues.description:
Overview

Replicate the legacy CacheManager QueueUtility behavior in the Timelyst Hangfire project. The CacheManager syncs tee time inventory from external booking systems (EZL, B9, AGI, USC, CC, etc.) into GolfNow's cache using a four-tier priority schedule system that determines sync frequency based on date range proximity.

Replace the legacy long-running console app (polling loop) with Hangfire-based scheduled jobs in gn-svc-timelyst.Hangfire.

Background — Legacy Schedule System

The legacy system uses three CRM SQL Server tables:

- CRMUniqueRackSchedule — Routing table that maps facility/interface/course to a schedule group via 4-tier waterfall: UniqueGolfCourseID > PlayFacilityID > InterfaceType > Global default

- CRMScheduleGroup — Named container grouping scheduling rules (e.g., "365 Day Schedule")

- CRMScheduleGroupDetail — Actual interval rules: "for days X through Y, sync every Z minutes" with Action type (Active/Reactive/SyncOnly)

SyncTypes (Action column):

- 0 = ActiveCacheAndSync — always fetch tee times

- 1 = ReactiveCacheAndSync — only fetch if tee times already exist in range

- 2 = SyncOnly — synchronize existing cached data only

Example 365-day schedule tiers:

Days Out

Frequency

Action

0–1

60 min (1 hr)

Active

2–7

120 min (2 hr)

Active

8–14

240 min (4 hr)

Active

15–30

480 min (8 hr)

Active

31–63

719 min (~12 hr)

Reactive

64–365

1439 min (~24 hr)

Reactive

Architecture — Hangfire Replacement

Infrastructure

Component

Technology

Job scheduler

Hangfire (Redis-backed)

Message queue

AWS SQS

Interface config

MongoDB (InterfaceConfiguration collection)

Schedule data

SQL Server (existing CRM tables, new Dapper repos)

Three-Layer Job Hierarchy

1. InterfaceConfigurationBootstrapJob (recurring, every 6 hours)

- Registered at startup — the only hardcoded job

- Reads MongoDB InterfaceConfiguration collection

- For each enabled interface: AddOrUpdate a ReconciliationJob

- Removes orphaned reconciliation jobs for disabled/deleted interfaces

2. CacheManagerScheduleReconciliationJob (per interface type, cron from MongoDB config)

- Queries all active facilities for this interface type from CRM SQL

- Resolves schedule per facility using 4-tier waterfall (UniqueGolfCourseID > PlayFacilityID > InterfaceType > Global)

- Creates/updates one Hangfire recurring job per facility + date-range tier

- Removes orphaned sync jobs for deactivated facilities

3. CacheManagerSyncJob (per facility + date range — SQS producer)

- Triggered by Hangfire cron (derived from Frequency in CRMScheduleGroupDetail)

- Publishes message to AWS SQS with: PlayFacilityID, InterfaceType, DaysOutStart, DaysOutEnd, Action

- A separate queue worker project processes sync items from SQS

Key Design Decisions

4-Tier Waterfall Resolution (Expanded from Legacy 3-Tier)

The legacy C# QueueUtility uses a 3-tier waterfall. The Hangfire version implements the full 4-tier waterfall from the [GolfCourse].[GetScheduleDetail] stored proc:

- UniqueGolfCourseID — most specific (course-level override)

- PlayFacilityID — facility-level override

- InterfaceType — interface default (e.g. "EZL"), where PlayFacilityID and UniqueGolfCourseID are NULL

- Global default — all nulls (least specific fallback)

One Job Per Facility Per Tier (Scale by Design)

Creates a Hangfire recurring job for every facility + date-range combination. E.g., 500 EZL facilities x 6 tiers = 3,000 recurring jobs. Scales horizontally by adding more Hangfire workers.

No 7-Day Window Chunking

The legacy system subdivides each range into 7-day windows. The Hangfire version uses detail ranges as-is from CRMScheduleGroupDetail — the 7-day windowing was a legacy implementation detail, not a business requirement.

Frequency-to-Cron Mapping

Legacy DB frequency values (59, 113, 239, etc.) were set just under round numbers to stagger polling. With cron-based scheduling, these are rounded up to clean cron intervals:

DB Frequency

Rounded To

Cron

59 min

60 min

0 */1 * * *

113 min

120 min

0 */2 * * *

239 min

240 min

0 */4 * * *

719 min

720 min

0 */12 * * *

1439 min

1440 min

0 0 */1 * *

ReactiveCacheAndSync Handled by Queue Worker

The Hangfire scheduler does NOT check for tee time existence. All Action types are enqueued to SQS on schedule. The queue worker handles Action=0 (always fetch), Action=1 (check existence first), and Action=2 (sync only).

Interface Configuration via MongoDB

Interface types are NOT hardcoded. A MongoDB InterfaceConfiguration collection drives which reconciliation jobs are registered. Supports enable/disable without redeployment, adding new interfaces by inserting a document, and per-interface reconciliation cron schedules.

What Replaces IsQueueable?

In the legacy system, IsQueueable checks elapsed time against the frequency. With Hangfire, the cron expression itself enforces the interval. The CRMUniqueRackQueueStatus table is replaced by Hangfire's built-in job execution history.

Data Access — New Repositories (Dapper)

Build new repositories in gn-svc-timelyst.Hangfire using Dapper against existing CRM SQL Server tables. Do NOT depend on legacy GolfNow.Data assemblies.

Required repository interfaces:

- IFacilityRepository — GetActiveFacilitiesByInterfaceAsync(interfaceType) — queries CRMGolfCourse joined with CRMUniqueGolfCourseMap

- IScheduleRepository — GetAllUniqueRackSchedulesAsync() and GetAllScheduleGroupDetailsAsync() — reads CRMUniqueRackSchedule and CRMScheduleGroupDetail

- IInterfaceConfigurationRepository — GetAllInterfacesAsync() — reads MongoDB InterfaceConfiguration collection

Implementation Tasks

- Create MongoDB InterfaceConfiguration collection schema and seed data

- Implement Dapper repositories (IFacilityRepository, IScheduleRepository) against CRM SQL tables

- Implement InterfaceConfigurationBootstrapJob (reads MongoDB, manages reconciliation job registrations)

- Implement CacheManagerScheduleReconciliationJob (per interface — resolves schedules, creates sync jobs)

- Implement 4-tier waterfall schedule resolution logic

- Implement FrequencyToCron mapping with clean interval rounding

- Implement CacheManagerSyncJob (SQS producer — publishes sync messages)

- Implement orphaned job cleanup for both reconciliation and sync jobs

- Configure SQS queue name via appsettings (environment-specific)

- Add DisableConcurrentExecution and AutomaticRetry(0) to all jobs

Migration Path

- Phase 1: Deploy alongside legacy QueueUtility (both running, legacy is primary). Queue worker is idempotent — duplicate messages are harmless.

- Phase 2: Validate Hangfire jobs produce correct SQS messages by comparing with legacy output.

- Phase 3: Disable legacy QueueUtility, Hangfire becomes primary.

- Phase 4: Remove legacy QueueUtility code and CRMUniqueRackQueueStatus dependency.

Reference

Full technical deep-dive with code examples, SQL schemas, and pseudocode: .claude/CacheManager-Schedule-System.md in the gn-svc-timelyst repository.

issues.summary: Update Fee Messaging Logic to Include Dynamic Transaction Fees
issues.description:
In order to display the correct fee messaging on the front end, we need to update our logic to account for dynamic transaction fees enabled in the Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees table.

Example:

- Revenue team updates trade transaction fees at FID 55 from $3.49 to $1.99

- This update is stored in Reservation.DynamicTransactionFees (not CRMOwnerGolfFacility)

- Current outcome: The API returns $3.49 fee messaging and therefore the UI displays this incorrect value

- Expected outcome: The API should return the $1.99 fee messaging in order for front end to display the correct value

Note: The transaction fee is correct at the invoice level, it’s just the Fee Messaging that needs updated

issues.summary: Set up and investigate Claude Code
issues.description:
Summary

This issue involves setting up and investigating Claude Code for adoption. It includes reviewing documentation, configuring environments, and running a pilot implementation.

Context

The goal is to prepare for the use of Claude Code by ensuring all necessary setups and configurations are in place. This will help in evaluating its effectiveness and identifying any potential issues.

Acceptance criteria

- Review available documentation and system requirements for Claude Code.

- Set up accounts, permissions, and access controls for stakeholders.

- Configure the development environment and install recommended IDE extensions or plugins.

- Connect Claude Code to relevant code repositories or projects.

- Define initial use cases and workflows for testing.

- Run a pilot implementation with a limited group of users.

- Collect structured feedback on value, gaps, and issues.

- Document findings, identified risks, configuration choices, and recommended next steps.

comments.author: Dewan Kabir
comments.body:
We have found out that an Automation user QAParness , was being used via an automation test script to update the Temporary Facility Closure records in the Facility Settings page .

We were able to locate that , by investigating an involved Stored Procedure , which was looking into the facility Closure Map table , and saw that if there was an active record, then the tee times would not be returned by the stored procedure .

Upon removing any Facility Closure records in GNC for the affected facility , we were able to see the loaded inventory and complete the booking process .

As a precaution , we made QAParness Inactive in AWS DEV , and are looking into the teams which might be using that Automation user .

We also observed that , the tee times / inventory were bookable after the End Date of the Facility Closure schedule .

issues.summary: Support multiple Apple Pay cryptograms for a purchase
issues.description:
Update OrderCheckout endpoints to support the client passing two Apple Pay Cryptograms as PaymentMethods to buy a Tee time + GolfPass in the same transaction.

Apple Pay Docs: https://applepaydemo.apple.com/

- Apple Pay creates a cryptogram for each merchant and the client (web/app) will call out to Apple Pay to get the cryptograms and pass them to the API. Apple Pay calls this “Multi Merchant”.

- Need the ability to support a tee time + golfpass transaction where the client can pass in both but the user will only see one Apple Pay prompt with the combined values

- This should have the same validations as a credit card transaction where GolfPass is processed first

- This should have the same validations as a credit card transaction where if the tee time fails, the GolfPass can still succeed and purchasef

- Ensure that standalone tee time transactions function with all payment methods including Apple Pay

- Ensure that standalone GolfPass transactions function with all payment methods including Apple Pay

- Test with Hot Deals, Course times, Prepaid Course Times, Prepaid times with GN & GC revenue allocation all in combination with and without GolfPass

- This will require full regression of OrderCheckout API

- We need backwards compatibility to not break current OrderCheckout

- Confirm GolfPass Renewals work with Apple Pay as payment method

- Test Free Trial renewal to paid product with Apple Pay

- Confirm No Shows are functional for Apple Pay reservations

- Confirm Refunds are functional for Apple Pay

issues.summary: CLONE - Club Champion Interface
issues.description:
Interface Integration Checklist
Simulator / Fittings API – Club Champion

---
- General Information

Interface Name: Club Champion Fittings Integration
Vendor / Partner Name: Club Champion
Primary Contact Name: Dhruv Bhalodi
Primary Contact Email: dhruvbhalodi@astuteconsultingllc.com
Postman Collection: Pending (to be provided)
Environments: QA and Production

---
- API Workflow Overview

Order of Operations:

- Auth

- Availability Info

- Schedule Appointment

- Cancellation (endpoint provided)

---
- Auth Call

Notes:

- Site can be null

- Secret can be null

- Response must return "access_token"

Validation:

- Access token retrieved successfully

- Token stored securely

- Token expiration handling confirmed

---
- Availability Info Call

Example Request Body:

{
"storeName": "Chicago",
//"fitterId": "AnyFitter",
"selectedFittings": [
"Iron"
],
"page": 1
}

Requirements:

- storeName required

- selectedFittings required (array)

- page must always be 1

- Do NOT call page 2

- Page 1 returns 0–60 days of inventory

- No inventory exists beyond 60 days

Time Handling:

- All times are in local facility time

- No time conversion required

---
- Schedule Appointment Call

Example Request:

{
"storeName": "Chicago",
"email": "test.customer@example.com",
"firstName": "Test",
"lastName": "Customer",
"phone": "3125550199",
"totalPrice": 350.00,
"appointmentStartDateTime": "2026-03-12T10:00:00.000Z",
"serviceList": [
"Iron"
]
}

Required Fields:

- storeName

- email (required)

- appointmentStartDateTime

- serviceList

Always Pass (Unmasked):

- Email

- Phone (if available)

- First name

- Last name

- Full name when available

Pricing:

- totalPrice passed

- Pricing structure exists in API (not yet live but available)

- No structural enhancement required later

---
- Cancellation

- Cancellation endpoint provided by vendor

- Uses Appointment Number

- Appointment number starts with “A”

- Confirm mapping to internal booking ID

- Validate cancellation response

- Validate error handling

---
- Sync & Inventory Rules

- Sync schedule: 0–60 days only

- Page 1 returns full 60-day window

- No polling beyond page 1

- Sync schedule aligned with other simulator interfaces

---
- Interface Configuration

Exposed Config Values:

- Store Name

- Selected Fitting (Free Text – e.g., Iron, Putter, etc.)

Interface Attributes Table (Hardcoded):

- Authorization configured

- Credentials stored securely

---
- Pricing & Notes Handling

Notes field must differentiate:

- Due at Course per player

- Due Online per player

Trade Logic Pattern:

request.TeeTime.IsTrade
? "GolfNow Trade Round: $0."
: $"Prepaid Course Round - Due at Course amount per player: {request.Pricing.DueAtCoursePerPlayer:C} - TeeTime Price: {request.Pricing.BaseSpecialRate:C}.";

- Matches Club Prophet formatting

- Consistent with other simulator interfaces

---
- Data Handling Requirements

- Always pass unmasked email

- Always pass unmasked phone (if available)

- Always pass full name (if available)

- Confirm no masking occurs in outbound payload

- Confirm PII compliance

---
- DevOps / Infrastructure

- Cache Manager instance request submitted

- Submitted prior to CORE release

- QA and Prod credentials configured

- Secrets stored securely

- Environment variables configured

- IP whitelisting confirmed (if required)

---
- Testing Checklist

Auth:

- Access token retrieved

- Expiration handled

GetFitting:

- Correct fittings returned per store

Availability:

- Returns 0–60 day window

- Page locked to 1

- Filtering by selected fitting works

Schedule:

- Appointment successfully created

- Pricing stored correctly

- Unmasked PII sent

- Time reflects correct local facility time

Cancellation:

- Appointment number mapping correct

- Cancellation succeeds

- Error handling validated

request.TeeTime.IsTrade

  • Always pass unmasked email

  • Always pass full name (if available)

  • Confirm no masking occurs in outbound payload

  • Confirm PII compliance

  1. DevOps / Infrastructure

  • Cache Manager instance request submitted

  • Submitted prior to CORE release

  • QA and Prod credentials configured

  • Secrets stored securely

  • Environment variables configured

  • IP whitelisting confirmed (if required)

  1. Testing Checklist

Auth:

  • Expiration handled

GetFitting:

Availability:

  • Returns 0–60 day window

  • Page locked to 1

  • Filtering by selected fitting works

Schedule:

  • Pricing stored correctly

issues.summary: Add Logic for Account Anniversary PFA Bonus Look Back Date
issues.description:
The business would like to add a restriction to the account anniversary PFA bonus that limits how far back we award the bonus.

Example: Business wants to limit bonus to accounts created on 1/1/2020 or later

- Customer A created account on 7/4/2023

- Customer A receives anniversary bonus on 7/4/2026

- Customer B created account on 1/1/2020

- Customer B receives anniversary bonus on 1/1/2026

- Customer C created account on 11/11/2017

- Customer C does not receive anniversary bonus on 11/11/2026

Note:

- The look back date should be configurable per campaign, not hard coded.

- The anniversary bonuses will be awarded moving forward, not retroactively

issues.summary: Tee Time Credits - Investigate if they are reusable after reservation is cancelled
issues.description:
Request :

Could you book a tee time using one of the $10 monthly promo codes, cancel the tee time, and then let me know if the promo code becomes available again to be used for a different tee time?
issues.descriptionHtml:
Request :

Could you book a tee time using one of the $10 monthly promo codes, cancel the tee time, and then let me know if the promo code becomes available again to be used for a different tee time?

comments.author: Dewan Kabir
comments.body:
Research :

We initially found our that in AWS DEV , the Strored Procedure : StoredProcedure [Merchandise].[GetUserSubscriptionsToProcess]  had a hard coded Customer Number being passed through in it , so when ever we ran the Subscription Item Processor task , it was being executed with only that Customer Record.

After we removed that hard coded data , we ran the proc , and saw the tons of staged data , which were ready to be processed , and so after executing the task , we saw that the records were being processed as expected , along side the emails for the Hot Deal Tee Time Credit Promo Codes coming through as well .

Once the task completed , we started testing with our target user , and saw that the promo code which was generated for the new user was associated with a promo code campaign which already expired .

After updating that promo code campaign , we started to test the promo code on a trade tee time , and saw regardless of the booking going through GNC / Reservation Service or API 2.1 , once the booking was cancelled , the tee time credit promo code still had the “ Claimed “ status .
comments.bodyHtml:
Research :

We initially found our that in AWS DEV , the Strored Procedure : StoredProcedure [Merchandise].[GetUserSubscriptionsToProcess] had a hard coded Customer Number being passed through in it , so when ever we ran the Subscription Item Processor task , it was being executed with only that Customer Record.

After we removed that hard coded data , we ran the proc , and saw the tons of staged data , which were ready to be processed , and so after executing the task , we saw that the records were being processed as expected , along side the emails for the Hot Deal Tee Time Credit Promo Codes coming through as well .

Once the task completed , we started testing with our target user , and saw that the promo code which was generated for the new user was associated with a promo code campaign which already expired .

After updating that promo code campaign , we started to test the promo code on a trade tee time , and saw regardless of the booking going through GNC / Reservation Service or API 2.1 , once the booking was cancelled , the tee time credit promo code still had the “ Claimed “ status .

issues.summary: Investigate GolfNow Tax Calculation Behavior and Share Vertex Request/Response Data with Commerce
issues.description:
Tax calculation behavior was observed to differ slightly between the GolfNow platform and the Commerce platform. To help diagnose and understand these discrepancies, an investigation was performed into how tax was being calculated on the GolfNow side.

As part of this effort, the Vertex tax request and response objects generated by GolfNow were captured and shared with the Commerce team. This information was provided to support troubleshooting efforts and to help identify where and why the tax calculation behavior between the two platforms may be diverging.

issues.summary: GeoPlace - add Golf.Helpers.Serilog for logging
issues.descriptionHtml:
Add GN logging into applications

Packages:

<PackageReference Include="GolfNow.Logging.Serilog" Version="3001.116.0.28" />
<PackageReference Include="Golf.Helpers.Serilog" Version="3001.113.0.56" />
<PackageReference Include="Serilog.AspNetCore" Version="10.0.0" />
<PackageReference Include="Serilog.Enrichers.Span" Version="3.1.0" />
<PackageReference Include="Serilog.Expressions" Version="5.0.0" />

appsetting.json

"Logging": {
  "Serilog": {
    "MinimumLevel": {
      "Default": "Warning",
      "Override": {
        "GolfNow": "Information",
        "Golf": "Information"
      }
    },
    "Using": [ "Golf.Helpers.Serilog" ],
    "Enrich": [
      "FromLogContext",
      "WithSourceAssemblyVersion",
      "WithApplicationVersion",
      "WithSpan",
      {
        "Name": "WithApplicationName",
        "Args": {
          "AppName": "GolfNow.Services.Auth.WebApi"
        }
      }
    ],
    "WriteTo": [
      {
        "Name": "AuthEventSplunkSink",
        "Args": {
          "Namespaces": [
            "GolfNow.Services.Auth.Identity"
          ],
          "SplunkHost": "SPLUNK_HOST",
          "SplunkUriPath": "services/collector/event",
          "SplunkEventCollectorToken": "SPLUNK_TOKEN",
          "RestrictedToMinimumLevel" :  "Information"
        }
      },
      {
        "Name": "FilteredGolfNowSink",
        "Args": {
          "ServiceBaseUrl": "#{Golf.Svc.Logging.URL}",
          "PropertyName": "TraceId",
          "VerboseRate": 0,
          "DebugRate": 0,
          "InformationRate": 0.25,
          "WarningRate": 1,
          "ErrorRate": 1,
          "FatalRate": 1
        }
      },
      {
        "Name": "File",
        "Args": {
          "formatter": {
            "type": "Serilog.Templates.ExpressionTemplate, Serilog.Expressions",
            "template": "[{@t:u}\t{@l:u3}\t{#if SourceContext is not null}{SourceContext}(v{SourceAssemblyVersion})\t{#end}{#if TraceId is not null}Trace:{TraceId}{#end}]\t{@m}{#if @x is not null}\tException: {@x}\n{#end}\n"
          },
          "path": "#{Logging.Folder.JSON}",
          "rollOnFileSizeLimit": true,
          "fileSizeLimitBytes": 10485760,
          "retainedFileCountLimit": 2
        }
      },
      {
        "Name": "Console",
        "Args": {
          "formatter": {
            "type": "Serilog.Templates.ExpressionTemplate, Serilog.Expressions",
            "template": "[{@t:u}\t{@l:u3}\t{#if SourceContext is not null}{SourceContext}(v{SourceAssemblyVersion})\t{#end}{#if TraceId is not null}Trace:{TraceId}{#end}]\t{@m}{#if @x is not null}\tException: {@x}\n{#end}\n"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
},

comments.author: Jeff Sykes
comments.body:
JEFF NOTES FROM PREVIOUS RESEARCH:

- The -1 Error coming back from AddMember is accurate/proper.

- The question is:  Why is CORE trying to run AddMember for a customer that already exists?

- Prior to AddMember I saw an API call being run twice to see if the customer already exists.  CORE passes-in an EZLinks “InternetUserID” param GUID:

- in all uppercase.

- in all lowercase.  (I don’t recall which of these 2 is attempted first)

If either of these say the customer already exists, CORE should not advance to AddMember to create a new customer.  CORE should instead use the InternetUserID string format that succeed and use that customer record for the booking call.

comments.author: Joshua Marquess
comments.body:
CORE workflow for EZ1 issues:

- CORE calls GetUserRegistration - pass USERID GUID as it is in database and contact ID does not exist proceed to AddMember

- If no contactID in response, we recall all UPPER Case

- If still no contactID in response, we call AddMember

- If no contactID, proceed to AddMember (-1 or 50003 or 500002)

- If -1 or 500003 or 500002 on response. Retry AddMember with all UPPER CASE

- If exception again, we fail call and process EZL1 error

Post meeting notes:

issues.summary: EZL Cart Fee Issue
issues.description:
Whenever a cart fee is added into GNC Configure Rate sets, we send the Green fee only as the rate to the EZTP tee sheet. The request is send over the total price with cart so that it can show up correctly in their slot breakout and pricing notes fields.

Richter Park - FID 5789

This course is just one example of the logic that is causing the wrong rate to show in EZTP.

When Cart Fee is being used (in this case $20), GNC is splitting the total price (GF + CF) up into 2 values and sending the wrong Green Fee amount over to EZTP. For example, a $97 rate was booked that includes the $20 rate fee, but EZTP reflects a $77 rate (cart fee removed). We need the logic updated so that the price booked shows exactly the same on EZTP.

Res 405196814

issues.summary: Support Customer Notes in Commerce API by Passing customerNotes Metadata Through to GolfNow Reservation Workflow
issues.description:
We need to enhance the Commerce → GolfNow reservation workflow to support customer-supplied notes entered during checkout. Currently, the Commerce API includes these notes in the item’s Metadata object under the customerNotes key, but the GolfNow API reservation workflow does not receive or process this value.

This ticket will introduce end-to-end handling of customer notes by:

Scope of Work

- Read the customerNotes metadata field from the Commerce API Item.Metadata object.

- Ensure this value is included when constructing the reservation request payload sent to the GolfNow API.

- Identify the correct field/property within the GolfNow API reservation workflow to map these notes into (e.g., reservation-level metadata or a dedicated customer notes field).

Acceptance Criteria

- Customer notes entered in Commerce successfully appear on the GolfNow reservation.

- Notes are visible in downstream systems that rely on GolfNow reservation data.

- Notes are passed to the tee sheet appended to the other system notes we pass to the teesheet

- Do not overwrite any existing logic for notes that we pass to the teesheet

- Replicated behavior for notes field on Add Reservation call in Transparent Redirect

issues.summary: Fix Commerce Workflow Failure When No Payment Is Due Online and No Customer Wallet Exists
issues.description:
Problem

The Commerce reservation workflow fails when nothing is due online and the customer does not have a wallet created with payment methods.

In this scenario, the workflow appears to still require a payment method to be present, even though no payment is required. This impacts both guest users and authenticated customers who do not yet have a wallet or saved payment methods.

Expected Behavior

When the total due online amount is $0.00, the Commerce workflow should allow the reservation to complete successfully without requiring a customer wallet or payment method.

Additional Context

This same scenario works correctly in the Transparent Redirect flow, where reservations with no amount due online are allowed to proceed even when no wallet or payment methods exist.

Because of this, it may be helpful to review how the Transparent Redirect flow handles zero-due reservations and align the Commerce workflow behavior accordingly.

Impact

- Blocks valid reservations when no payment is required

- Affects both guest and authenticated customers without wallets

- Creates inconsistent behavior between Commerce and Transparent Redirect flows

issues.summary: Improve Robustness of Cached Invoice Removal During Item Removal
issues.description:
The Remove Item endpoint should be improved to more reliably clear cached invoice data when items are removed from a cart.

While stale invoice data is not currently causing functional issues, cached invoices may remain in the system longer than necessary after item removal. The Remove Item flow should be updated to proactively clear invoice cache entries as soon as possible, across a wider set of scenarios.

The desired outcome is improved cache hygiene and more consistent cleanup of invoice data during item removal, helping ensure the system remains efficient and avoids unnecessary retention of cached invoices.

comments.author: Tyler Olechnowicz
comments.body:
QA

Previously, invoices were not able to be removed from the cache unless the OrderInvoiceResponseCacheKey property was present in the item metadata. This property only gets added to the metadata after the GenerateDistributions endpoint is executed.

Execute the CreateInvoice endpoint and then execute the RemoveItem endpoint and make sure that the invoice is removed from the cache. You will know that the invoice is removed from the cache because re-executing the CreateInvoice endpoint will take the normal amount of time instead of being lightening quick.

The cache key is built off of these parameters, so make sure that these values are the same for both the CreateInvoice and RemoveItem calls:

cacheKeyToRemove = RedisKeyBuilder.BuildGolfNowInvoiceKey<OrderInvoiceResponse>(
request.CartKey,
request.Item.CartItemKey,
clientTokenClaims.ClientUsername,
clientTokenClaims.ChannelId,
teeTimeId,
request.UserAccount.EmailAddress,
request.Item.Quantity,
request.Item.UnitPrice.Amount);

issues.summary: Update RefundOrderInInterfaceActivity to Send Payment Method Type and Transaction ID from Payment Processing API to Vendor Service
issues.description:
Problem

Refunds are successfully processed through the Payments system. However, the notification we send to Vendor Service after a refund does not include all of the information Vendor Service needs to properly reflect the refund.

When PaymentMethodKey-based payments are used, the refund notification relies on our internal payment method type, which does not represent the actual underlying payment method used by Payments. In addition, the refund confirmation reference returned by Payments is not included in the notification.

As a result, refunds complete successfully on our side, but Vendor Service cannot reliably associate or represent the refund in their system.

---
Desired Outcome

Enhance the refund notification sent to Vendor Service so that, when applicable:

- The underlying payment method type used by Payments is included

- The refund transaction identifier is included

- The refund confirmation reference is included

This will allow Vendor Service to correctly reflect and reconcile refunds without changing the existing refund execution flow.

---
Payment Method Handling

When a PaymentMethodKey-based payment is involved:

- The underlying payment method type should be resolved using the Payment Processing API

- The resolved value should be mapped to the payment method format expected by Vendor Service

- If an underlying payment method type is not available, existing internal payment type behavior should be preserved

Vendor Service recognizes the following payment method values:

- "credit" or "creditcard"

- "accountbalance"

- "g1payment"

- Any other value is treated as "unknown"

---
Metadata Requirements

The refund notification must include the following values in the RefundItem.Metadata dictionary:

- TransactionID
Populated with the refund transaction ID returned by the Payment Processing API

- RefundConfirmationID
Populated with the refund confirmation reference returned by Payments (PNREF)

---
Scope

- Update the Vendor Service refund notification built in RefundOrderInInterfaceActivity

- Resolve and populate the underlying payment method type when available

- Populate RefundItem.PaymentMethod using the resolved payment method mapping

- Populate RefundItem.Metadata["TransactionID"] with the refund transaction ID

- Populate RefundItem.Metadata["RefundConfirmationID"] with the refund confirmation reference

- Preserve existing refund execution behavior
issues.descriptionHtml:
Problem

Refunds are successfully processed through the Payments system. However, the notification we send to Vendor Service after a refund does not include all of the information Vendor Service needs to properly reflect the refund.

When PaymentMethodKey-based payments are used, the refund notification relies on our internal payment method type, which does not represent the actual underlying payment method used by Payments. In addition, the refund confirmation reference returned by Payments is not included in the notification.

As a result, refunds complete successfully on our side, but Vendor Service cannot reliably associate or represent the refund in their system.

Desired Outcome

Enhance the refund notification sent to Vendor Service so that, when applicable:

  • The underlying payment method type used by Payments is included

  • The refund transaction identifier is included

  • The refund confirmation reference is included

This will allow Vendor Service to correctly reflect and reconcile refunds without changing the existing refund execution flow.

Payment Method Handling

When a PaymentMethodKey-based payment is involved:

  • The underlying payment method type should be resolved using the Payment Processing API

  • The resolved value should be mapped to the payment method format expected by Vendor Service

  • If an underlying payment method type is not available, existing internal payment type behavior should be preserved

Vendor Service recognizes the following payment method values:

  • "credit" or "creditcard"

  • "accountbalance"

  • "g1payment"

  • Any other value is treated as "unknown"

Metadata Requirements

The refund notification must include the following values in the RefundItem.Metadata dictionary:

  • TransactionID
    Populated with the refund transaction ID returned by the Payment Processing API

  • RefundConfirmationID
    Populated with the refund confirmation reference returned by Payments (PNREF)

Scope

  • Update the Vendor Service refund notification built in RefundOrderInInterfaceActivity

  • Resolve and populate the underlying payment method type when available

  • Populate RefundItem.PaymentMethod using the resolved payment method mapping

  • Populate RefundItem.Metadata["TransactionID"] with the refund transaction ID

  • Populate RefundItem.Metadata["RefundConfirmationID"] with the refund confirmation reference

  • Preserve existing refund execution behavior

comments.author: Yoel Martin Pardo
comments.body:
QA: The only way that we found a way to recreate the issue was calling the Add Customer endpoint with an Inactive customer account.

In order to validate the scenarios above, please follow the steps above:

1- Create a customer account using Add Customer endpoint.

2- Get the customer Id and run query above on Loyalty database:

SELECT * FROM [LoyaltyActions].[ActionQueue] WHERE CustomerId = 'CustomerId'

You should see a record with ActionTypeId = 4

3- Delete the record.

DELETE [LoyaltyActions].[ActionQueue] WHERE CustomerId = 'CustomerId'

4- Run Update Customer endpoint and check loyalty query again. You should not see any new record.

5- Duplicate Add Account endpoint and replace email and username with the data for the customer that you are testing with and run endpoint.

You should get an error saying customer already exists.

6- Update customer status be Inactive:

UPDATE CRMcustomer SET CStatus = 'Inactive' WHERE CustomerNumber = 'CustomerNumber'

7- Run Add Customer endpoint again.

You should get a 200k response and you should not see a new record on the loyalty table. The record should only be created when you are adding a new customer or when converting a guest to customer account.

In order to test convert guest to customer account, please use the Convert to Customer endpoint and also the Add Customer endpoint.

issues.summary: Disable Swagger UI  and ReDoc and API Documentation in Production Environment
issues.description:
Swagger UI and ReDoc documentation are currently enabled across all environments. For security and best-practice reasons, we should disable Swagger and ReDoc in the Production environment while keeping it available in Development, Staging, and other non-production deployments.

This update will ensure that:

- Swagger UI and ReDoc are not accessible in Production.

- These tools remain fully enabled in non-production environments for development, debugging, and QA testing.

- URL rewrite rules that redirect the root path to /swagger do not execute in Production.

Acceptance Criteria

- Swagger UI and ReDoc are not available in Production.

- /swagger, /swagger/index.html, and /redoc return 404 or do not map routes in Production.

- Root URL rewrite to Swagger is disabled in Production.

- Non-production environments still fully support Swagger and ReDoc pages.

issues.summary: Enhance Post Score logic to check Total, Front and Back Rating Availability
issues.description:
Results from research of https://golfnow.atlassian.net/browse/CFE-1670

:question: How can we make sure a user knows whether they’re allowed to post an 18 hole score, a 10-17 hole score, or a 9 hole score based on the USGA rating data available to us?

- we always load an 18 hole scorecard on Compete, but users may only be able to post for 9 holes, even if they’ve scored more

- this is a result of USGA tee marker data only containing “Front” half (1-9 holes) rating and slope data

Desired UX:

- a user can save a scorecard for any course we have in inventory, no problem (9, 10-17, 18)

- when they go to post a score, we need to know what ratings we have available

- Total

- Front

- Back

:check_mark:  Acceptance Criteria

- if we are missing “Back” rating and slope, we can only post the scores for 1-9 as a 9-hole round, and must alert user

- post holesScored = 9 and side = front for holes 1-9

- if we have Total, Front and Back ratings for the teemarker:

- we will ALWAYS post an 18 hole score when we have all 18 scores

- holesScored = 18 and side = All18

- we will ALWAYS post 10-17 holes scored when we have 10-17 holes scored

- holes scored = 10_17 and side = All18

@Andre Gamboa @Alex McNay please correct variable names and values above if they differ from Graph

:bookmark:  Please link Swagger and/or other documentation created as part of this effort

Link:

This ensures the front-end is armed with information they need for linked dependencies.

STR:

- score a full 18 hole round on the Bobby Jones Magnolia course - Id 1808

- Attempt to post the score to the USGA using the All18 tee set

- You’ll get an error saying the course is only able to post a 9 hole score

- The issue is centers around the fact that this 9 hole course doesn’t have a Back-9 holeRange and hasn’t account for an 18 hole round with it’s Total holeRange, which is just a duplicate of the Front-9 slope and rating

Query to show all the TeeMarkers that have a Front-9 (1) rating equal to their Total/18 Hole (3) rating. Meaning that they are on a 9 hole course that isn’t setup to score an 18 hole scorecard

SELECT Distinct(t1.TeeMarkerId)
FROM GolfCourse.TeeMarkerRating t1
JOIN GolfCourse.TeeMarkerRating t2
ON t1.teeMarkerId = t2.teeMarkerId
WHERE t1.Rating = t2.Rating AND t1.holeRange = 1 AND t2.holeRange = 3;

issues.summary: Accepting a USGA account link request sets all DB values to 3
issues.description:
:question: How can we sever the USGA Golfer ID from the Compete CustomerID so that a future GPA Access Approval does not trigger a link for PREVIOUS/REVOKED Customers?

Backend Research ticket for the issue below

If a user approves a link to a USGA account, and that USGA account was originally linked to another Compete user, both users will get their status updated to 3 - accepted. This is because we don’t have a way to know the difference between multiple USGA records in the golfer.accessRequest table that have the same USGA email and USGA golferId.

STR

- create a user in compete

- link that user to a USGA account

- unlink that compete user from that USGA account

- create a second user in compete

- link the same USGA account to the second compete user

- we will see both compete account are actively linked to the same USGA account

Yesterday I ran the individual indexer for this course and it pulled in the YELLOW tee that was added by USGA. Today, 11/20 around 12PM both Graph and Mongo DB became unavailable for brief amount of time. Now that YELLOW tee is missing from the FE and the api response, when it was there last night and this morning. There is something that is recycling the api data or response and is removing the tees that the mapping process is creating when a match to the USGA tee isn’t found. They still in the data base, but it is taking an individual reindex on the endpoint in the comment below to bring them back into the Graph response for course search.

Current DB values - Yellow is present

Current API response - Yellow is missing | was there last night and this morning

Front end from last night after an individual reindex - Yellow is present

Front end currently - yellow is missing, this is explained by it missing from the API up stream

comments.author: Allen Shoup
comments.body:
Notes from Nov 25th chat (Daniel, Andre, Matt, Alex, Allen):

- we can use USGA verified data for ALL users

- we don’t need to show “verified” badging for the unlinked user

- ideally we only send a linked user the USGA tee sets and courses if we know they are linked

- ideally we should only import and display tee sets and courses FOR USGA ONLY if we have it

- if we have a mapping we pass USGA only to ALL users

- provider 4 for dataSourceId

- if we don’t have a mapping we pass Grint data only to ALL users

- provider 2 for dataSourceId

- leverage the isEnabled field in our DB and use 1 for active and 0 for inactive as tied to the USGA course data updated via webhooks

issues.summary: Restrict USGA account linking if GN user and USGA user have different genders
issues.description:
Summary: {Describe the issue and provide any relevant context}

Currently both our Golfnow/Compete account and the USGA account have independent gender values, each stored in independent systems. This is allowing a Male Golfnow user to link to a Female USGA user or vice versa. When this occurs, Compete defaults to the tee selection of the Golfnow user, and once that round is scored and posted to USGA, and error is thrown for incompatible tees to the USGA gender.

Steps to Reproduce: {If applicable, list the steps to reproduce the described issue in a clear and concise bulleted list}

- Login as a Male Golfnow user/or create a new Male Golfnow user account in compete

- navigate to the USGA linking flow and link this Male Golfnow user to a Female USGA account - This is where the new validation needs to be implemented

- confirm through email the link to establish this connection

- once the accounts are linked, open the play tab on compete and score any casual round on a USGA course with the tees provided through regular casual round setup

- after finishing the round attempt to push your score to USGA for handicaping purposes

Expected Results: {What is the expected or correct behavior?}

- We would expect this linkage to be prevented earlier in the flow, only same gendered accounts can be linked, or at the very least be able to push scores to the USGA

Actual Results: {What is the observed behavior?}

- currently we are getting an error when trying to push a score to the USGA from tees that do not match the USGA user gender.

“errorMessage”: “The golfer’s gender should match with the tee set gender”,

issues.summary: Propagate Facility Merchant Key Updates from GNC to Commerce
issues.description:
When a facility’s merchant key is updated in GNC (full-stack update), the change is not currently communicated to Commerce.

As a result, Commerce may continue using an outdated merchant key, which can lead to inconsistencies between systems and potential downstream issues during payment processing.

Desired Outcome

Ensure that whenever a facility’s merchant key is updated in GNC, the updated key is sent to Commerce using the endpoint provided by the Commerce team.

This allows Commerce to stay in sync with the latest facility merchant configuration and ensures accurate payment handling.

Scope

- Detect full-stack facility merchant key updates in GNC

- Invoke the Commerce-provided endpoint with the updated merchant key

- Ensure Commerce receives and applies the updated value

issues.summary: Backend needs to send back USGA gender if the player is linked AND GN gender in Player Round object
issues.description:
:question: What’s the issue:

There is potential for Gender mismatch between a USGA (provider) account and the API 2.1 profile gender. This creates issues in Tee Selection and other gender-related features.

This is an issue for checking Gender for golfers included on the end-users round, not the end-user themselves.

Front-end needs to know the provider (USGA) gender for scoring purposes so we can be sure there’s no mismatch

:check_mark:  Acceptance Criteria

- Need to send back USGA gender rather than GN gender for users that are linked in PlayerRound Object. Backend is sending us gender using playerGender. Backend should send us USGA gender in playerGender or backend can make a new field.

issues.summary: Save an 18-hole total scorecard
issues.description:
:book:  User Story

Golfers must have the option (per USGA) to post “total” scores. These scores can be done at a 9-hole or 18-hole total. It is the quickest way to take a scorecard and submit a valid score to the handicapping provider.

:check_mark:  Acceptance Criteria

- golfer selects a course

- golfer selects a tee set for the course

- we now have the course rating and slope information for the given course and tee set

- golfer selects equivalent of “post a quick score”

- golfer selects from:

- post 9-hole score (front 9 or back 9)

- post 18 hole score using 9 & 9

- post 18 hole score total

- golfer is presented with a new view that summarizes the course data they are posting to and is given prompts for keypad entry for the scoring

- golfer taps into 18-hole single input and can enter any value using the keypad

- golfer inputs the gross score of 85

- golfer will always input gross score

- golfer is presented option to Post Score to (provider) because there is a valid input of 85

- golfer selects the Post Score option

- the score is posted for the course, tee set and gross score to the provider

- the score is saved to their Round History

- front-end will need to present a response from the API as to whether the score was posted successfully to provider (if applicable) AND saved to their Compete account

- this can be done using our standard solo score confirmation view but we’ll need to incorporate the course rating and slope info

🔖  Please link Swagger and/or other documentation created as part of this effort

Link:

This ensures the front-end is armed with information they need for linked dependencies.
